## 2026-10-13 — 008-settings-cli: Bounded Unix mechanism refined; current-source proof pending

- **Prerequisite:** Root-approved correction of actual process-mask finding and independent mechanism decision.
- **Required inputs:** Current plan, kernel peer-UID/directory contract, informative OS references and exact restoration evidence.
- **Action:** CurrentUID directory0700 and pinned guards plus both-side kernel UID before bytes replace socket-mode prescription; no umask/pathchmod/bootstrap permission framework. Step5 retains lease-proven reclamation.
- **Execution evidence:** Native fd-fchmod EINVAL and pinned-open EOPNOTSUPP; own incomplete bootstrap hunks surgically restored, no successful compile/RED/PASS claim. Earlier tests remain historical snapshots.
- **Success criteria:** FR/AC IDs, seven steps, business/release scope unchanged; Step1 In Progress, fresh implementation/tests/reviews/audit and official plan refresh pending.
- **Failure handling:** Read [mechanism review](features/008-settings-cli/proofs/current-run-step1/minimal-channel-review.json) and [restoration](features/008-settings-cli/proofs/current-run-step1/bootstrap-surgical-restore.json). No Step2 or current-source certification before accepted gates.

- **Action:** Refresh latest ten entries newest first; preserve feature statuses/metadata. Retain socket failure paths fail-closed, avoiding same-UID check/unlink races; lease-proven reclamation belongs to Step 5.
- **Execution evidence:** Documentary/source inspection only; prior 20/20 and quality PASS bind the earlier source snapshot. Fresh worker-source checks/review/audit are pending.

# Constitution — Handy

## Project Identity

Retain observed packages handy-app, handy.
Independent families:

| Layer | Choice | Version | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| JavaScript | JavaScript | Unknown | package.json |
| React | React | ^18.3.1 | package.json |
| Vite | Vite | ^6.4.1 | package.json |
| TypeScript | TypeScript | ~5.6.3 | package.json |
| Rust | Rust | Unknown | src-tauri/Cargo.toml |
| Tauri | Tauri | 2.11.5 | src-tauri/Cargo.toml |

## Architecture Principles

- Preserve the existing source and native/frontend boundaries.
- Derive stack and manager choices from manifests; unsupported business decisions remain Unknown.
- Tool version availability certifies tooling only;
  application build, UI and runtime require separate execution evidence.
- Specify changed behavior before implementing it;
  require meaningful tests and current source verification.

## Testing Standards

Read [testing strategy](testing/strategy.md).

### Native platform evidence (user decision 2026-10-13)

- Code targets every supported platform (macOS, Windows, Linux) and must build and pass its automated tests.
- macOS native evidence is required before a feature is marked Implemented.
- Native evidence that needs Windows, Linux, an older Handy binary or a second user account is recorded as **pending release evidence** with the exact check to run. It never blocks implementation steps, feature completion on the integration branch, or the merge into `dev`; it is never claimed as passed.
- Implementations follow the reviewed spec at its minimal scope: a plan mechanism that the spec does not require (for example replaying commands for an older running Handy) is not built.

# Feature Spec: Microphone Priority

## Header

- **Feature:** Microphone Priority
- **Branch:** None — specification only (--no-branch)
- **Date:** 2026-10-09
- **Status:** Planned
- **Input:** Program item 1 (user request 2026-10-12): in settings, show an ordered microphone list reorderable by drag and drop. At each recording, try the first available microphone, then the next ones, and finally the system default microphone. Display the microphone actually used and the unavailable devices, without deleting their preferences after a disconnection. Preserve the existing closed-lid (clamshell) behavior. Migrate the legacy single selection. F8 (settings CLI, feature 008) provides the shared persistent configuration CLI before F1 ships.
- **Feature Number:** 001
## User Scenarios & Testing

### Story 1 — Edit ordered microphone choices `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** add, remove and reorder microphone choices, **so that** each recording uses my preferred available device.

**Priority reason:** Device choice controls the core recording workflow.
**Independent test:** Configure two devices, move the second above the first, verify only the draft changed, activate Save, reload settings and inspect the committed order.

```gherkin
Feature: Ordered microphone preferences
  Scenario: Reorder available devices
    Given the configured order is USB headset then MacBook microphone
    When the user moves MacBook microphone above USB headset
    Then the draft order is MacBook microphone then USB headset
    And the persisted order remains USB headset then MacBook microphone before Save
    When the user activates Save and it succeeds
    Then the persisted order is MacBook microphone then USB headset
    And the next recording attempts MacBook microphone first
  Scenario: Invalid duplicate choice
    Given USB headset is already configured
    When the user adds USB headset again
    Then the duplicate is rejected with an actionable error
    And the saved order remains unchanged
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Edit draft priority list] --> B{Valid unique choices?}
  B -- No --> D[Show error and retain saved order]
  B -- Yes --> S{Save activated?}
  S -- No --> A
  S -- Yes --> C{Commit succeeds?}
  C -- No --> D
  C -- Yes --> E[Persist complete new order]
  E --> F[Next recording uses committed order]
```

### Story 2 — Record through availability fallback `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** see unavailable choices and record with the next usable microphone, **so that** disconnecting a preferred device does not destroy my preferences.

**Priority reason:** Fallback prevents loss of the core recording capability.
**Independent test:** Disconnect the first configured device, start a recording and compare the effective device with unchanged stored preferences.

```gherkin
Feature: Microphone availability fallback
  Scenario: First choice unavailable
    Given USB headset then MacBook microphone is configured
    And USB headset is disconnected while MacBook microphone is available
    When a recording starts
    Then MacBook microphone is opened
    And USB headset remains first in the configured list with an unavailable label
  Scenario: No configured device opens
    Given every configured microphone is unavailable or fails to open
    When a recording starts
    Then the system default is attempted after the configured choices
    And failure of that attempt reports a recording error without changing preferences
  Scenario: Reconnection restores priority
    Given the first configured microphone is unavailable for one recording
    When it reconnects before the next recording starts
    Then it is attempted before the lower priority microphones
  Scenario: Ambiguous name is skipped
    Given "USB headset" is configured first and two present devices are named "USB headset"
    When a recording starts
    Then "USB headset" counts as a failed attempt with reason ambiguous
    And the next configured choice is attempted
  Scenario: Always-on stream follows the priority
    Given always-on microphone mode is enabled and no recording is active
    When the user saves a new priority order
    Then the input stream reopens on the first usable choice of the new order
  Scenario: Device lost during a recording
    Given a recording is in progress on USB headset
    When USB headset disconnects
    Then the recording ends and the audio captured before the loss is transcribed
    And the user is told the recording was cut short
    And the configured list is unchanged
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Start recording with current configuration] --> B{Next configured choice exists?}
  B -- Yes --> C{Present and opens?}
  C -- Yes --> D[Record with effective device]
  C -- No --> B
  B -- No --> E{System default opens?}
  E -- Yes --> D
  E -- No --> F[Report recording error]
  D --> G[Retain configured priority]
  F --> G
```

## Acceptance Criteria

### AC-001

**Criterion:** The settings UI displays the configured order, supports add/remove and both pointer and keyboard reorder, and preserves the exact committed order after restart. Duplicate or empty device identities are rejected without a partial write.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 1

### AC-002

**Criterion:** Each configured choice remains visible with available, unavailable, ambiguous or unknown status. Availability refreshes when the audio settings open, every 5 seconds while they remain open, and on manual Retry; refresh errors show unknown status and an actionable retry. The microphone actually used is displayed separately from saved order: during a recording or an open always-on stream, the current device and its reason (first choice, fallback, clamshell, system default); otherwise the device used by the last recording since launch, labelled as such, or "not used yet" after a restart. Add offers the currently enumerated devices. Status uses text in addition to color.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 2

### AC-003

**Criterion:** Whenever the input stream opens — at the start of a recording, or, in always-on microphone mode, when the stream opens at launch, after a committed priority change while no recording is active, or after a device loss — attempt configured devices in saved order and use the first device that is present, unambiguous and opens. A configured name matching several present devices counts as a failed attempt with reason ambiguous. Each open attempt times out after 2 seconds and the whole resolution after 6 seconds; until the stream is ready the indicator keeps its existing arming state and audio spoken before readiness is not captured. Attempt the system default only after configured attempts fail (after the single fresh re-enumeration, unresolvable entries count as failed attempts); if no device opens, report the recording error. Transient enumeration/open failures do not modify the saved list.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 2

### AC-004

**Criterion:** A fallback, disconnect or reconnect never deletes/reorders saved choices or resets the clamshell setting. A reconnected higher priority device is preferred on the next recording; in always-on mode the priority is re-resolved when a recording starts and, when the result differs from the open stream's device, the stream reopens on it before capture begins. Editing priority during a recording affects the next session and does not interrupt or discard the current session's captured audio.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Stories 1 and 2

### AC-005

**Criterion:** The closed-lid behavior is preserved exactly: with a configured override and a confirmed closed lid, attempt the clamshell microphone; if it is unavailable or fails to open, attempt the system default, as today. Open lid or unknown lid state uses the normal priority list. All settings remain unchanged by resolution.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 3

### AC-006

**Criterion:** On first load without the new priority key, a non-default legacy selected_microphone becomes one priority entry; null/default becomes an empty normal priority list; the closed-lid override precedence in AC-005 still applies. An explicitly stored new list, including an empty list, wins. Migration is idempotent, retains unavailable legacy choices, preserves clamshell settings and leaves the original store recoverable if persistence fails.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 3

### AC-007

**Criterion:** UI and F8 CLI invoke shared backend validation and transaction semantics. Valid writes commit the complete order once; invalid input, persistence failure and stale revision return explicit errors with no partial state change. On a stale revision the UI keeps the draft, shows that settings changed elsewhere and offers Reload, which displays the committed order and discards the draft. A committed priority update invalidates cached resolution for the next stream opening without interrupting an active recording.
**Priority:** P2 | **Story:** Story 4

### AC-008

**Criterion:** F8 offers `handy settings microphones list` (configured order, availability, effective device and reason) and `handy settings microphones set-priority <name>...` (complete order, optional expected revision). With `--json`, stdout contains only the F8 JSON envelope; errors use the F8 stable codes (`validation_failed`, `revision_conflict`, `persistence_failed`) and exit codes; reads expose no credentials. F8 is delivered before F1 release; no MCP control server is introduced.
**Priority:** P2 | **Story:** Story 4

## Functional Requirements

### FR-001

**Requirement:** Persist a unique ordered list of microphone choices and expose accessible add/remove/reorder controls in the existing audio settings.
**AC References:** AC-001, AC-007

### FR-002

**Requirement:** Report refreshed availability and effective input separately from configured preferences; failed enumeration is unknown, not proof that a device disappeared. Same-named ambiguous devices are reported as ambiguous, are skipped as a failed attempt at stream opening rather than resolved to an arbitrary device, and remain saved until explicitly edited.
**AC References:** AC-002, AC-003

### FR-003

**Requirement:** Resolve and open normal microphone choices in order, then system default, with bounded attempts and explicit failure. Keep the configured list unchanged during availability resolution or stream recovery.
**AC References:** AC-003, AC-004

### FR-004

**Requirement:** Apply changes at the next stream opening and retain the current session's chosen device while recording. A device loss ends the current recording: audio captured before the loss is kept and transcribed normally, the user is told the recording was cut short, and no other microphone is spliced into its samples. The next stream opening resolves the priority again.
**AC References:** AC-004, AC-007

### FR-005

**Requirement:** Preserve the existing closed-lid behavior (override first, then system default) and never erase the clamshell setting or the normal priority list.
**AC References:** AC-005

### FR-006

**Requirement:** Migrate old single microphone selection only when the priority key is absent, retaining intent and recoverability without changing unrelated settings.
**AC References:** AC-006

### FR-007

**Requirement:** Share typed validation, atomic persistence, revision conflict handling, cache invalidation and setting change notifications between UI and CLI.
**AC References:** AC-001, AC-007, AC-008

### FR-008

**Requirement:** Extend F8 settings JSON operations with priority read/write and device-status read contracts, preserving configured/effective separation and documented error codes.
**AC References:** AC-008

## Clarifications

- Scope (updated 2026-10-12): this spec covers microphone choice only. It belongs to a ten-feature program (001–010) specified in list order; F8 denotes feature `008-settings-cli`, the shared configuration foundation shipped before any other program feature. The program includes the recovery bubble (010). No MCP server is introduced.
- Closed lid (decision 2026-10-12, following "preserve the existing closed-lid behavior"): override first, then system default exactly as today; the normal list is not tried with a closed lid. An empty normal list falls through to system default when the lid is open/unknown. A configured override with a confirmed closed lid is still attempted first. Reset explicitly empties only the normal list and leaves clamshell unchanged.
- Device identity uses existing exact device names until a backend offers stable identifiers. Enumeration indices are session-local and never persisted as identity. Multiple devices with the same name are ambiguous; no arbitrary first-match selection.
- UI edits a draft; Save commits the complete list. UI offers move-up/move-down controls and pointer reorder; persisted choices can be removed even while unavailable.
- Resolution/open attempts are bounded to each configured choice once, one fresh re-enumeration on stale-cache failure, then one system-default attempt. A choice already tried is not retried indefinitely.
- Recording settings are captured at session start. Edits do not restart an active recording; in always-on mode an edit saved during a recording reopens the stream after that recording ends. A disconnected current input ends the recording with the captured audio kept (FR-004); the next recording uses fresh resolution.
- F8 supplies the shared settings transaction/revision contract; proposed operation naming is finalized with F8 before application implementation.

## Edge Cases

- Channel selection: the existing channel setting applies only when valid for the opened device; otherwise the device's default channel mapping is used and the setting is not changed.
- Legacy key: after migration `selected_microphone` stays stored unchanged (not read while the priority key exists) so a downgrade keeps the previous choice; the legacy set command is replaced by the priority operations.
- Reset: empties the draft normal list only; it requires Save and leaves clamshell unchanged.
- Empty normal list: use and show system default when the lid is open/unknown or no usable override applies; a confirmed closed lid still attempts the configured override first.
- All devices missing: retain configured entries and show the attempted default or recording error.
- Enumeration error: mark availability unknown and retain preferences; after the single fresh re-enumeration, configured entries count as failed attempts, the system default is attempted, and the enumeration warning is shown.
- Duplicate names: mark ambiguous; do not persist transient enumeration indices or select an arbitrary match.
- Concurrent reorder and start: capture one committed revision; edits affect the next session.
- Persistence failure: restore last committed settings and allow retry without erasing the migration source.
- Repeated device failures: bounded attempts terminate with an error; no unbounded stream reopen loop.

## Acceptance Criteria

### AC-001

**Criterion:** The settings UI lists rules in their saved order with recognized and replacement text, and supports add, edit and delete (delete asks for confirmation). Add, edit and delete change a draft; Save persists the complete rule set once; a restart shows the same rules in the same order. The list view and the bulk text view edit the same draft: switching view with unsaved changes asks the user to save or discard them first.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 1

### AC-002

**Criterion:** A rule is valid when the trimmed recognized text has 1–100 characters, contains no line break, tab or `;`, and does not start with `#`; and the trimmed replacement has 1–500 characters and contains no line break or tab. Recognized text is unique by its normalized key (trimmed, inner whitespace collapsed to one space, Unicode case-folded). Invalid or duplicate input is rejected with a field error and no partial write. The rule set holds at most 1000 rules.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Stories 1 and 2

### AC-003

**Criterion:** The bulk editor shows all rules as text in the exchange format, accepts pasted text, and shows a line-by-line preview (add, update, delete, unchanged, ignored, error) before applying. Any error line disables Apply. Applying replaces the saved set with exactly the previewed set in one commit.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 2

### AC-004

**Criterion:** The exchange format is UTF-8 text with one rule per line. A line containing a tab splits on its first tab; otherwise it splits on its first `;`. Blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored. The first line that is neither blank nor a comment is ignored as a header when it equals (case-insensitively, after trimming) `texte_reconnu;remplacement` or `recognized;replacement`. Export writes the header `recognized;replacement`, then one `recognized;replacement` line per rule in list order; because AC-002 forbids tab, `;` and a leading `#` in recognized text and tab in replacements, every valid rule set round-trips. Replacement text may contain `;`. CSV quoting is not supported; spreadsheet copy and paste uses the tab separator.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Stories 2 and 3

### AC-005

**Criterion:** Import accepts a file up to 1 MB in merge or replace mode. Merge updates the replacement of rules whose normalized key matches, keeps their position, and appends new rules in file order. Replace makes the file content the whole rule set in file order. Duplicate keys inside one file or block are errors. Import is atomic: on any error, unreadable file or persistence failure, saved rules are unchanged. Export then replace-import of the same file reproduces the same rules and order.
**Priority:** P2 | **Story:** Story 3

### AC-006

**Criterion:** Matching is case-insensitive (Unicode case folding) and the replacement is inserted exactly as written. A match must start and end on word boundaries: the characters immediately before and after the match are not Unicode letters or digits, or are the text edges. On a side where the recognized text begins or ends with a CJK ideograph, kana or hangul character, no boundary check applies, because those scripts are written without spaces. A whitespace run inside the recognized text matches any non-empty whitespace run; other characters match literally. Punctuation adjacent to a match is kept.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 4

### AC-007

**Criterion:** Rules apply in one left-to-right pass over the final recognized text. At each position the rule with the longest normalized key wins; ties follow list order. A matched span is replaced and scanning continues after it; replacement output is never rescanned (no chaining). Rules apply after speech recognition, language detection and Chinese script conversion, and before the existing approximate custom-word correction, filler removal, normalization and AI post-processing. Approximate correction never alters a span produced by a replacement. The inserted text and the history text include the replacements. Rules committed from the UI or the CLI apply from the next dictation of the running app. An empty rule set leaves text unchanged.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 4

### AC-008

**Criterion:** The settings CLI (008) offers list, add, update, remove, import (merge/replace, dry run, file or stdin) and export (file or stdout) for rules, using the same validation, preview and atomic commit as the UI. With JSON output, stdout contains only JSON; errors carry stable codes and non-zero exit codes; a stale expected revision returns a conflict without writing.
**Priority:** P2 | **Story:** Story 5

# Feature Spec: Multiple Dictation Shortcuts

## Header

- **Feature:** Multiple Dictation Shortcuts
- **Branch:** None — specification only (program specified before `spec-ship`)
- **Date:** 2026-10-12
- **Status:** Planned
- **Input:** Program item 4: allow at least two configurable shortcuts for the same transcription action. The existing shortcuts for different actions (with or without post-processing) are not enough. Keep the existing activation behavior and detect shortcut conflicts. Program item 8 requires the settings CLI to read and modify shortcuts.
- **Feature Number:** 004
## User Scenarios & Testing

### Story 1 — Add a second shortcut for dictation `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** bind two or more key combinations to the dictation action, **so that** I can start dictation from the hand position that suits each keyboard or app.

**Priority reason:** This is the requested capability.
**Independent test:** Add a second shortcut to the dictation action, restart, then start and stop dictation with each shortcut in turn.

```gherkin
Feature: Several shortcuts for one action
  Scenario: Add an alternative shortcut
    Given the dictation action has the shortcut "option+space"
    When the user adds the shortcut "ctrl+option+d" to the same action
    Then the dictation action lists "option+space" and "ctrl+option+d"
    And pressing either shortcut starts a dictation
  Scenario: Remove an alternative shortcut
    Given the dictation action has two shortcuts
    When the user removes "ctrl+option+d"
    Then only "option+space" starts a dictation
  Scenario: The last shortcut cannot be removed
    Given the dictation action has one shortcut
    When the user inspects its remove control
    Then removal is unavailable with an explanation that each action keeps at least one shortcut
    And the user can still change or reset that shortcut
  Scenario: Fifth shortcut
    Given the dictation action has four shortcuts
    When the user inspects the add control
    Then adding is unavailable with an explanation of the four-shortcut limit
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Record a new key combination] --> B{Valid for the keyboard implementation?}
  B -- No --> C[Show validation error; keep saved shortcuts]
  B -- Yes --> D{Conflicts with another shortcut or the OS?}
  D -- Yes --> E[Show conflict naming the other action; keep saved shortcuts]
  D -- No --> F[Register and persist the added shortcut]
  F --> G[Every shortcut of the action triggers it]
```

### Story 2 — Keep the existing activation behavior `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** have every shortcut follow my activation mode, **so that** toggle, push-to-talk and hold-or-toggle behave as before.

**Priority reason:** Breaking activation semantics would make dictation unreliable.
**Independent test:** For each activation mode, start with shortcut A and try to stop with shortcut A and with shortcut B of the same action.

```gherkin
Feature: Activation semantics with several shortcuts
  Scenario: Toggle mode
    Given the activation mode is toggle
    And the dictation action has shortcuts A and B
    When the user presses A to start and then presses B
    Then the dictation stops
  Scenario: Push-to-talk mode
    Given the activation mode is push-to-talk
    And the user holds A to record
    When the user presses and releases B during the recording
    Then the recording continues
    And it stops when A is released
  Scenario: Hold-or-toggle mode
    Given the activation mode is hold-or-toggle
    When the user taps A shorter than the hold threshold
    Then the dictation stays on until a shortcut of the action is pressed again
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Shortcut of the action pressed] --> B{Activation mode}
  B -- Toggle --> C{Session active?}
  C -- No --> D[Start session]
  C -- Yes --> E[Stop session]
  B -- Push-to-talk or held --> F{Session started by this shortcut?}
  F -- Yes --> G[Stop on its release]
  F -- No --> H[Ignore input while session active]
```

### Story 3 — Detect conflicts `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** be told when a combination is already used, **so that** one key press never triggers two actions.

**Priority reason:** Conflict detection is explicitly required.
**Independent test:** Try to add the cancel shortcut, the post-processing shortcut and an OS-reserved combination as dictation shortcuts.

```gherkin
Feature: Shortcut conflicts
  Scenario: Combination used by another action
    Given "option+shift+space" is the post-processing shortcut
    When the user adds "shift+option+space" to the dictation action
    Then the shortcut is rejected because it is already used by the post-processing action
    And the saved shortcuts are unchanged
  Scenario: Duplicate within the same action
    Given the dictation action has "option+space"
    When the user adds "option+space" again
    Then the shortcut is rejected as already assigned to this action
  Scenario: Combination unavailable from the OS
    Given another application already registered the combination globally
    When the user adds it
    Then registration fails with an explanation and nothing is saved
  Scenario: Modifier-only overlap
    Given the keyboard implementation allows modifier-only shortcuts
    And "option" is a dictation shortcut
    When the user adds "option+space" to another action
    Then the shortcut is rejected because pressing "option+space" would also trigger "option"
    And the saved shortcuts are unchanged
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Candidate combination] --> B[Normalize modifiers and key]
  B --> C{Equal to an existing shortcut?}
  C -- Yes --> D[Reject: name the owning action]
  C -- No --> E{Modifier-only overlap?}
  E -- Yes --> F[Reject: overlap would double trigger]
  E -- No --> G{OS registration succeeds?}
  G -- No --> H[Reject with OS reason]
  G -- Yes --> I[Persist]
```

### Story 4 — Manage shortcuts from the CLI `P2`

**As an** automation user, **I want to** list, add, remove and reset shortcuts from the CLI, **so that** I can provision Handy on several machines.

**Priority reason:** The settings CLI (008) covers shortcuts from its first version.
**Independent test:** Add, list, conflict and reset shortcuts with `--json` on an isolated store and a running instance.

```gherkin
Feature: Shortcuts through the settings CLI
  Scenario: Add an alternative shortcut
    When the user runs the shortcut add operation for the dictation action with "ctrl+option+d"
    Then the JSON output lists both shortcuts of the action and the new revision
  Scenario: Conflict through the CLI
    When the user adds the cancel shortcut to the dictation action
    Then the command exits with the validation exit code
    And the JSON error code is "shortcut_conflict" and names the owning action
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[CLI shortcut operation] --> B[Shared validation and conflict check]
  B --> C{Valid?}
  C -- No --> D[JSON error with stable code]
  C -- Yes --> E[Persist; running instance re-registers shortcuts]
```
## Acceptance Criteria

### AC-001

**Criterion:** The dictation action and the dictation-with-post-processing action each keep 1 to 4 shortcuts: the last shortcut cannot be removed (only changed or reset) and adding is unavailable at four, with an explanation. The settings UI lists every shortcut of an action with add and remove controls; adding records a key combination with the existing recorder of the active keyboard implementation. After restart all shortcuts are registered and trigger their action.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 1

### AC-002

**Criterion:** Upgrading keeps each existing shortcut as the first shortcut of its action, stored where earlier versions read it, so that a downgrade keeps that first shortcut working and ignores the additional ones; actions and stored bindings other than these two are unchanged. Reset restores the action to its single default shortcut. Stored shortcuts that already conflict under the new checker at upgrade keep their current registration and behavior unchanged; the settings show a conflict warning on them, and the checker applies only to new additions and changes.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 1

### AC-003

**Criterion:** The global activation mode and hold threshold apply to every shortcut of an action. In toggle mode and in the locked (toggled) phase of hold-or-toggle, any shortcut of the action that started the session stops it. In push-to-talk and in the held phase of hold-or-toggle, only the release of the shortcut that started the session ends it, and other shortcuts are ignored during the session, as different bindings are today. A press remembered while processing belongs to the action in toggle mode and to the pressed shortcut in hold modes. Debounce, the deferred release and the remembered press while processing keep their current behavior.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 2

### AC-004

**Criterion:** Before saving, a candidate is normalized (modifier order, left/right-agnostic modifiers as the implementation reports them) and compared with every shortcut of every action, including cancel and prompt shortcuts from feature 005. An equal combination is rejected with the owning action named. A modifier-only shortcut whose modifiers are a subset of another shortcut's modifiers is rejected, because one press would trigger both. With the Tauri implementation, an OS registration failure rejects the change with the OS reason; the HandyKeys implementation performs no OS registration and relies on these checks. Rejections leave saved shortcuts unchanged.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 3

### AC-005

**Criterion:** No action can be left without a shortcut. The cancel shortcut keeps its current dynamic registration while recording and its current platform limits.
**Priority:** P2 | **Story:** Story 1

### AC-006

**Criterion:** The settings CLI (008) offers shortcut list, add, remove and reset per action using the stored text syntax of the active keyboard implementation, with the same validation, limits and conflict check (removing the last shortcut is refused with `validation_failed`). A running instance applies the change without restart. With `--json`, conflicts use the stable code `shortcut_conflict` and include the owning action, the limit uses `limit_exceeded`, and other errors use the F8 envelope codes.
**Priority:** P2 | **Story:** Story 4

## Behavioral AC

Signals extracted: form, validation, keyboard shortcut, conflict, warning, confirm dialog, loading, keyboard navigation. Official `detect_traits` returned async_action, has_validation, is_keyboard_navigable, is_submittable.

### async_action

```gherkin
Feature: Shortcut registration feedback
  Scenario: Registration in progress
    Given the user recorded a valid combination
    When registration is in progress
    Then the add control is busy
    And the shortcut row matches visual state "loading"
  Scenario: Registration failure
    Given the OS refused the combination
    When the user inspects the row
    Then the reason and a retry are shown and saved shortcuts are unchanged
    And the shortcut row matches visual state "error"
  Scenario: Registration success
    Given registration succeeded
    When the list refreshes
    Then the new shortcut is listed
    And the shortcut row matches visual state "success"
  Scenario: Idle list
    Given no registration is pending
    When the user opens the shortcut settings
    Then the shortcut row matches visual state "idle"
```

### has_validation

```gherkin
Feature: Shortcut validation
  Scenario: Nothing recorded
    Given the recorder captured no key yet
    When the user inspects Add
    Then Add is unavailable
    And the recorder matches visual state "empty"
  Scenario: Conflicting combination
    Given the recorded combination equals another action's shortcut
    When validation runs
    Then the conflict names the other action
    And the recorder matches visual state "invalid"
  Scenario: Valid combination
    Given the recorded combination is unique and valid
    When validation runs
    Then no error is shown
    And the recorder matches visual state "valid"
```

### is_keyboard_navigable

<!-- WARNING: No visual states defined for trait "is_keyboard_navigable" in ui-behavioral-taxonomy.md -->

```gherkin
Feature: Keyboard shortcut management
  Scenario: Tab traversal
    Given the shortcut settings are open
    When the user presses Tab
    Then each shortcut row, remove control and add control receives visible focus in reading order
  Scenario: Leave the recorder
    Given the recorder is capturing keys
    When focus leaves the recorder
    Then capture stops without saving, as with the existing recorder
```

### is_submittable

```gherkin
Feature: Commit a shortcut
  Scenario: Valid recording enables Add
    Given a valid unique combination is recorded
    When the user inspects Add
    Then Add matches visual state "enabled"
  Scenario: Invalid recording disables Add
    Given the recorded combination conflicts
    When the user inspects Add
    Then Add matches visual state "disabled"
  Scenario: Commit in progress
    Given the user activates Add
    When registration is pending
    Then Add matches visual state "loading"
```
## Functional Requirements

### FR-001

**Requirement:** Store an ordered list of 1–4 shortcuts per transcription action, migrate each existing single shortcut, and register every shortcut with the active keyboard implementation.
**AC References:** AC-001, AC-002

### FR-002

**Requirement:** Route every shortcut of an action to that action while preserving activation-mode semantics, session ownership by the starting shortcut for hold modes, debounce and pending-press behavior.
**AC References:** AC-003

### FR-003

**Requirement:** Provide one shared conflict checker over all shortcuts of all actions (normalized equality, modifier-only overlap, OS registration result where the implementation registers) used by UI and CLI.
**AC References:** AC-004, AC-006

### FR-004

**Requirement:** Allow removing any shortcut except the last one of an action, and enforce the four-shortcut limit.
**AC References:** AC-005

### FR-005

**Requirement:** Expose shortcut list, add, remove and reset through the settings CLI with live re-registration in a running instance and stable error codes.
**AC References:** AC-006

## Key Entities

| Entity | Description | Key fields |
|---|---|---|
| Action shortcuts | Shortcuts bound to one action | action id, ordered shortcut strings (1–4), default shortcut |
| Normalized combination | Comparable form of a shortcut | modifiers set, key, implementation |
| Conflict result | Outcome of a check | kind (duplicate, overlap warning, OS refusal), owning action |

## Clarifications

- Current code (2026-10-12): one `current_binding` string per binding id; global activation mode and hold threshold; the coordinator ignores a different binding pressed during a session; the only conflict check is the Tauri `is_registered` test; HandyKeys and the frontend have none.
- `[ASSUMED]` Maximum 4 shortcuts per action; enough for "at least two" without cluttering the settings.
- `[ASSUMED]` Multiple shortcuts apply to both transcription actions (with and without post-processing); prompt-specific shortcuts are defined by feature 005 and use the same conflict checker.
- `[ASSUMED]` In hold modes the session is owned by the starting shortcut, matching today's rule for different bindings; toggle treats all shortcuts of the action as one. The coordinator and both keyboard implementations identify events by binding id today; events will need both the action id and the shortcut identity.
- Decision 2026-10-12 (user): legacy conflicts keep today's behavior. Shortcuts that conflict under the new checker when the upgrade runs stay registered exactly as today; a warning marks them in settings until the user changes them; the checker governs only new additions and changes.
- `[ASSUMED]` Starting dictation from the tray is out of scope; every action keeps at least one shortcut.
- Program context: specified in list order (001–010); the settings CLI foundation (008) ships first.

## QE Analysis

- **Criticality:** High; **Blast radius:** Dictation start/stop for every user; **Primary risk:** Activation regression and double triggering; **Confidence:** Medium (coordinator source read, nothing executed).
- **Dimensions:** Functional correctness, regression, platform compatibility (Tauri vs HandyKeys, macOS/Windows/Linux), data migration, accessibility, UX.
- **P0 gates/evidence:** Coordinator state-machine unit tests for each activation mode with two shortcuts; migration test from single bindings; conflict checker table tests (equal, reordered modifiers, modifier-only overlap, cross-action, cancel).
- **P1 gates/evidence:** Native manual test on macOS with both keyboard implementations; Linux limits unchanged; UI keyboard checks; CLI JSON contract and live re-registration test.
- **Non-functional expectations:** With four shortcuts per action, the time from key press to recording start stays within 10 ms of the single-shortcut baseline; no key events are logged above debug level.
- **Missing evidence:** No native runtime test; mockups deferred before `spec-ship`.
- **Boundary:** QE defines risk and test sufficiency; the independent review judges requirements; Penflow governs UI design evidence; spec-test executes runtime proof.

## Screens

| Screen | Status | Reference |
|--------|--------|-----------|
| shortcut-settings | Modified | Mockup to produce before `spec-ship` (user decision 2026-10-12: lightweight UI contract during specification) |

- General settings shortcut area and post-processing shortcut area show a list of shortcuts per action.

## Penflow Contract

- Planned `flow_id: multiple-dictation-shortcuts`, `screen_id: shortcut-settings`. Per the user decision of 2026-10-12 (lightweight UI contract), the Penflow flow/screen contract, semantic and test IDs and the Pencil mockup are produced in one pass for all program features before `spec-ship`; the planned IDs above are authoritative until then. No inspection READY or certification PASS is claimed.

## Edge Cases

- Switching keyboard implementation invalidates one alternative shortcut: only that shortcut is reset or removed and reported, as today's reset of invalid bindings.
- macOS password-field keyboard protection active (another app holds exclusive key input): recording a shortcut is blocked as today and the UI says why.
- Two shortcuts pressed simultaneously: debounce and session ownership prevent a double start.
- Post-processing disabled: its shortcuts are unregistered but kept, as today for its single shortcut.
## Success Criteria

### SC-001

Coordinator tests cover all three activation modes with two shortcuts and pass with zero changes to existing single-shortcut test expectations.

### SC-002

The conflict checker rejects 100% of equal combinations across all actions in table tests, including modifier reordering.

### SC-003

A user with a migrated store, including one with legacy conflicting shortcuts, can start and stop dictation with the original shortcut without reconfiguration, with every legacy shortcut behaving as before the upgrade.

# Feature Spec: Custom AI Prompts

## Header

- **Feature:** Custom AI Prompts
- **Branch:** None — specification only (program specified before `spec-ship`)
- **Date:** 2026-10-12
- **Status:** Planned
- **Input:** Program item 5: create, name, edit and delete transcript-processing prompts: minimal correction, friendly rephrasing, clarification, shortening, notes, translation… Select them from the settings and from the dictation indicator, with an optional associated shortcut and a test. Allow processing by a local or remote AI, with provider and model configuration. Keep the initial transcript if processing fails. The extra actions visible in Spokenly screenshots (scripts, launching apps, OCR) are not requested. Program item 8 requires the settings CLI to read and modify prompts.
- **Feature Number:** 005
## User Scenarios & Testing

### Story 1 — Manage a prompt library `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** create, name, edit and delete processing prompts, **so that** I can keep one prompt per writing need.

**Priority reason:** The library is the base of selection, shortcuts and tests.
**Independent test:** Create "Shorten", edit its text, restart, delete it, and check the list each time.

```gherkin
Feature: Prompt library
  Scenario: Starter prompts on first use
    Given the user has only the existing "Improve Transcriptions" prompt
    When the settings load after upgrade
    Then the library also contains the starter prompts "Minimal correction", "Friendly rephrasing", "Clarify", "Shorten", "Notes" and "Translate to English"
    And "Improve Transcriptions" is unchanged
  Scenario: Create and edit a prompt
    When the user creates a prompt named "Formal email" with a text containing "${output}"
    And later changes its text and saves
    Then the library lists "Formal email" with the new text after restart
  Scenario: Reject an invalid prompt
    Given the prompt name or text is empty
    When the user inspects Save
    Then Save stays disabled and a field error explains what is missing
    And the library is unchanged
  Scenario: Delete the default prompt
    Given "Shorten" is the default prompt
    When the user deletes "Shorten" and confirms
    Then the default prompt becomes "None"
    And shortcuts bound to "Shorten" are removed and reported
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Create, edit or delete prompt] --> B{Name and text valid, name unique?}
  B -- No --> C[Field error; library unchanged]
  B -- Yes --> D{Deleting a referenced prompt?}
  D -- Yes --> E[Confirm; clear default and remove its shortcuts]
  D -- No --> F[Commit]
  E --> F
  F --> G[Library persisted with new revision]
```

### Story 2 — Choose the prompt for a dictation `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** pick the prompt in the settings or from the dictation indicator, **so that** each dictation gets the processing I need.

**Priority reason:** Selection from the indicator is explicitly requested and changes how processing is triggered.
**Independent test:** Set a default prompt in settings, start a post-processing dictation, change the prompt from the indicator during the recording, and check which prompt processed the text.

```gherkin
Feature: Prompt selection
  Scenario: Default prompt from settings
    Given "Minimal correction" is the default prompt
    When the user dictates with the post-processing shortcut
    Then the transcript is processed with "Minimal correction"
  Scenario: Change the prompt from the indicator
    Given a dictation is recording and the indicator shows "Minimal correction"
    When the user opens the prompt menu on the indicator and chooses "Shorten"
    Then the indicator shows "Shorten"
    And this dictation is processed with "Shorten"
    And the default prompt in settings is still "Minimal correction"
  Scenario: Process a plain dictation from the indicator
    Given a dictation started with the plain dictation shortcut shows "None" on the indicator
    When the user chooses "Notes" on the indicator before the recording stops
    Then this dictation is processed with "Notes"
  Scenario: Choosing None skips processing
    Given a post-processing dictation is recording
    When the user chooses "None" on the indicator
    Then the raw transcript is inserted without AI processing
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Dictation starts] --> B{Started by}
  B -- Plain shortcut --> C[Prompt for this dictation: None]
  B -- Post-processing shortcut --> D[Prompt: default prompt]
  B -- Prompt shortcut --> E[Prompt: that prompt]
  C --> F{User changes it on the indicator before stop?}
  D --> F
  E --> F
  F -- Yes --> G[Use the chosen prompt for this dictation only]
  F -- No --> H[Keep the start prompt]
  G --> I[Process or skip when None]
  H --> I
```

### Story 3 — Configure local or remote AI per prompt `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** run a prompt with a local or a remote provider and model, **so that** I can keep private text local and use a stronger remote model when needed.

**Priority reason:** Provider choice is explicitly requested and affects privacy and cost.
**Independent test:** Configure "Minimal correction" to use the local provider and "Translate to English" to use a remote provider; process one dictation with each and inspect the request target.

```gherkin
Feature: Provider and model per prompt
  Scenario: Prompt uses the default provider
    Given "Notes" has no provider override
    When a dictation is processed with "Notes"
    Then the default provider and its model are used
  Scenario: Prompt overrides provider and model
    Given "Minimal correction" uses the local custom provider at "http://localhost:11434/v1" with model "llama3.2"
    When a dictation is processed with "Minimal correction"
    Then the request goes to that local endpoint with that model
  Scenario: Provider not ready
    Given "Translate to English" uses a remote provider without an API key
    When the user selects it in settings
    Then the prompt shows that its provider is not ready and how to fix it
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Prompt chosen] --> B{Prompt has provider override?}
  B -- Yes --> C[Use override provider and model]
  B -- No --> D[Use default provider and model]
  C --> E{Provider ready: endpoint, model, key if needed?}
  D --> E
  E -- No --> F[Skip processing; keep raw transcript; show reason]
  E -- Yes --> G[Send request]
```

### Story 4 — Keep the transcript when processing fails `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** always get my words even when the AI fails, **so that** a dictation is never lost.

**Priority reason:** Losing text is the worst outcome of a dictation tool.
**Independent test:** Point a prompt at an unreachable endpoint, then at an endpoint that times out, and dictate each time.

```gherkin
Feature: Fallback to the initial transcript
  Scenario: Provider error
    Given the chosen prompt's provider returns an error
    When the dictation is processed
    Then the initial transcript is inserted
    And the indicator says AI processing failed and the original text was inserted
    And the history keeps the initial transcript and records the failure
  Scenario: Timeout
    Given the provider does not answer within 30 seconds
```

## Acceptance Criteria

### AC-001

**Criterion:** The settings UI lists prompts with name, provider (default or override) and shortcut, and supports create, edit and delete with confirmation. A prompt is valid when its trimmed name has 1–60 characters and is unique case-insensitively, and its text has 1–8000 characters. The library holds at most 50 prompts. Changes persist across restarts.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 1

### AC-002

**Criterion:** On upgrade, existing prompts and the existing selected prompt are kept unchanged, and the starter prompts Minimal correction, Friendly rephrasing, Clarify, Shorten, Notes and Translate to English are added once when absent by name; they are editable and deletable. Starter prompts are added only while the library has room under its limit. Existing prompts that break the new validation rules are kept, flagged invalid and cannot be used until edited.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 1

### AC-003

**Criterion:** The existing "AI post-processing" switch keeps its meaning: when off, no dictation is processed, prompt shortcuts are unregistered and the indicator menu is hidden. When on, settings define one default prompt or "None". The plain dictation shortcut starts with "None", the post-processing shortcut with the default prompt, and a prompt shortcut with its prompt. While a dictation is recording, the indicator shows the prompt for this dictation and offers a menu listing "None" and every prompt; a choice applies to this dictation only and does not change the default. The menu opens within 200 ms without taking keyboard focus from the user's application, on every platform where the indicator is shown.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 2

### AC-004

**Criterion:** Each prompt uses the default provider and model unless it defines a provider and model override. Providers are the existing ones, including the local custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint and, where available, Apple Intelligence. A prompt whose provider lacks a required endpoint, model or API key is shown as not ready with the missing item; processing with it skips the AI step.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 3

### AC-005

**Criterion:** When the AI step fails (provider or HTTP error, empty or whitespace-only result, provider not ready) or the whole step, including any internal retry or fallback request, exceeds 30 seconds, the initial transcript is inserted, the indicator states for at least 4 seconds that processing failed and the original was inserted, and the history keeps the initial transcript, the prompt name and the failure reason. Cancelling during processing inserts nothing; history behaves as today for cancelled dictations.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 4

### AC-006

**Criterion:** A prompt may have 0–2 shortcuts. A prompt shortcut starts a dictation processed with that prompt and follows the global activation mode. Prompt shortcuts use the shared conflict checker of feature 004 against every other shortcut. Deleting a prompt removes its shortcuts after confirmation.
**Priority:** P2 | **Story:** Story 5

### AC-007

**Criterion:** The test panel runs a prompt on editable sample text (prefilled with the last transcript when one exists) and shows the result, provider, model and duration, or the error, within the 30-second limit. A test never inserts text into another application and never writes history.
**Priority:** P2 | **Story:** Story 5

### AC-008

**Criterion:** The settings CLI (008) offers prompt list, create, update, delete, set-default and set-provider-override (provider id and model, or `--clear` to return to the default provider); prompt shortcuts are managed with the shortcut operations of feature 004. Outputs never contain API keys, in stdout, stderr or logs; provider readiness is reported as ready or the missing item. With `--json`, stdout contains only the JSON envelope; errors use stable codes.
**Priority:** P2 | **Story:** Story 6

## Clarifications

- Current code (2026-10-12): prompt create/update/delete commands exist; one selected prompt id (default none, so processing is silently skipped until chosen); processing runs only from the post-processing shortcut; no request timeout; on failure the original transcript is kept; providers include OpenAI-compatible remote services, a local custom endpoint defaulting to `http://localhost:11434/v1`, and Apple Intelligence on Apple Silicon.
- `[ASSUMED]` The starter prompts' texts are written in the plan and stored as ordinary prompts; "Translate to English" is one starter, and users create other target languages by copying it.
- `[ASSUMED]` A per-prompt provider/model override implements "configuration of provider and model"; API keys stay per provider.
- Provider configuration (base URL, model, API key) stays in the existing settings UI; the CLI only sets per-prompt overrides.
- `[ASSUMED]` A non-JSON reply in structured mode keeps today's behavior (the reply text is used); only errors, timeouts and empty results trigger the fallback.
- `[ASSUMED]` 30-second limit for the whole AI step, 50 prompts, 60-character names, 8000-character texts, 0–2 shortcuts per prompt.
- `[ASSUMED]` The indicator choice applies to the current dictation only; the default changes only in settings or the CLI.
- Out of scope: scripts, launching applications, OCR and any other Spokenly action not listed in the Input.
- Program context: specified in list order (001–010); the settings CLI foundation (008) ships first; shortcuts reuse the conflict checker of 004.

## QE Analysis

- **Criticality:** High; **Blast radius:** Every processed dictation and provider credentials; **Primary risk:** Lost or altered text and secret exposure; **Confidence:** Medium (post-processing source mapped, nothing executed).
- **Dimensions:** Functional correctness, data integrity, security (API keys, local vs remote routing), reliability (timeouts), UX, accessibility, migration.
- **P0 gates/evidence:** Fallback tests for error, invalid output, empty output, not-ready provider and timeout; prompt resolution tests per trigger and indicator choice; migration test keeping existing prompts and selection; secret-redaction tests over CLI stdout/stderr and logs.
- **P1 gates/evidence:** Indicator menu does not steal focus (native check on macOS); routing tests proving override requests reach the configured endpoint; UI keyboard and validation checks; test panel never writes history.
- **Non-functional expectations:** Request limit 30 seconds; the indicator menu opens within 200 ms; no transcript or prompt text in logs above debug level; API keys never logged at any level.
- **Missing evidence:** No runtime test; starter prompt texts to be written in the plan; mockups deferred before `spec-ship`.
- **Boundary:** QE defines risk and test sufficiency; the independent review judges requirements; Penflow governs UI design evidence; spec-test executes runtime proof; a security audit of credential storage is separate.

# Feature Spec: Destination Application

## Header

- **Feature:** Destination Application
- **Branch:** None — specification only (program specified before `spec-ship`)
- **Date:** 2026-10-12
- **Status:** Planned
- **Input:** Program item 6: remember the application at dictation start. Show its logo and name near the live indicator. Switching applications during the recording must not change this destination. At the end, return to the chosen application to insert the text. During the dictation, allow a deliberate change of destination from the badge: for example, start in ChatGPT, move to Comet, then explicitly choose Comet as the destination. Preserve the transcript if the application or the target field is no longer available. ## Acceptance Criteria

### AC-001

**Criterion:** When a dictation starts and the frontmost application is not Handy, Handy records its identity (bundle identifier on macOS; application user model ID on Windows when available, otherwise executable path), display name, icon and process id. Application switches during the recording, processing and AI step do not change it. When Handy is frontmost, no destination is recorded.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 1

### AC-002

**Criterion:** With "Return to the dictation's application" on (default on where supported), before insertion Handy activates the destination and waits until it is frontmost, for at most 1 second and without freezing Handy's interface, re-checks that it is still frontmost immediately before inserting (a failed re-check counts as an activation failure, without retry), then runs the configured insertion method unchanged. With the paste method "none" no application is activated. With the setting off, or without a destination, insertion targets the frontmost application as today.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Stories 1 and 5

### AC-003

**Criterion:** While the indicator is visible and "Return to the dictation's application" is on and supported, a badge next to it shows the destination icon and name, or "Frontmost app" without a destination. The badge has the accessible name "Destination: <name>". When the setting is off or unsupported, no badge is shown. With the overlay style set to none, no badge is shown and the destination behavior still applies.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 2

### AC-004

**Criterion:** Until insertion begins, the badge shows a cross control: one click on it removes the destination of the current dictation (badge "Frontmost app", text inserted into the application frontmost at the end), as the menu entry "Frontmost app at the end" does; the cross has the accessible name "Remove destination". Clicking the badge itself opens a menu listing the application frontmost now first (Handy excluded), then other running applications that have windows, each with icon and name, and "Frontmost app at the end". Choosing an entry changes the destination of the current dictation only and updates the badge within 200 ms; dismissing keeps it. When insertion begins, an open menu closes and later choices are ignored. Opening and using the menu does not take keyboard focus from the user's application.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 3

### AC-005

**Criterion:** If the destination is no longer running, is not frontmost within 1 second of activation, or the insertion method reports failure, no text is sent to any other application; the transcript stays in history whenever history saving succeeds as today, the indicator displays the reason (app closed, activation failed, insertion failed) for at least 4 seconds (with the overlay style none, the recovery bubble of 010 carries the reason), and the transcript is handed to the recovery bubble (010).
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 4

### AC-006

**Criterion:** Destination, insertion method and clipboard handling are separate settings and steps: this feature decides only which application is activated. Handy passes the insertion method's outcome (for smart paste, the outcomes of 007) to the recovery bubble (010) and to automatic Enter (009), reports "insertion attempted" when the method reports success, and never reports that text was verified in a field except when the method itself verified it (the smart paste outcome "inserted, verified" of 007, based on reading the field back).
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 4

### AC-007

**Criterion:** Support is macOS and Windows. On Linux, and wherever the frontmost application cannot be read, the setting is shown as unavailable on this system with the reason, and insertion behaves as today.
**Priority:** P2 | **Story:** Story 5

### AC-008

**Criterion:** The settings CLI (008) reads and sets "Return to the dictation's application" with the same validation as the UI, including the unsupported-platform refusal. With `--json`, stdout contains only the JSON envelope.
**Priority:** P2 | **Story:** Story 5

| Entity | Description | Key fields |

| Destination | Application targeted by one dictation | identity, display name, icon, process id, source (captured or badge), captured at |
| Insertion outcome | Result reported after insertion | attempted, app closed, activation failed, insertion failed |

## Clarifications

- Current code (2026-10-12): no capture of the frontmost application exists; text goes to whatever application is frontmost at paste time. The overlay is a non-activating panel that accepts clicks.
- `[ASSUMED]` The destination is an application, not a window or a field. Activating it returns to its last active window; whether its text field still has focus is decided by that application. Field-level detection belongs to the recovery bubble (010).
- `[ASSUMED]` 1-second activation wait; reason shown for at least 4 seconds.
- `[ASSUMED]` On by default where supported, because the request describes it as the expected behavior; a switch restores the previous behavior.
- Decision 2026-10-13 (Julien): a cross on the badge removes the remembered destination in one click; the menu remains for choosing another application.
- `[ASSUMED]` The badge menu is pointer-operated so that it never takes keyboard focus; keyboard users keep the captured destination or use PIN operations (009).
- The live destination status is not exposed by this feature's CLI; PIN status belongs to feature 009.
- `[ASSUMED]` Linux is out of scope because reading the frontmost application is not reliable across Wayland compositors.
- Compatibility with ChatGPT, Comet and other applications is unverified; the plan includes native checks with these applications.
- Pinning the destination across dictations is feature 009; the recovery bubble is 010; smart paste (007) is an insertion method that runs after this feature has activated the destination.
- Program context: specified in list order (001–010); the settings CLI foundation (008) ships first.

## QE Analysis

- **Criticality:** High; **Blast radius:** Where every transcript goes; **Primary risk:** Text sent to the wrong application or lost; **Confidence:** Low-medium (no existing capture code; platform behavior unverified).
- **Dimensions:** Functional correctness, security/privacy (wrong-window leakage), reliability, platform compatibility, accessibility, UX.
- **P0 gates/evidence:** State tests proving app switches do not change the destination; tests proving no insertion occurs when the destination is closed or not frontmost in time; badge change applies to the current dictation only.
- **P1 gates/evidence:** Native macOS checks with TextEdit, Notes, ChatGPT desktop and Comet (start in one, switch, choose from badge); Windows check with two applications; non-activating menu check; screen-reader label check.
- **Non-functional expectations:** Capture at start under 50 ms; activation wait bounded at 1 second; badge update under 200 ms; no window titles or text logged above debug level.
- **Missing evidence:** No runtime test; real compatibility with ChatGPT and Comet unverified; mockups deferred before `spec-ship`.
- **Boundary:** QE defines risk and test sufficiency; the independent review judges requirements; Penflow governs UI design evidence; spec-test executes runtime proof.

## Edge Cases

- Destination restarted during the recording (new process, same identity): the running instance with that identity is activated.
- Several windows of the destination: activation returns to its last active window.
- Destination in full screen on another Space: activation switches to that Space before insertion.
- Dictation cancelled: no activation and no insertion.
- Same app chosen from the badge as captured: no change.

# Feature Spec: Smart Paste

## Header

- **Feature:** Smart Paste
- **Branch:** None — specification only (program specified before `spec-ship`)
- **Date:** 2026-10-12
- **Status:** Planned
- **Input:** Program item 7, scope replaced on 2026-10-12 by Julien's decision (relayed from Codex): replace the clipboard recovery window (10–15 seconds) with smart paste inspired by Spokenly; do not plan or implement the recovery window for now; keep number 7. Read the Spokenly smart-paste report (`.investigations/spokenly-smart-paste-2026-10-09/rapport.md`). Adopt its documented principles in Handy: multi-type save of the clipboard; transcript provided on demand by a pasteboard data provider; single first-read callback; current-host-only and transient marking; restoration after the read with a fallback delay and a `changeCount` guard that preserves any newer copy; strategy adapted to the application and the keyboard, selecting the ABC then US layout and restoring the keyboard afterwards. Static Spokenly constants: 300 ms / 800 ms, Jump Desktop 1.5 s / 3 s. Inserting through `AXSelectedText` stays a distinct method (superseded by the decision of 2026-10-13 below); destination and PIN act upstream. Verify real insertion and compatibility, because the reverse-engineering evidence is static. Decisions of 2026-10-13 (Julien): (1) a previous clipboard content or an earlier transcript must never be pasted by mistake: restore only after a read confirmed after the paste keystroke, once reads have been quiet for 300 ms after the last one, and never restore when no read occurred (the transcript stays and recovery is offered); (2) try direct insertion through the accessibility API first, verified by reading the field back, then fall back to the clipboard paste, then to the recovery bubble. Program item 8 requires the settings CLI to read and modify output behaviors.
- **Feature Number:** 007
## User Scenarios & Testing

### Story 1 — Paste without losing my clipboard `P1`

**As a** Handy user on macOS, **I want to** have the transcript pasted while my clipboard comes back intact, **so that** dictating never destroys what I had copied.

**Priority reason:** Clipboard loss is the main cost of clipboard-based insertion.
**Independent test:** Copy rich content (text with formatting and an image), dictate into TextEdit, and compare the clipboard before and after.

```gherkin
Feature: Smart paste restores the previous clipboard
  Scenario: Restore after the target reads the transcript
    Given the clipboard holds rich text and an image
    And the paste method is smart paste and the clipboard paste is used
    When a dictation produces "hello world" and TextEdit reads the clipboard after the paste keystroke
    Then TextEdit receives "hello world"
    And 300 ms after the last read the clipboard holds the same rich text and image as before
  Scenario: Probe then read
    Given a Chromium-based target reads the clipboard twice, 150 ms apart, after the paste keystroke
    When smart paste waits for restoration
    Then restoration happens 300 ms after the second read, not after the first
  Scenario: No read never restores the previous content
    Given the paste method is smart paste and the clipboard paste is used
    When the target never reads the clipboard within 800 ms after the paste keystroke
    Then the previous clipboard content is not restored
    And the transcript stays on the clipboard
    And the insertion outcome is "not read"
  Scenario: Empty clipboard before
    Given the clipboard was empty before the dictation
    When the restoration runs
    Then the clipboard is empty again
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD

  B --> C[Prepare clipboard: current host only, transient marker]
```

### Story 2 — Never overwrite a newer copy `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** keep anything copied after the dictation started pasting, **so that** restoration never erases my own work.

**Priority reason:** Overwriting a fresh copy is unrecoverable data loss.
**Independent test:** Make the target delay its read, copy something else before restoration, and check the clipboard afterwards.

```gherkin

    When the user copies "new text" before the restoration runs
    Then the restoration is abandoned
    And the clipboard still holds "new text"
  Scenario: Another application writes the clipboard
    Given smart paste published the transcript
    When another application writes an image before the restoration runs
    Then the image stays on the clipboard
```

### Story 3 — Adapt to the application and the keyboard `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** have smart paste choose a strategy that works in the frontmost application and with my keyboard layout, **so that** paste works in remote-desktop apps and with non-US layouts.

**Priority reason:** A wrong strategy types garbage or pastes nothing in these environments.

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** have the transcript written straight into the text field when the application allows it, **so that** my clipboard is never touched and the insertion is proven.

## Acceptance Criteria

AC-001 to AC-007 belonged to the retired clipboard recovery window scope and are not reused (see Clarifications).

### AC-008

**Criterion:** With smart paste on macOS, before writing, Handy saves every pasteboard item with all its types as data; it then prepares the general pasteboard for current-host-only content, adds the `org.nspasteboard.TransientType` marker, and publishes the transcript as an item whose plain-text data is provided on demand. The data provider supplies the full transcript on every request and reports the first request after the paste keystroke exactly once. Requests before the keystroke are served but do not count as the first read. The keystroke instant is recorded immediately before the first key-down of the Cmd+V chord is posted, as in the current reliable paste; reads served while the chord is held count. Waiting and posting the chord never block the serving of pasteboard reads. The existing delay before the keystroke (`paste_delay_ms`) still applies, the fixed delay after it (`paste_delay_after_ms`) is replaced by smart paste timings, and the V key is resolved after any layout switch of AC-011 for the layout then active. Saving the previous content is bounded to 200 ms and 50 MB; a type that cannot be saved within those bounds is skipped, and "exactly" in AC-009 applies to the saved types.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 1

### AC-009

**Criterion:** Restoration requires a read observed after the paste keystroke. It runs once no new read has occurred for 300 ms after the last read, and at the latest 8 s after the first read if reads keep coming (for Jump Desktop, `com.p5sys.jump.mac.viewer`: 1.5 s of quiet). When no read is observed within 800 ms after the keystroke (3 s for Jump Desktop), the outcome is "not read", the saved snapshot is discarded and the previous content is never restored for that dictation: the transcript stays on the clipboard until the user or another application replaces it. A restoration puts back the saved items and types exactly, or clears the pasteboard if it was empty, only when the pasteboard `changeCount` still equals the value recorded at publication; otherwise it does nothing.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Stories 1 and 2

### AC-010

**Criterion:** Strategy by destination bundle identifier: `com.apple.ScreenContinuity` (iPhone Mirroring) and `com.microsoft.rdc.macos` (Windows App) receive the transcript as Unicode key events without clipboard use; `com.apple.ScreenSharing` receives a clipboard write of the transcript without a paste keystroke and keeps it until the user copies something else; every other application uses direct insertion (AC-017) and then the clipboard paste of AC-008/AC-009. The accessibility permission check applies to the strategies that post key events (clipboard paste and Unicode typing). With clipboard handling "copy to clipboard", Unicode typing also leaves the transcript on the clipboard.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 3

### AC-011

**Criterion:** For the clipboard paste, when the current input source is a keyboard layout other than ABC or US, Handy selects `com.apple.keylayout.ABC`, or `com.apple.keylayout.US` when ABC cannot be selected, waits 50 ms for the switch to apply, sends Cmd+V, and restores the previous input source 100 ms after the last key of the chord is released. When the current input source is an input method, or neither layout can be selected, Handy sends Cmd+V without changing it.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 3

### AC-012

**Criterion:** Smart paste reports one outcome per dictation: "insertion attempted, read observed" when a read followed the keystroke; "not read" when none did; "permission missing" when accessibility permission is absent (checked before the clipboard is touched, so no keystroke is sent and the clipboard is unchanged); "typed" for Unicode typing; "clipboard handed over" for Screen Sharing, shown on the indicator as "Text placed on the clipboard for the remote screen"; "insertion failed" when posting the chord or the Unicode key events fails, or the transaction cannot start. Direct insertion adds "inserted, verified" and "uncertain" (AC-017). Only "inserted, verified", "insertion attempted, read observed" and "typed" count as a successful insertion for automatic Enter (009). "Not read", "permission missing", "uncertain" and "insertion failed" are handled as an insertion failure by the recovery bubble (010). The outcome is known only after the read or the 800 ms decision delay; automatic Enter and recovery wait for it. "Clipboard handed over" is neither a success for automatic Enter nor a failure for recovery. Only "inserted, verified" states that the field contains the text, because the field was read back; every other outcome makes no claim about the field content. If a read arrives after "not read" was declared, the transcript (still on the clipboard) is served, the outcome stays "not read" for automatic Enter, and the recovery bubble states that the text may have been pasted after all.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 4

### AC-013

**Criterion:** When clipboard handling is "copy to clipboard", smart paste replaces the restoration by leaving the transcript on the clipboard as plain text, as the current paths do; after a verified direct insertion it also writes the transcript to the clipboard as plain text. The history entry is never modified by smart paste.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 1

### AC-014

**Criterion:** Smart paste is a paste method available on macOS and is the default there for new installations. On upgrade on macOS, the beta "reliable paste" switch is removed from macOS: users whose paste method is Cmd+V move to smart paste, whether or not the beta switch was on; users with any other method keep it and the beta switch is dropped. On Windows the beta "reliable paste" switch and its path stay unchanged; Linux paste methods are unchanged.
**Priority:** P2 | **Story:** Story 5

### AC-015

**Criterion:** The settings CLI (008) reads and sets the paste method including `smart_paste`, with the UI validation (`smart_paste` refused outside macOS with `validation_failed`). With `--json`, stdout contains only the JSON envelope.
**Priority:** P2 | **Story:** Story 5

### AC-017

**Criterion:** On macOS, for applications not covered by AC-010, smart paste first tries direct insertion: with accessibility permission, and only when the focused element belongs to the destination application's process (006), it reads the focused element's text value and selected range, sets `AXSelectedText` to the transcript, then reads the value again, polling for up to 150 ms to let applications that update asynchronously apply the change. The attempt is verified when the new value equals the old value with the selected range replaced by the transcript; the outcome is then "inserted, verified" and the clipboard is never touched. If the element is a password field (role AXSecureTextField) or its value cannot be read, direct insertion is skipped; if the value is still unchanged at the end of the read-back window (whether setting reported success or failure), smart paste falls back to the clipboard paste (AC-008/AC-009). If the value changed but does not match the expected result, smart paste does not fall back, to avoid inserting the text twice, and the outcome is "uncertain".
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 6

### AC-018

**Criterion:** The insertion chain is: direct accessibility insertion (AC-017), then clipboard paste, then recovery bubble (010) for the outcomes "not read", "permission missing", "uncertain" and "insertion failed". Direct insertion, including the read-back window, adds at most 250 ms before the fallback starts.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 6

### AC-016

**Criterion:** Before release, native checks record the outcome, the inserted text and the restored clipboard for TextEdit, Notes, ChatGPT, Comet and one Chromium-based application, with AZERTY, US and Dvorak layouts, recording for each run which path was used (direct insertion or clipboard paste); applications where direct insertion is not verified exercise the clipboard paste, and for iPhone Mirroring, Windows App, Screen Sharing and Jump Desktop when available on the test machine; unavailable applications are listed as not verified. Pass thresholds over 10 runs per pair: direct insertion, transcript present exactly once and verified at least 9 times; clipboard paste, transcript inserted and previous clipboard restored at least 9 times; Unicode typing, transcript typed correctly at least 9 times; Screen Sharing, transcript available on the remote side at least 9 times. TextEdit, Notes, ChatGPT and Comet must pass with AZERTY, US and Dvorak before release, and no run of any application may deliver a previous clipboard content or a previous transcript; failures elsewhere are listed as known incompatibilities.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Stories 1, 3 and 4
