**Independent test:** For each activation mode, start with shortcut A and try to stop with shortcut A and with shortcut B of the same action.

```gherkin
Feature: Activation semantics with several shortcuts
  Scenario: Toggle mode
    Given the activation mode is toggle
    And the dictation action has shortcuts A and B
    When the user presses A to start and then presses B
    Then the dictation stops
  Scenario: Push-to-talk mode
    Given the activation mode is push-to-talk
    And the user holds A to record
    When the user presses and releases B during the recording
    Then the recording continues
    And it stops when A is released
  Scenario: Hold-or-toggle mode
    Given the activation mode is hold-or-toggle
    When the user taps A shorter than the hold threshold
    Then the dictation stays on until a shortcut of the action is pressed again
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Shortcut of the action pressed] --> B{Activation mode}
  B -- Toggle --> C{Session active?}
  C -- No --> D[Start session]
  C -- Yes --> E[Stop session]
  B -- Push-to-talk or held --> F{Session started by this shortcut?}
  F -- Yes --> G[Stop on its release]
  F -- No --> H[Ignore input while session active]
```

", "start_line": 62, "end_line": 98, "start_byte": 2660, "end_byte": 4173}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/004-multiple-dictation-shortcuts/spec.md:L99-L140", "source": ".specs/features/004-multiple-dictation-shortcuts/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 3 — Detect conflicts `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** be told when a combination is already used, **so that** one key press never triggers two actions.

**Priority reason:** Conflict detection is explicitly required.
**Independent test:** Try to add the cancel shortcut, the post-processing shortcut and an OS-reserved combination as dictation shortcuts.

```gherkin
Feature: Shortcut conflicts
  Scenario: Combination used by another action
    Given "option+shift+space" is the post-processing shortcut
    When the user adds "shift+option+space" to the dictation action
    Then the shortcut is rejected because it is already used by the post-processing action
    And the saved shortcuts are unchanged
  Scenario: Duplicate within the same action
    Given the dictation action has "option+space"
    When the user adds "option+space" again
    Then the shortcut is rejected as already assigned to this action
  Scenario: Combination unavailable from the OS
    Given another application already registered the combination globally
    When the user adds it
    Then registration fails with an explanation and nothing is saved
  Scenario: Modifier-only overlap
    Given the keyboard implementation allows modifier-only shortcuts
    And "option" is a dictation shortcut
    When the user adds "option+space" to another action
    Then the shortcut is rejected because pressing "option+space" would also trigger "option"
    And the saved shortcuts are unchanged
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Candidate combination] --> B[Normalize modifiers and key]
  B --> C{Equal to an existing shortcut?}
  C -- Yes --> D[Reject: name the owning action]
  C -- No --> E{Modifier-only overlap?}
  E -- Yes --> F[Reject: overlap would double trigger]
  E -- No --> G{OS registration succeeds?}
  G -- No --> H[Reject with OS reason]
  G -- Yes --> I[Persist]
```

**Criterion:** The global activation mode and hold threshold apply to every shortcut of an action. In toggle mode and in the locked (toggled) phase of hold-or-toggle, any shortcut of the action that started the session stops it. ", "start_line": 21, "end_line": 22, "start_byte": 954, "end_byte": 983}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/005-custom-ai-prompts/spec.md:L23-L63", "source": ".specs/features/005-custom-ai-prompts/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 1 — Manage a prompt library `P1`

", "start_line": 64, "end_line": 107, "start_byte": 2793, "end_byte": 4895}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/005-custom-ai-prompts/spec.md:L108-L141", "source": ".specs/features/005-custom-ai-prompts/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 3 — Configure local or remote AI per prompt `P1`

", "start_line": 21, "end_line": 22, "start_byte": 906, "end_byte": 935}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md:L23-L58", "source": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 1 — Edit ordered microphone choices `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** add, remove and reorder microphone choices, **so that** each recording uses my preferred available device.

**Priority reason:** Device choice controls the core recording workflow.
**Independent test:** Configure two devices, move the second above the first, verify only the draft changed, activate Save, reload settings and inspect the committed order.

```gherkin
Feature: Ordered microphone preferences
  Scenario: Reorder available devices
    Given the configured order is USB headset then MacBook microphone
    When the user moves MacBook microphone above USB headset
    Then the draft order is MacBook microphone then USB headset
    And the persisted order remains USB headset then MacBook microphone before Save
    When the user activates Save and it succeeds
    Then the persisted order is MacBook microphone then USB headset
    And the next recording attempts MacBook microphone first
  Scenario: Invalid duplicate choice
    Given USB headset is already configured
    When the user adds USB headset again
    Then the duplicate is rejected with an actionable error
    And the saved order remains unchanged
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Edit draft priority list] --> B{Valid unique choices?}
  B -- No --> D[Show error and retain saved order]
  B -- Yes --> S{Save activated?}
  S -- No --> A
  S -- Yes --> C{Commit succeeds?}
  C -- No --> D
  C -- Yes --> E[Persist complete new order]
  E --> F[Next recording uses committed order]
```

", "start_line": 23, "end_line": 58, "start_byte": 935, "end_byte": 2486}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md:L59-L112", "source": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 2 — Record through availability fallback `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** see unavailable choices and record with the next usable microphone, **so that** disconnecting a preferred device does not destroy my preferences.

**Priority reason:** Fallback prevents loss of the core recording capability.
**Independent test:** Disconnect the first configured device, start a recording and compare the effective device with unchanged stored preferences.

```gherkin
Feature: Microphone availability fallback
  Scenario: First choice unavailable
    Given USB headset then MacBook microphone is configured
    And USB headset is disconnected while MacBook microphone is available
    When a recording starts
    Then MacBook microphone is opened
    And USB headset remains first in the configured list with an unavailable label
  Scenario: No configured device opens
    Given every configured microphone is unavailable or fails to open
    When a recording starts
    Then the system default is attempted after the configured choices
    And failure of that attempt reports a recording error without changing preferences
  Scenario: Reconnection restores priority
    Given the first configured microphone is unavailable for one recording
    When it reconnects before the next recording starts
    Then it is attempted before the lower priority microphones
  Scenario: Ambiguous name is skipped
    Given "USB headset" is configured first and two present devices are named "USB headset"
    When a recording starts
    Then "USB headset" counts as a failed attempt with reason ambiguous
    And the next configured choice is attempted
  Scenario: Always-on stream follows the priority
    Given always-on microphone mode is enabled and no recording is active
    When the user saves a new priority order
    Then the input stream reopens on the first usable choice of the new order
  Scenario: Device lost during a recording
    Given a recording is in progress on USB headset
    When USB headset disconnects
    Then the recording ends and the audio captured before the loss is transcribed
    And the user is told the recording was cut short
    And the configured list is unchanged
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Start recording with current configuration] --> B{Next configured choice exists?}
  B -- Yes --> C{Present and opens?}
  C -- Yes --> D[Record with effective device]
  C -- No --> B
  B -- No --> E{System default opens?}
  E -- Yes --> D
  E -- No --> F[Report recording error]
  D --> G[Retain configured priority]
  F --> G
```

", "start_line": 59, "end_line": 112, "start_byte": 2486, "end_byte": 5051}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md:L113-L154", "source": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 3 — Preserve clamshell and upgrade behavior `P1`

**As a** existing Handy user, **I want to** retain my current microphone and clamshell choices during upgrade, **so that** the new list respects existing intent.

**Priority reason:** Migration and clamshell behavior affect persisted configuration and shared runtime.
**Independent test:** Load a legacy settings fixture and exercise open-lid and closed-lid resolution.

```gherkin
Feature: Compatible microphone priority migration
  Scenario: Legacy selection migration
    Given the stored settings have selected_microphone equal to USB headset
    And no microphone priority setting exists
    When the settings load after upgrade
    Then USB headset becomes the sole configured priority entry
    And the clamshell microphone setting is unchanged
    And a second load preserves the same configuration
  Scenario: Closed lid override unavailable
    Given a clamshell override and an ordered priority list are configured
    And the lid is closed
    And the override cannot be opened
    When a recording starts
    Then the system default is attempted, as in the current behavior
    And neither the override nor the list is erased
  Scenario: Open lid does not prefer the override
    Given the lid is open or its state cannot be determined
    When a recording starts
    Then the normal configured priority list is used
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Load settings] --> B{Priority key absent?}
  B -- Yes --> C[Migrate legacy selection once]
  B -- No --> D[Retain existing priority]
  C --> E{Closed lid and override configured?}
  D --> E
  E -- Yes --> F{Override opens?}
  F -- Yes --> G[Record with override]
  F -- No --> I[System default, as today]
  E -- No --> H[Resolve normal priority then default]
```

", "start_line": 113, "end_line": 154, "start_byte": 5051, "end_byte": 6840}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md:L155-L184", "source": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 4 — Use identical UI and CLI configuration contracts `P2`

**As a** automation user, **I want to** read and update the microphone list through JSON CLI operations, **so that** scripts receive the same validation and persisted outcome as settings UI.

**Priority reason:** F8 is the foundational control surface required before F1 delivery.
**Independent test:** Run equivalent valid and invalid UI/CLI writes against an isolated settings store and compare readback.

```gherkin
Feature: Shared microphone settings operations
  Scenario: CLI saves a valid complete order
    Given the settings CLI foundation is implemented
    When the user submits a valid ordered microphone list through its JSON write operation
    Then the shared backend validates and persists that list
    And a JSON read reports configured order separately from effective microphone and availability
  Scenario: Concurrent stale write
    Given the UI has saved a newer settings revision
    When the CLI submits an earlier expected revision
    Then it returns a conflict without partially writing settings
    And a fresh read reports the UI's order
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[UI or CLI submits list and revision] --> B{Valid input and current revision?}
  B -- Yes --> C[Persist once and publish committed revision]
  B -- No --> D[Return validation error or revision conflict]
  C --> E[Readback same order from either surface]
  D --> F[Retain previous configuration]
```

", "start_line": 185, "end_line": 186, "start_byte": 8310, "end_byte": 8334}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md:L187-L191", "source": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### AC-001

", "start_line": 187, "end_line": 191, "start_byte": 8334, "end_byte": 8636}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md:L192-L196", "source": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### AC-002

**Criterion:** Each configured choice remains visible with available, unavailable, ambiguous or unknown status. Availability refreshes when the audio settings open, every 5 seconds while they remain open, and on manual Retry; refresh errors show unknown status and an actionable retry. The microphone actually used is displayed separately from saved order: during a recording or an open always-on stream, the current device and its reason (first choice, fallback, clamshell, system default); otherwise the device used by the last recording since launch, labelled as such, or "not used yet" after a restart. Add offers the currently enumerated devices. Status uses text in addition to color.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 2

", "start_line": 192, "end_line": 196, "start_byte": 8636, "end_byte": 9378}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md:L197-L201", "source": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### AC-003

**Criterion:** Whenever the input stream opens — at the start of a recording, or, in always-on microphone mode, when the stream opens at launch, after a committed priority change while no recording is active, or after a device loss — attempt configured devices in saved order and use the first device that is present, unambiguous and opens. A configured name matching several present devices counts as a failed attempt with reason ambiguous. Each open attempt times out after 2 seconds and the whole resolution after 6 seconds; until the stream is ready the indicator keeps its existing arming state and audio spoken before readiness is not captured. Attempt the system default only after configured attempts fail (after the single fresh re-enumeration, unresolvable entries count as failed attempts); if no device opens, report the recording error. Transient enumeration/open failures do not modify the saved list.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 2

", "start_line": 197, "end_line": 201, "start_byte": 9378, "end_byte": 10349}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md:L202-L206", "source": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### AC-004

**Criterion:** A fallback, disconnect or reconnect never deletes/reorders saved choices or resets the clamshell setting. A reconnected higher priority device is preferred on the next recording; in always-on mode the priority is re-resolved when a recording starts and, when the result differs from the open stream's device, the stream reopens on it before capture begins. Editing priority during a recording affects the next session and does not interrupt or discard the current session's captured audio.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Stories 1 and 2

", "start_line": 202, "end_line": 206, "start_byte": 10349, "end_byte": 10913}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md:L207-L211", "source": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### AC-005

**Criterion:** The closed-lid behavior is preserved exactly: with a configured override and a confirmed closed lid, attempt the clamshell microphone; if it is unavailable or fails to open, attempt the system default, as today. ", "start_line": 425, "end_line": 429, "start_byte": 25882, "end_byte": 26490}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md:L430-L442", "source": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## Edge Cases

- Channel selection: the existing channel setting applies only when valid for the opened device; otherwise the device's default channel mapping is used and the setting is not changed.
- Legacy key: after migration `selected_microphone` stays stored unchanged (not read while the priority key exists) so a downgrade keeps the previous choice; the legacy set command is replaced by the priority operations.
- Reset: empties the draft normal list only; it requires Save and leaves clamshell unchanged.
- Empty normal list: use and show system default when the lid is open/unknown or no usable override applies; a confirmed closed lid still attempts the configured override first.
- All devices missing: retain configured entries and show the attempted default or recording error.
- Enumeration error: mark availability unknown and retain preferences; after the single fresh re-enumeration, configured entries count as failed attempts, the system default is attempted, and the enumeration warning is shown.
- Duplicate names: mark ambiguous; do not persist transient enumeration indices or select an arbitrary match.
- Concurrent reorder and start: capture one committed revision; edits affect the next session.
- Persistence failure: restore last committed settings and allow retry without erasing the migration source.
- Repeated device failures: bounded attempts terminate with an error; no unbounded stream reopen loop.

**Criterion:** A rule is valid when the trimmed recognized text has 1–100 characters, contains no line break, tab or `;`, and does not start with `#`; and the trimmed replacement has 1–500 characters and contains no line break or tab. Recognized text is unique by its normalized key (trimmed, inner whitespace collapsed to one space, Unicode case-folded). Invalid or duplicate input is rejected with a field error and no partial write. The rule set holds at most 1000 rules.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Stories 1 and 2

**Criterion:** The bulk editor shows all rules as text in the exchange format, accepts pasted text, and shows a line-by-line preview (add, update, delete, unchanged, ignored, error) before applying. **Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 2

", "start_line": 223, "end_line": 227, "start_byte": 10500, "end_byte": 10859}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/002-word-replacements/spec.md:L228-L232", "source": ".specs/features/002-word-replacements/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### AC-004

**Criterion:** The exchange format is UTF-8 text with one rule per line. A line containing a tab splits on its first tab; otherwise it splits on its first `;`. Blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored. The first line that is neither blank nor a comment is ignored as a header when it equals (case-insensitively, after trimming) `texte_reconnu;remplacement` or `recognized;replacement`. Export writes the header `recognized;replacement`, then one `recognized;replacement` line per rule in list order; because AC-002 forbids tab, `;` and a leading `#` in recognized text and tab in replacements, every valid rule set round-trips. Replacement text may contain `;`. CSV quoting is not supported; spreadsheet copy and paste uses the tab separator.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Stories 2 and 3

**Criterion:** Import accepts a file up to 1 MB in merge or replace mode. Merge updates the replacement of rules whose normalized key matches, keeps their position, and appends new rules in file order. Replace makes the file content the whole rule set in file order. Duplicate keys inside one file or block are errors. Import is atomic: on any error, unreadable file or persistence failure, saved rules are unchanged. Export then replace-import of the same file reproduces the same rules and order.

", "start_line": 233, "end_line": 237, "start_byte": 11672, "end_byte": 12222}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/002-word-replacements/spec.md:L238-L242", "source": ".specs/features/002-word-replacements/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### AC-006

**Criterion:** Matching is case-insensitive (Unicode case folding) and the replacement is inserted exactly as written. A match must start and end on word boundaries: the characters immediately before and after the match are not Unicode letters or digits, or are the text edges. On a side where the recognized text begins or ends with a CJK ideograph, kana or hangul character, no boundary check applies, because those scripts are written without spaces. A whitespace run inside the recognized text matches any non-empty whitespace run; other characters match literally. Punctuation adjacent to a match is kept.

", "start_line": 238, "end_line": 242, "start_byte": 12222, "end_byte": 12884}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/002-word-replacements/spec.md:L243-L247", "source": ".specs/features/002-word-replacements/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### AC-007

**Criterion:** Rules apply in one left-to-right pass over the final recognized text. At each position the rule with the longest normalized key wins; ties follow list order. A matched span is replaced and scanning continues after it; replacement output is never rescanned (no chaining). Rules apply after speech recognition, language detection and Chinese script conversion, and before the existing approximate custom-word correction, filler removal, normalization and AI post-processing. Approximate correction never alters a span produced by a replacement. The inserted text and the history text include the replacements. Rules committed from the UI or the CLI apply from the next dictation of the running app. An empty rule set leaves text unchanged.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 4

- Recognized text with accents or non-Latin letters: Unicode case folding applies; boundaries follow AC-006, including the CJK exception.

- Settings changed by the CLI while the UI editor has unsaved edits: UI Save returns a revision conflict and offers reload.
- Very long transcript: matching remains linear in text length times rule count, within the stated budget.

", "start_line": 21, "end_line": 22, "start_byte": 803, "end_byte": 832}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/003-recognition-vocabulary/spec.md:L23-L57", "source": ".specs/features/003-recognition-vocabulary/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 1 — Maintain the vocabulary list `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** add, remove and paste vocabulary terms, **so that** names and technical terms I use are known to the recognizer.

**Priority reason:** The term list is the input of every other story.
**Independent test:** Paste four terms (one per line, one duplicate), save, reload settings and inspect the stored list.

```gherkin
Feature: Vocabulary list
  Scenario: Paste several terms
    Given the vocabulary is empty
    When the user pastes the lines "Claude Code", "Claude Sonnet", "claude code" and "OpenClaw"
    Then the preview shows three terms to add and "claude code" as a duplicate of "Claude Code"
    When the user applies the preview
    Then the vocabulary is "Claude Code", "Claude Sonnet", "OpenClaw" in that order
  Scenario: Remove a term
    Given the vocabulary contains "OpenClaw"
    When the user removes "OpenClaw"
    Then the saved vocabulary no longer contains it
  Scenario: Reject an invalid term
    When the user adds a term of 101 characters
    Then the term is rejected with an explanation of the 100-character limit
    And the saved vocabulary is unchanged
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Add, remove or paste terms] --> B{Each term valid and unique?}
  B -- No --> C[Show per-term error; keep saved list]
  B -- Yes --> D{Commit succeeds?}
  D -- No --> C
  D -- Yes --> E[Persist ordered vocabulary with new revision]
  E --> F[Next recognition uses the committed vocabulary]
```

", "start_line": 23, "end_line": 57, "start_byte": 832, "end_byte": 2329}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/003-recognition-vocabulary/spec.md:L58-L105", "source": ".specs/features/003-recognition-vocabulary/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 2 — See whether the vocabulary is effective `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** see, for the selected model, whether the vocabulary is used during recognition, **so that** I am never misled by a setting that has no effect.

**Priority reason:** The request explicitly forbids presenting an unsupported setting as effective.
**Independent test:** Select a Whisper model, then a Parakeet model, then a live-streaming configuration, and read the status shown each time.

```gherkin
Feature: Truthful vocabulary status
  Scenario: Model that supports recognition context
    Given the selected model declares recognition-context support
    And batch transcription is used
    When the user opens the vocabulary settings
    Then the status says the vocabulary is used during recognition by this model
  Scenario: Model without recognition context
    Given the selected model declares no recognition-context support
    When the user opens the vocabulary settings
    Then the status says this model cannot use the vocabulary during recognition
    And the status says approximate correction after recognition applies instead
    And no control suggests that recognition is influenced
  Scenario: Live streaming
    Given the live overlay produces the final text through streaming recognition
    When the user opens the vocabulary settings
    Then the status says recognition context is not used in live streaming
  Scenario: Capability unknown
    Given no model is loaded and the selected model's capabilities cannot be read
    When the user opens the vocabulary settings
    Then the status says support is unknown until the model loads
  Scenario: Supporting model but nothing to send
    Given the selected model supports recognition context in batch mode
    And the vocabulary is empty, or no term fits within the model's context budget
    When the user opens the vocabulary settings
    Then the status says no term is sent, with the reason (empty vocabulary or terms over the limit)
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Selected model and recognition mode] --> B{Capabilities readable?}
  B -- No --> C[Status: unknown until model loads]
  B -- Yes --> D{Streaming produces final text?}
  D -- Yes --> E[Status: not used in live streaming]
  D -- No --> F{Model declares context support?}
  F -- Yes --> I{At least one term fits the budget?}
  I -- Yes --> G[Status: used during recognition]
  I -- No --> J[Status: no term sent, with reason]
  F -- No --> H[Status: not supported; approximate correction applies]
```

", "start_line": 58, "end_line": 105, "start_byte": 2329, "end_byte": 4871}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/003-recognition-vocabulary/spec.md:L106-L142", "source": ".specs/features/003-recognition-vocabulary/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 3 — Bias recognition on supporting engines `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** have my terms passed to the recognizer when it supports it, **so that** "Claude Code" is recognized instead of "Cloud Code".

**Priority reason:** This is the recognition-time effect the user asked for.
**Independent test:** Transcribe a fixed audio sample saying "Claude Code" with and without the vocabulary on a supporting model, and inspect the engine request.

```gherkin
Feature: Vocabulary as recognition context
  Scenario: Supporting model receives the terms
    Given the vocabulary is "Claude Code", "OpenClaw"
    And the selected model supports recognition context in batch mode
    When a dictation is transcribed
    Then the engine request contains "Claude Code" and "OpenClaw" through the model's supported mechanism
  Scenario: Vocabulary exceeds the context budget
    Given the vocabulary is longer than the selected model's context budget
    When a dictation is transcribed
    Then terms are sent in list order until the budget is reached
    And the settings show how many terms are sent and which are not
  Scenario: Unsupported model is not sent the terms
    Given the selected model does not support recognition context
    When a dictation is transcribed
    Then no context is sent to the engine
    And approximate correction applies to the recognized text
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Dictation ready for recognition] --> B{Model supports context in this mode?}
  B -- No --> C[Recognize without context]
  C --> D[Approximate correction with vocabulary]
  B -- Yes --> E[Take terms in list order within budget]
  E --> F[Recognize with context]
  D --> G[Continue text pipeline]
  F --> G
```

", "start_line": 21, "end_line": 22, "start_byte": 747, "end_byte": 776}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/004-multiple-dictation-shortcuts/spec.md:L23-L61", "source": ".specs/features/004-multiple-dictation-shortcuts/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 1 — Add a second shortcut for dictation `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** bind two or more key combinations to the dictation action, **so that** I can start dictation from the hand position that suits each keyboard or app.

**Priority reason:** This is the requested capability.
**Independent test:** Add a second shortcut to the dictation action, restart, then start and stop dictation with each shortcut in turn.

```gherkin
Feature: Several shortcuts for one action
  Scenario: Add an alternative shortcut
    Given the dictation action has the shortcut "option+space"
    When the user adds the shortcut "ctrl+option+d" to the same action
    Then the dictation action lists "option+space" and "ctrl+option+d"
    And pressing either shortcut starts a dictation
  Scenario: Remove an alternative shortcut
    Given the dictation action has two shortcuts
    When the user removes "ctrl+option+d"
    Then only "option+space" starts a dictation
  Scenario: The last shortcut cannot be removed
    Given the dictation action has one shortcut
    When the user inspects its remove control
    Then removal is unavailable with an explanation that each action keeps at least one shortcut
    And the user can still change or reset that shortcut
  Scenario: Fifth shortcut
    Given the dictation action has four shortcuts
    When the user inspects the add control
    Then adding is unavailable with an explanation of the four-shortcut limit
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Record a new key combination] --> B{Valid for the keyboard implementation?}
  B -- No --> C[Show validation error; keep saved shortcuts]
  B -- Yes --> D{Conflicts with another shortcut or the OS?}
  D -- Yes --> E[Show conflict naming the other action; keep saved shortcuts]
  D -- No --> F[Register and persist the added shortcut]
  F --> G[Every shortcut of the action triggers it]
```

", "start_line": 23, "end_line": 61, "start_byte": 776, "end_byte": 2660}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/004-multiple-dictation-shortcuts/spec.md:L62-L98", "source": ".specs/features/004-multiple-dictation-shortcuts/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 2 — Keep the existing activation behavior `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** have every shortcut follow my activation mode, **so that** toggle, push-to-talk and hold-or-toggle behave as before.

**Priority reason:** Breaking activation semantics would make dictation unreliable.
**Independent test:** For each activation mode, start with shortcut A and try to stop with shortcut A and with shortcut B of the same action.

```gherkin
Feature: Activation semantics with several shortcuts
  Scenario: Toggle mode
    Given the activation mode is toggle
    And the dictation action has shortcuts A and B
    When the user presses A to start and then presses B
    Then the dictation stops
  Scenario: Push-to-talk mode
    Given the activation mode is push-to-talk
    And the user holds A to record
    When the user presses and releases B during the recording
    Then the recording continues
    And it stops when A is released
  Scenario: Hold-or-toggle mode
    Given the activation mode is hold-or-toggle
    When the user taps A shorter than the hold threshold
    Then the dictation stays on until a shortcut of the action is pressed again
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Shortcut of the action pressed] --> B{Activation mode}
  B -- Toggle --> C{Session active?}
  C -- No --> D[Start session]
  C -- Yes --> E[Stop session]
  B -- Push-to-talk or held --> F{Session started by this shortcut?}
  F -- Yes --> G[Stop on its release]
  F -- No --> H[Ignore input while session active]
```

", "start_line": 62, "end_line": 98, "start_byte": 2660, "end_byte": 4173}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/004-multiple-dictation-shortcuts/spec.md:L99-L140", "source": ".specs/features/004-multiple-dictation-shortcuts/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 3 — Detect conflicts `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** be told when a combination is already used, **so that** one key press never triggers two actions.

**Priority reason:** Conflict detection is explicitly required.
**Independent test:** Try to add the cancel shortcut, the post-processing shortcut and an OS-reserved combination as dictation shortcuts.

```gherkin
Feature: Shortcut conflicts
  Scenario: Combination used by another action
    Given "option+shift+space" is the post-processing shortcut
    When the user adds "shift+option+space" to the dictation action
    Then the shortcut is rejected because it is already used by the post-processing action
    And the saved shortcuts are unchanged
  Scenario: Duplicate within the same action
    Given the dictation action has "option+space"
    When the user adds "option+space" again
    Then the shortcut is rejected as already assigned to this action
  Scenario: Combination unavailable from the OS
    Given another application already registered the combination globally
    When the user adds it
    Then registration fails with an explanation and nothing is saved
  Scenario: Modifier-only overlap
    Given the keyboard implementation allows modifier-only shortcuts
    And "option" is a dictation shortcut
    When the user adds "option+space" to another action
    Then the shortcut is rejected because pressing "option+space" would also trigger "option"
    And the saved shortcuts are unchanged
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Candidate combination] --> B[Normalize modifiers and key]
  B --> C{Equal to an existing shortcut?}
  C -- Yes --> D[Reject: name the owning action]
  C -- No --> E{Modifier-only overlap?}
  E -- Yes --> F[Reject: overlap would double trigger]
  E -- No --> G{OS registration succeeds?}
  G -- No --> H[Reject with OS reason]
  G -- Yes --> I[Persist]
```

", "start_line": 21, "end_line": 22, "start_byte": 954, "end_byte": 983}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/005-custom-ai-prompts/spec.md:L23-L63", "source": ".specs/features/005-custom-ai-prompts/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 1 — Manage a prompt library `P1`

", "start_line": 64, "end_line": 107, "start_byte": 2793, "end_byte": 4895}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/005-custom-ai-prompts/spec.md:L108-L141", "source": ".specs/features/005-custom-ai-prompts/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 3 — Configure local or remote AI per prompt `P1`

", "start_line": 381, "end_line": 385, "start_byte": 17860, "end_byte": 18115}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/008-settings-cli/plan.md:L82-L101", "source": ".specs/features/008-settings-cli/plan.md", "role": "plan", "text": "### Routing, startup fence and legacy compatibility

New app acquires a per-user/store instance lease before loading settings, under settings.lock, publishes its private endpoint before releasing startup ownership, and keeps the lease until shutdown. A headless writer acquires settings.lock, then checks the new lease/endpoint and passive legacy state again immediately before commit. GUI startup for the new version uses that same lock; it reads a complete commit or establishes ownership before the CLI can mutate. The lease is separate from the transaction lock; a busy or starting owner never means offline permission. A stale new-version endpoint is reclaimable only after OS liveness/ownership proof and protected removal; ambiguous access returns unavailable with no write.

| OS | Private request channel / peer verification | Passive older-instance detection |
|---|---|---|
| macOS | Short AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM path in a canonical current-UID-owned directory (0700), with owner/type/device/inode guards; both endpoints enforce kernel peer UID via getpeereid before any application bytes | Inspect `/tmp/com_pais_handy_si.sock` type/owner without connecting, reading a legacy frame, invoking callback or removing it. Reuse inspect_legacy_path and its Absent/Occupied/Unavailable results. Stale/uncertain legacy resources refuse mutation rather than authorize deletion |
| Linux | AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM under validated current-UID-owned directory (0700), XDG_RUNTIME_DIR or short private fallback, with owner/type/device/inode guards; both endpoints enforce checked SO_PEERCRED UID before any application bytes | Query session DBus `com.pais.handy.SingleInstance` through NameHasOwner/GetNameOwner only; never own that name, serve ExecuteCallback or call it. Errors/unknown scope refuse mutation |
| Windows | Named pipe keyed by SID+store hash, protected current-logon-SID DACL, reject remote clients and verify client token | Query legacy `com.pais.handy-sim` mutex and `com.pais.handy-sic`/`com.pais.handy-siw` target without WM_COPYDATA. Never reserve the mutex or create a compatibility window/message loop. Missing/ambiguous ownership evidence refuses mutation |

Unix channel authorization uses the validated canonical current-UID directory with mode 0700 plus retained directory/socket owner, type, device/inode and single-link checks. Revalidate directory identity before/after bind and before accept/connect; refuse hostile aliases/replacements without touching substitutes. Bind without changing process-global umask, pathname chmod or a bootstrap-permission framework. Socket mode is diagnostic, not a portable security boundary. On macOS, ACLs can grant traversal/connection beyond ordinary mode bits, so mode 0700 alone is not exhaustive access proof: accepted clients and connected servers must each pass kernel-derived expected UID authentication before request parsing, response rendering or any application read/write. Failure closes/refuses the connection with no application bytes or store mutation; protocol UID/PID fields are never authorization evidence. Same-UID identity changes fail closed; no atomic pathname-race guarantee is claimed. Failed/closed socket names are retained rather than removed through a racy stat/check-then-unlink; Step 5 implements reviewed lease-proven reclamation so normal restart remains possible. Never delete the legacy singleton path.

**Informative:** Inspect [Linux unix(7)](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/unix.7.html) for pathname/socket permission portability and kernel SO_PEERCRED context; inspect [Apple getpeereid(3)](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/System/Conceptual/ManPages_iPhoneOS/man3/getpeereid.3.html) for both-side peer effective UID authentication. These references explain the mechanism; they add no external normative requirement or acceptance graph.

Inspect the locked [macOS plugin source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tauri-apps/plugins-workspace/single-instance-v2.4.0/plugins/single-instance/src/platform_impl/macos.rs), [Windows source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tauri-apps/plugins-workspace/single-instance-v2.4.0/plugins/single-instance/src/platform_impl/windows.rs) and [Linux source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tauri-apps/plugins-workspace/single-instance-v2.4.0/plugins/single-instance/src/platform_impl/linux.rs). Cargo.lock resolves 2.4.0; recalculate identities if that dependency changes. Legacy identities do not prove store identity, so refuse conservatively for a same-user legacy owner even with an apparently different store. Do not connect/send an empty command: macOS empty streams can invoke show-window. Detected old instance means unavailable/5 and byte-identical store/revision, for reads or writes that would otherwise go to it.

Minimal AC-005 scope: passive detection and refusal only. **No legacy invocation handoff, worker, spool, capture, acknowledgement, replay or recovery daemon is planned.** Offline CLI and new startup never impersonate an old singleton. Existing historical flags still use their current single-instance flow outside `settings`. Remove obsolete spike decoder/spool/reservation code and handoff tests during implementation, preserving the passive probe and reusable private-resource/peer-UID helpers. No code is removed by this planning command. Older versions do not participate in the new lock: a launch after the final passive probe is not claimed to be atomically fenced or delivered/replayed. This unsupported old-version race is documented; deterministic probes refuse an owner that appears before commit. Real older-binary race observations are pending release evidence, never a demand to recreate replay.

Requests to a running new app carry protocol version, user/store identity, opaque request ID, typed operation, expected revision and dry_run. Bound UTF-8 frames to 1 MiB, reject malformed/oversized input without raw dumps. Domain imports share this technical limit until their owner defines another. Requests contain no raw argv. Use a monotonic 5 s end-to-end response deadline, including lock/persistence/transport wait. Successful M1 reads finish within 2 s; timeout failures are measured separately. No offline fallback write or blind retry after submission/timeout; reread revision/value first. Late replies cannot resurrect an expired request.

", "start_line": 21, "end_line": 22, "start_byte": 906, "end_byte": 935}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md:L23-L58", "source": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 1 — Edit ordered microphone choices `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** add, remove and reorder microphone choices, **so that** each recording uses my preferred available device.

**Priority reason:** Device choice controls the core recording workflow.
**Independent test:** Configure two devices, move the second above the first, verify only the draft changed, activate Save, reload settings and inspect the committed order.

```gherkin
Feature: Ordered microphone preferences
  Scenario: Reorder available devices
    Given the configured order is USB headset then MacBook microphone
    When the user moves MacBook microphone above USB headset
    Then the draft order is MacBook microphone then USB headset
    And the persisted order remains USB headset then MacBook microphone before Save
    When the user activates Save and it succeeds
    Then the persisted order is MacBook microphone then USB headset
    And the next recording attempts MacBook microphone first
  Scenario: Invalid duplicate choice
    Given USB headset is already configured
    When the user adds USB headset again
    Then the duplicate is rejected with an actionable error
    And the saved order remains unchanged
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Edit draft priority list] --> B{Valid unique choices?}
  B -- No --> D[Show error and retain saved order]
  B -- Yes --> S{Save activated?}
  S -- No --> A
  S -- Yes --> C{Commit succeeds?}
  C -- No --> D
  C -- Yes --> E[Persist complete new order]
  E --> F[Next recording uses committed order]
```

", "start_line": 23, "end_line": 58, "start_byte": 935, "end_byte": 2486}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md:L59-L112", "source": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 2 — Record through availability fallback `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** see unavailable choices and record with the next usable microphone, **so that** disconnecting a preferred device does not destroy my preferences.

**Priority reason:** Fallback prevents loss of the core recording capability.
**Independent test:** Disconnect the first configured device, start a recording and compare the effective device with unchanged stored preferences.

```gherkin
Feature: Microphone availability fallback
  Scenario: First choice unavailable
    Given USB headset then MacBook microphone is configured
    And USB headset is disconnected while MacBook microphone is available
    When a recording starts
    Then MacBook microphone is opened
    And USB headset remains first in the configured list with an unavailable label
  Scenario: No configured device opens
    Given every configured microphone is unavailable or fails to open
    When a recording starts
    Then the system default is attempted after the configured choices
    And failure of that attempt reports a recording error without changing preferences
  Scenario: Reconnection restores priority
    Given the first configured microphone is unavailable for one recording
    When it reconnects before the next recording starts
    Then it is attempted before the lower priority microphones
  Scenario: Ambiguous name is skipped
    Given "USB headset" is configured first and two present devices are named "USB headset"
    When a recording starts
    Then "USB headset" counts as a failed attempt with reason ambiguous
    And the next configured choice is attempted
  Scenario: Always-on stream follows the priority
    Given always-on microphone mode is enabled and no recording is active
    When the user saves a new priority order
    Then the input stream reopens on the first usable choice of the new order
  Scenario: Device lost during a recording
    Given a recording is in progress on USB headset
    When USB headset disconnects
    Then the recording ends and the audio captured before the loss is transcribed
    And the user is told the recording was cut short
    And the configured list is unchanged
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Start recording with current configuration] --> B{Next configured choice exists?}
  B -- Yes --> C{Present and opens?}
  C -- Yes --> D[Record with effective device]
  C -- No --> B
  B -- No --> E{System default opens?}
  E -- Yes --> D
  E -- No --> F[Report recording error]
  D --> G[Retain configured priority]
  F --> G
```

", "start_line": 59, "end_line": 112, "start_byte": 2486, "end_byte": 5051}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md:L113-L154", "source": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 3 — Preserve clamshell and upgrade behavior `P1`

**As a** existing Handy user, **I want to** retain my current microphone and clamshell choices during upgrade, **so that** the new list respects existing intent.

**Priority reason:** Migration and clamshell behavior affect persisted configuration and shared runtime.
**Independent test:** Load a legacy settings fixture and exercise open-lid and closed-lid resolution.

```gherkin
Feature: Compatible microphone priority migration
  Scenario: Legacy selection migration
    Given the stored settings have selected_microphone equal to USB headset
    And no microphone priority setting exists
    When the settings load after upgrade
    Then USB headset becomes the sole configured priority entry
    And the clamshell microphone setting is unchanged
    And a second load preserves the same configuration
  Scenario: Closed lid override unavailable
    Given a clamshell override and an ordered priority list are configured
    And the lid is closed
    And the override cannot be opened
    When a recording starts
    Then the system default is attempted, as in the current behavior
    And neither the override nor the list is erased
  Scenario: Open lid does not prefer the override
    Given the lid is open or its state cannot be determined
    When a recording starts
    Then the normal configured priority list is used
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Load settings] --> B{Priority key absent?}
  B -- Yes --> C[Migrate legacy selection once]
  B -- No --> D[Retain existing priority]

**Criterion:** Whenever the input stream opens — at the start of a recording, or, in always-on microphone mode, when the stream opens at launch, after a committed priority change while no recording is active, or after a device loss — attempt configured devices in saved order and use the first device that is present, unambiguous and opens. ", "start_line": 425, "end_line": 429, "start_byte": 25882, "end_byte": 26490}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md:L430-L442", "source": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## Edge Cases

- Channel selection: the existing channel setting applies only when valid for the opened device; otherwise the device's default channel mapping is used and the setting is not changed.
- Legacy key: after migration `selected_microphone` stays stored unchanged (not read while the priority key exists) so a downgrade keeps the previous choice; the legacy set command is replaced by the priority operations.
- Reset: empties the draft normal list only; it requires Save and leaves clamshell unchanged.
- Empty normal list: use and show system default when the lid is open/unknown or no usable override applies; a confirmed closed lid still attempts the configured override first.
- All devices missing: retain configured entries and show the attempted default or recording error.
- Enumeration error: mark availability unknown and retain preferences; after the single fresh re-enumeration, configured entries count as failed attempts, the system default is attempted, and the enumeration warning is shown.
- Duplicate names: mark ambiguous; do not persist transient enumeration indices or select an arbitrary match.
- Concurrent reorder and start: capture one committed revision; edits affect the next session.
- Persistence failure: restore last committed settings and allow retry without erasing the migration source.
- Repeated device failures: bounded attempts terminate with an error; no unbounded stream reopen loop.

", "start_line": 104, "end_line": 140, "start_byte": 4806, "end_byte": 6435}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/002-word-replacements/spec.md:L141-L179", "source": ".specs/features/002-word-replacements/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 4 — Predictable application to recognized text `P1`

```gherkin

  Scenario: Case-insensitive match, replacement inserted as written
    Given the rule "cloud code" to "Claude Code" exists

  Scenario: Whole words only
    Given the rule "art" to "ART" exists
    When the recognized text is "smart art"

  Scenario: Longest rule wins on overlap
    Given the rules "Cloud" to "Claude" and "Cloud Code" to "Claude Code CLI" exist in that order
    When the recognized text is "cloud code and cloud"
    Then the output is "Claude Code CLI and Claude"
  Scenario: No chaining
    Given the rules "A1" to "B1" and "B1" to "C1" exist

    Then the output is "B1"
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Final recognized text] --> B[Scan left to right]
  B --> C{Rule matches here on word boundaries? longest first, then list order}
  C -- Yes --> D[Emit replacement as written; skip matched span]
  C -- No --> E[Emit current character]
  D --> F{End of text?}
  E --> F
  F -- No --> B
  F -- Yes --> G[Pass text to next pipeline step]
```

**Criterion:** A rule is valid when the trimmed recognized text has 1–100 characters, contains no line break, tab or `;`, and does not start with `#`; and the trimmed replacement has 1–500 characters and contains no line break or tab. ", "start_line": 223, "end_line": 227, "start_byte": 10500, "end_byte": 10859}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/002-word-replacements/spec.md:L228-L232", "source": ".specs/features/002-word-replacements/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### AC-004

**Criterion:** The exchange format is UTF-8 text with one rule per line. A line containing a tab splits on its first tab; otherwise it splits on its first `;`. Blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored. The first line that is neither blank nor a comment is ignored as a header when it equals (case-insensitively, after trimming) `texte_reconnu;remplacement` or `recognized;replacement`. Export writes the header `recognized;replacement`, then one `recognized;replacement` line per rule in list order; because AC-002 forbids tab, `;` and a leading `#` in recognized text and tab in replacements, every valid rule set round-trips. Replacement text may contain `;`. CSV quoting is not supported; spreadsheet copy and paste uses the tab separator.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Stories 2 and 3

", "start_line": 228, "end_line": 232, "start_byte": 10859, "end_byte": 11672}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/002-word-replacements/spec.md:L233-L237", "source": ".specs/features/002-word-replacements/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### AC-005

**Criterion:** Import accepts a file up to 1 MB in merge or replace mode. Merge updates the replacement of rules whose normalized key matches, keeps their position, and appends new rules in file order. Replace makes the file content the whole rule set in file order. Duplicate keys inside one file or block are errors. Import is atomic: on any error, unreadable file or persistence failure, saved rules are unchanged. Export then replace-import of the same file reproduces the same rules and order.
**Priority:** P2 | **Story:** Story 3

", "start_line": 233, "end_line": 237, "start_byte": 11672, "end_byte": 12222}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/002-word-replacements/spec.md:L238-L242", "source": ".specs/features/002-word-replacements/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### AC-006

**Criterion:** Matching is case-insensitive (Unicode case folding) and the replacement is inserted exactly as written. A match must start and end on word boundaries: the characters immediately before and after the match are not Unicode letters or digits, or are the text edges. On a side where the recognized text begins or ends with a CJK ideograph, kana or hangul character, no boundary check applies, because those scripts are written without spaces. A whitespace run inside the recognized text matches any non-empty whitespace run; other characters match literally. Punctuation adjacent to a match is kept.

", "start_line": 238, "end_line": 242, "start_byte": 12222, "end_byte": 12884}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/002-word-replacements/spec.md:L243-L247", "source": ".specs/features/002-word-replacements/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### AC-007

**Criterion:** Rules apply in one left-to-right pass over the final recognized text. At each position the rule with the longest normalized key wins; ties follow list order. A matched span is replaced and scanning continues after it; replacement output is never rescanned (no chaining). Rules apply after speech recognition, language detection and Chinese script conversion, and before the existing approximate custom-word correction, filler removal, normalization and AI post-processing. Approximate correction never alters a span produced by a replacement. The inserted text and the history text include the replacements. Rules committed from the UI or the CLI apply from the next dictation of the running app. An empty rule set leaves text unchanged.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 4

  Scenario: Paste several terms

  Scenario: Remove a term
    Given the vocabulary contains "OpenClaw"
    When the user removes "OpenClaw"
    Then the saved vocabulary no longer contains it

", "start_line": 21, "end_line": 22, "start_byte": 747, "end_byte": 776}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/004-multiple-dictation-shortcuts/spec.md:L23-L61", "source": ".specs/features/004-multiple-dictation-shortcuts/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 1 — Add a second shortcut for dictation `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** bind two or more key combinations to the dictation action, **so that** I can start dictation from the hand position that suits each keyboard or app.

**Priority reason:** This is the requested capability.
**Independent test:** Add a second shortcut to the dictation action, restart, then start and stop dictation with each shortcut in turn.

```gherkin
Feature: Several shortcuts for one action
  Scenario: Add an alternative shortcut
    Given the dictation action has the shortcut "option+space"
    When the user adds the shortcut "ctrl+option+d" to the same action
    Then the dictation action lists "option+space" and "ctrl+option+d"
    And pressing either shortcut starts a dictation
  Scenario: Remove an alternative shortcut
    Given the dictation action has two shortcuts
    When the user removes "ctrl+option+d"
    Then only "option+space" starts a dictation
  Scenario: The last shortcut cannot be removed
    Given the dictation action has one shortcut
    When the user inspects its remove control
    Then removal is unavailable with an explanation that each action keeps at least one shortcut
    And the user can still change or reset that shortcut
  Scenario: Fifth shortcut
    Given the dictation action has four shortcuts
    When the user inspects the add control
    Then adding is unavailable with an explanation of the four-shortcut limit
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Record a new key combination] --> B{Valid for the keyboard implementation?}
  B -- No --> C[Show validation error; keep saved shortcuts]
  B -- Yes --> D{Conflicts with another shortcut or the OS?}
  D -- Yes --> E[Show conflict naming the other action; keep saved shortcuts]
  D -- No --> F[Register and persist the added shortcut]
  F --> G[Every shortcut of the action triggers it]
```

", "start_line": 23, "end_line": 61, "start_byte": 776, "end_byte": 2660}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/004-multiple-dictation-shortcuts/spec.md:L62-L98", "source": ".specs/features/004-multiple-dictation-shortcuts/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 2 — Keep the existing activation behavior `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** have every shortcut follow my activation mode, **so that** toggle, push-to-talk and hold-or-toggle behave as before.

**Priority reason:** Breaking activation semantics would make dictation unreliable.
**Independent test:** For each activation mode, start with shortcut A and try to stop with shortcut A and with shortcut B of the same action.

```gherkin
Feature: Activation semantics with several shortcuts
  Scenario: Toggle mode
    Given the activation mode is toggle
    And the dictation action has shortcuts A and B
    When the user presses A to start and then presses B
    Then the dictation stops
  Scenario: Push-to-talk mode
    Given the activation mode is push-to-talk
    And the user holds A to record
    When the user presses and releases B during the recording
    Then the recording continues
    And it stops when A is released
  Scenario: Hold-or-toggle mode
    Given the activation mode is hold-or-toggle
    When the user taps A shorter than the hold threshold
    Then the dictation stays on until a shortcut of the action is pressed again
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Shortcut of the action pressed] --> B{Activation mode}
  B -- Toggle --> C{Session active?}
  C -- No --> D[Start session]
  C -- Yes --> E[Stop session]
  B -- Push-to-talk or held --> F{Session started by this shortcut?}
  F -- Yes --> G[Stop on its release]
  F -- No --> H[Ignore input while session active]
```

", "start_line": 62, "end_line": 98, "start_byte": 2660, "end_byte": 4173}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/004-multiple-dictation-shortcuts/spec.md:L99-L140", "source": ".specs/features/004-multiple-dictation-shortcuts/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 3 — Detect conflicts `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** be told when a combination is already used, **so that** one key press never triggers two actions.

**Priority reason:** Conflict detection is explicitly required.
**Independent test:** Try to add the cancel shortcut, the post-processing shortcut and an OS-reserved combination as dictation shortcuts.

```gherkin
Feature: Shortcut conflicts
  Scenario: Combination used by another action
    Given "option+shift+space" is the post-processing shortcut
    When the user adds "shift+option+space" to the dictation action
    Then the shortcut is rejected because it is already used by the post-processing action
    And the saved shortcuts are unchanged
  Scenario: Duplicate within the same action
    Given the dictation action has "option+space"
    When the user adds "option+space" again
    Then the shortcut is rejected as already assigned to this action
  Scenario: Combination unavailable from the OS
    Given another application already registered the combination globally
    When the user adds it
    Then registration fails with an explanation and nothing is saved
  Scenario: Modifier-only overlap
    Given the keyboard implementation allows modifier-only shortcuts
    And "option" is a dictation shortcut
    When the user adds "option+space" to another action
    Then the shortcut is rejected because pressing "option+space" would also trigger "option"
    And the saved shortcuts are unchanged
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Candidate combination] --> B[Normalize modifiers and key]
  B --> C{Equal to an existing shortcut?}
  C -- Yes --> D[Reject: name the owning action]
  C -- No --> E{Modifier-only overlap?}
  E -- Yes --> F[Reject: overlap would double trigger]
  E -- No --> G{OS registration succeeds?}
  G -- No --> H[Reject with OS reason]
  G -- Yes --> I[Persist]
```

", "start_line": 21, "end_line": 22, "start_byte": 954, "end_byte": 983}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/005-custom-ai-prompts/spec.md:L23-L63", "source": ".specs/features/005-custom-ai-prompts/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 1 — Manage a prompt library `P1`

", "start_line": 64, "end_line": 107, "start_byte": 2793, "end_byte": 4895}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/005-custom-ai-prompts/spec.md:L108-L141", "source": ".specs/features/005-custom-ai-prompts/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 3 — Configure local or remote AI per prompt `P1`

", "start_line": 108, "end_line": 141, "start_byte": 4895, "end_byte": 6529}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/005-custom-ai-prompts/spec.md:L142-L178", "source": ".specs/features/005-custom-ai-prompts/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 4 — Keep the transcript when processing fails `P1`

", "start_line": 381, "end_line": 385, "start_byte": 17860, "end_byte": 18115}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/008-settings-cli/plan.md:L102-L122", "source": ".specs/features/008-settings-cli/plan.md", "role": "plan", "text": "### Descriptors, output domain and contract rendering

Descriptor inventory covers every AppSettings field, with wire type, enum/range, mutable/read-only, secret/presence projection, owning domain, runtime effect and validator. Build a reviewed manifest plus an independent test inventory from serialized default settings and all UI adapters; a descriptor omission fails, not silently hides a setting. Existing scalar settings are generic-settable except internal fields (schema, revision, onboarding/migration markers, manager-only model state) and provider configuration, which remain read-only from CLI. API-key fields are secret and never generic-settable. Lists/maps return validation_failed naming their owning domain command, plus `not available in this build` when unregistered; include owning command even when unavailable to satisfy AC-002. Optional values have descriptor-defined null handling; non-null boolean accepts exactly true/false, numeric parses without overflow, enums use existing serde values, strings preserve bytes without trimming meaningful content.

Redact via explicit public projection, never AppSettings Serialize or Debug. `post_process_api_keys` becomes per-provider `{present:boolean}` only; nested/future secrets inherit the rule. All stdout, stderr, parse errors, IPC diagnostics and logs sanitize raw candidate values. Public errors use stable English text and object details, with field/issues where applicable; no OS trace, raw document or credential in details. Reject `paste_method=invalid_method` identically via UI and CLI rather than existing default-to-ctrl_v behavior. UI maps code+field to i18n keys, falling back to a translated generic error, not free-text parsing.

`output get [KEY]` and `output set KEY VALUE` delegate to the same descriptors for existing paste_method, clipboard_handling, auto_submit, auto_submit_key, paste_delay_ms, paste_delay_after_ms, reliable_paste, typing_tool, external_script_path and append_trailing_space. Existing enum values remain unchanged: ctrl_v/direct/none/shift_insert/ctrl_shift_v/external_script; dont_modify/copy_to_clipboard; enter/ctrl_enter/cmd_enter. When 007 ships, it extends the same output descriptor and validation path with paste_method=smart_paste on macOS (validation_failed outside macOS), using the existing commit_mutation service and Domain trait; 008 alone keeps the existing methods. Feature 007 owns the macOS migration/default and removal of the beta reliable_paste switch; the Windows reliable_paste switch/path and Linux methods stay unchanged. This is configuration, not insertion execution. Keep destination 006/009, insertion method and clipboard handling separate. The 007 outcome contract is: "insertion attempted, read observed", "not read", "permission missing", "typed", "clipboard handed over", "insertion failed". Only read observed and typed authorize automatic Enter in 009; not read, permission missing and insertion failed route to recovery in 010. Clipboard handed over is neither Enter nor verified insertion. Outcomes wait for the read/fallback decision and never claim text verified in a field. A committed output setting proves configuration only.

Domain trait registers command schema/help, file/`-` input, pure parsing/validation, preview, typed patch and export formatter. Valid dry-run loads latest revision, validates fully, emits preview/revision with exit 0, and does not persist or call effects. Invalid dry-run returns validation_failed/2 with issues, no success preview. `-` explicitly requests stdin, never prompts; non-UTF-8 text returns byte offset in details. Export `-` human mode is raw exchange content only; JSON is data.content. Fixture domain proves bulk merge/replace/atomic all-or-nothing and live-only unavailable behavior; it never appears in production help.

| Result | Exit |
|---|---|
| success | 0 |
| persistence_failed, internal_error | 1 |
| usage_error, validation_failed, shortcut_conflict, limit_exceeded | 2 |
| revision_conflict (`details.current_revision`) | 3 |
| not_found | 4 |
| unavailable (timeout: `details.outcome=unknown`) | 5 |

The enum+single renderer owns this mapping. Every JSON operation emits exactly one `{ok:true,revision:N,data:...}` or `{ok:false,error:{code,message,details:{...}}}` followed by newline; diagnostics go to stderr. No newly introduced HTTP endpoints: OpenAPI would misrepresent local IPC. Contract is the typed DTO/JSON-schema and command matrix in Step 2; no openapi.yaml generated.

", "start_line": 21, "end_line": 22, "start_byte": 906, "end_byte": 935}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md:L23-L58", "source": ".specs/features/001-microphone-priority/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 1 — Edit ordered microphone choices `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** add, remove and reorder microphone choices, **so that** each recording uses my preferred available device.

**Priority reason:** Device choice controls the core recording workflow.
**Independent test:** Configure two devices, move the second above the first, verify only the draft changed, activate Save, reload settings and inspect the committed order.

```gherkin
Feature: Ordered microphone preferences
  Scenario: Reorder available devices
    Given the configured order is USB headset then MacBook microphone
    When the user moves MacBook microphone above USB headset
    Then the draft order is MacBook microphone then USB headset
    And the persisted order remains USB headset then MacBook microphone before Save
    When the user activates Save and it succeeds
    Then the persisted order is MacBook microphone then USB headset
    And the next recording attempts MacBook microphone first
  Scenario: Invalid duplicate choice
    Given USB headset is already configured
    When the user adds USB headset again
    Then the duplicate is rejected with an actionable error
    And the saved order remains unchanged
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Edit draft priority list] --> B{Valid unique choices?}
  B -- No --> D[Show error and retain saved order]
  B -- Yes --> S{Save activated?}
  S -- No --> A
  S -- Yes --> C{Commit succeeds?}
  C -- No --> D
  C -- Yes --> E[Persist complete new order]
  E --> F[Next recording uses committed order]
```

**Criterion:** Whenever the input stream opens — at the start of a recording, or, in always-on microphone mode, when the stream opens at launch, after a committed priority change while no recording is active, or after a device loss — attempt configured devices in saved order and use the first device that is present, unambiguous and opens. - **Criticality:** High; **Blast radius:** Shared; **Primary risk:** Regression; **Confidence:** Medium for source understanding, Low for unexecuted runtime.

- **P0 gates/evidence:** Gherkin-derived resolver, migration and transaction tests; unavailable preference retention; clamshell regression fixtures; UI/CLI equivalence and stale revision tests; native disconnect/reconnect and restart evidence.
- **P1 gates/evidence:** Keyboard reorder/focus and text status checks; bounded enumeration/open attempts; i18next and strict generated bindings; settings UI visual gate.
- **Non-functional expectations:** Device enumeration and opening sit behind an injectable seam so disconnect/ambiguity tests are deterministic; never enumerate on the webview/main loop; bound attempts by configured length; serialize settings commits and recording boundaries; labels and recovery errors are translated; no audio, device names or credential payloads in debug output added by this feature.
- **Missing evidence:** All application tests are PLANNED. No native Handy recording, build, migration or UI assertion has run for this feature. Draft UI contract, independent review, clarification, design and finalization gates remain open until their receipts exist.
- **Boundary:** QE defines risk/test sufficiency. Independent review judges requirements. Penflow governs UI source/design evidence. spec-test executes runtime proof; broader security audit is separate.

**Criterion:** A rule is valid when the trimmed recognized text has 1–100 characters, contains no line break, tab or `;`, and does not start with `#`; and the trimmed replacement has 1–500 characters and contains no line break or tab. **Criterion:** The exchange format is UTF-8 text with one rule per line. A line containing a tab splits on its first tab; otherwise it splits on its first `;`. Blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored. The first line that is neither blank nor a comment is ignored as a header when it equals (case-insensitively, after trimming) `texte_reconnu;remplacement` or `recognized;replacement`. Export writes the header `recognized;replacement`, then one `recognized;replacement` line per rule in list order; because AC-002 forbids tab, `;` and a leading `#` in recognized text and tab in replacements, every valid rule set round-trips. Replacement text may contain `;`. CSV quoting is not supported; spreadsheet copy and paste uses the tab separator.

**Criterion:** Matching is case-insensitive (Unicode case folding) and the replacement is inserted exactly as written. A match must start and end on word boundaries: the characters immediately before and after the match are not Unicode letters or digits, or are the text edges. On a side where the recognized text begins or ends with a CJK ideograph, kana or hangul character, no boundary check applies, because those scripts are written without spaces. **Criterion:** Rules apply in one left-to-right pass over the final recognized text. At each position the rule with the longest normalized key wins; ties follow list order. Rules apply after speech recognition, language detection and Chinese script conversion, and before the existing approximate custom-word correction, filler removal, normalization and AI post-processing. Rules committed from the UI or the CLI apply from the next dictation of the running app. An empty rule set leaves text unchanged.

", "start_line": 21, "end_line": 22, "start_byte": 803, "end_byte": 832}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/003-recognition-vocabulary/spec.md:L23-L57", "source": ".specs/features/003-recognition-vocabulary/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 1 — Maintain the vocabulary list `P1`

", "start_line": 23, "end_line": 57, "start_byte": 832, "end_byte": 2329}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/003-recognition-vocabulary/spec.md:L58-L105", "source": ".specs/features/003-recognition-vocabulary/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 2 — See whether the vocabulary is effective `P1`

    And batch transcription is used

", "start_line": 21, "end_line": 22, "start_byte": 747, "end_byte": 776}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/004-multiple-dictation-shortcuts/spec.md:L23-L61", "source": ".specs/features/004-multiple-dictation-shortcuts/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 1 — Add a second shortcut for dictation `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** bind two or more key combinations to the dictation action, **so that** I can start dictation from the hand position that suits each keyboard or app.

**Priority reason:** This is the requested capability.
**Independent test:** Add a second shortcut to the dictation action, restart, then start and stop dictation with each shortcut in turn.

```gherkin
Feature: Several shortcuts for one action
  Scenario: Add an alternative shortcut
    Given the dictation action has the shortcut "option+space"
    When the user adds the shortcut "ctrl+option+d" to the same action
    Then the dictation action lists "option+space" and "ctrl+option+d"
    And pressing either shortcut starts a dictation
  Scenario: Remove an alternative shortcut
    Given the dictation action has two shortcuts
    When the user removes "ctrl+option+d"
    Then only "option+space" starts a dictation
  Scenario: The last shortcut cannot be removed
    Given the dictation action has one shortcut
    When the user inspects its remove control
    Then removal is unavailable with an explanation that each action keeps at least one shortcut
    And the user can still change or reset that shortcut
  Scenario: Fifth shortcut
    Given the dictation action has four shortcuts
    When the user inspects the add control
    Then adding is unavailable with an explanation of the four-shortcut limit
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Record a new key combination] --> B{Valid for the keyboard implementation?}
  B -- No --> C[Show validation error; keep saved shortcuts]
  B -- Yes --> D{Conflicts with another shortcut or the OS?}
  D -- Yes --> E[Show conflict naming the other action; keep saved shortcuts]
  D -- No --> F[Register and persist the added shortcut]
  F --> G[Every shortcut of the action triggers it]
```

", "start_line": 23, "end_line": 61, "start_byte": 776, "end_byte": 2660}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/004-multiple-dictation-shortcuts/spec.md:L62-L98", "source": ".specs/features/004-multiple-dictation-shortcuts/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 2 — Keep the existing activation behavior `P1`

```gherkin
Feature: Activation semantics with several shortcuts
  Scenario: Toggle mode
    Given the activation mode is toggle
    And the dictation action has shortcuts A and B

    Then the dictation stops
  Scenario: Push-to-talk mode
    Given the activation mode is push-to-talk

    When the user presses and releases B during the recording
    Then the recording continues

    When the user taps A shorter than the hold threshold
    Then the dictation stays on until a shortcut of the action is pressed again

  B -- Toggle --> C{Session active?}
  C -- No --> D[Start session]

", "start_line": 62, "end_line": 98, "start_byte": 2660, "end_byte": 4173}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/004-multiple-dictation-shortcuts/spec.md:L99-L140", "source": ".specs/features/004-multiple-dictation-shortcuts/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 3 — Detect conflicts `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** be told when a combination is already used, **so that** one key press never triggers two actions.

**Priority reason:** Conflict detection is explicitly required.
**Independent test:** Try to add the cancel shortcut, the post-processing shortcut and an OS-reserved combination as dictation shortcuts.

```gherkin
Feature: Shortcut conflicts
  Scenario: Combination used by another action
    Given "option+shift+space" is the post-processing shortcut
    When the user adds "shift+option+space" to the dictation action
    Then the shortcut is rejected because it is already used by the post-processing action
    And the saved shortcuts are unchanged
  Scenario: Duplicate within the same action
    Given the dictation action has "option+space"
    When the user adds "option+space" again
    Then the shortcut is rejected as already assigned to this action
  Scenario: Combination unavailable from the OS
    Given another application already registered the combination globally
    When the user adds it
    Then registration fails with an explanation and nothing is saved
  Scenario: Modifier-only overlap
    Given the keyboard implementation allows modifier-only shortcuts
    And "option" is a dictation shortcut
    When the user adds "option+space" to another action
    Then the shortcut is rejected because pressing "option+space" would also trigger "option"
    And the saved shortcuts are unchanged
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Candidate combination] --> B[Normalize modifiers and key]
  B --> C{Equal to an existing shortcut?}
  C -- Yes --> D[Reject: name the owning action]
  C -- No --> E{Modifier-only overlap?}
  E -- Yes --> F[Reject: overlap would double trigger]
  E -- No --> G{OS registration succeeds?}
  G -- No --> H[Reject with OS reason]
  G -- Yes --> I[Persist]
```

", "start_line": 64, "end_line": 107, "start_byte": 2793, "end_byte": 4895}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/005-custom-ai-prompts/spec.md:L108-L141", "source": ".specs/features/005-custom-ai-prompts/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 3 — Configure local or remote AI per prompt `P1`
