", "start_line": 21, "end_line": 22, "start_byte": 2026, "end_byte": 2055}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md:L23-L67", "source": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 1 — Paste without losing my clipboard `P1`

**As a** Handy user on macOS, **I want to** have the transcript pasted while my clipboard comes back intact, **so that** dictating never destroys what I had copied.

**Priority reason:** Clipboard loss is the main cost of clipboard-based insertion.
**Independent test:** Copy rich content (text with formatting and an image), dictate into TextEdit, and compare the clipboard before and after.

```gherkin
Feature: Smart paste restores the previous clipboard
  Scenario: Restore after the target reads the transcript
    Given the clipboard holds rich text and an image
    And the paste method is smart paste and the clipboard paste is used
    When a dictation produces "hello world" and TextEdit reads the clipboard after the paste keystroke
    Then TextEdit receives "hello world"
    And 300 ms after the last read the clipboard holds the same rich text and image as before
  Scenario: Probe then read
    Given a Chromium-based target reads the clipboard twice, 150 ms apart, after the paste keystroke
    When smart paste waits for restoration
    Then restoration happens 300 ms after the second read, not after the first
  Scenario: No read never restores the previous content
    Given the paste method is smart paste and the clipboard paste is used
    When the target never reads the clipboard within 800 ms after the paste keystroke
    Then the previous clipboard content is not restored
    And the transcript stays on the clipboard
    And the insertion outcome is "not read"
  Scenario: Empty clipboard before
    Given the clipboard was empty before the dictation
    When the restoration runs
    Then the clipboard is empty again
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Transcript ready, destination frontmost] --> B[Save every item and type of the clipboard]
  B --> C[Prepare clipboard: current host only, transient marker]
  C --> D[Publish transcript as on-demand item]
  D --> E[Send paste keystroke]
  E --> F{Read observed after keystroke within 800 ms?}
  F -- Yes --> G[Wait until 300 ms without any new read]
  F -- No --> H[Outcome: not read; transcript stays; never restore]
  G --> I{changeCount unchanged since publication?}
  I -- Yes --> J[Restore saved content or clear]
  I -- No --> K[Leave the newer content]
```

", "start_line": 23, "end_line": 67, "start_byte": 2055, "end_byte": 4358}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md:L68-L95", "source": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 2 — Never overwrite a newer copy `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** keep anything copied after the dictation started pasting, **so that** restoration never erases my own work.

**Priority reason:** Overwriting a fresh copy is unrecoverable data loss.
**Independent test:** Make the target delay its read, copy something else before restoration, and check the clipboard afterwards.

```gherkin
Feature: changeCount guard
  Scenario: User copies before restoration
    Given smart paste published the transcript
    When the user copies "new text" before the restoration runs
    Then the restoration is abandoned
    And the clipboard still holds "new text"
  Scenario: Another application writes the clipboard
    Given smart paste published the transcript
    When another application writes an image before the restoration runs
    Then the image stays on the clipboard
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Restoration due] --> B[Read current changeCount]
  B --> C{Equal to the count recorded at publication?}
  C -- No --> D[Abandon restoration]
  C -- Yes --> E[Restore saved content]
```

", "start_line": 68, "end_line": 95, "start_byte": 4358, "end_byte": 5467}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md:L96-L141", "source": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 3 — Adapt to the application and the keyboard `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** have smart paste choose a strategy that works in the frontmost application and with my keyboard layout, **so that** paste works in remote-desktop apps and with non-US layouts.

**Priority reason:** A wrong strategy types garbage or pastes nothing in these environments.
**Independent test:** Dictate with an AZERTY layout into TextEdit, into Screen Sharing, into iPhone Mirroring and into Jump Desktop when available, and check the text and the restored layout.

```gherkin

  Scenario: Keyboard layout other than ABC or US

    And the previous layout is restored 100 ms after the keystroke
  Scenario: Input method active
    Given the current input source is an input method such as Japanese Kana
    When smart paste sends the paste keystroke
    Then the input source is not changed
  Scenario: iPhone Mirroring or Windows App
    Given the destination is iPhone Mirroring or Windows App
    When smart paste inserts the transcript
    Then the transcript is typed as Unicode key events without using the clipboard
  Scenario: Screen Sharing
    Given the destination is Screen Sharing

  Scenario: Jump Desktop timings
    Given the destination is Jump Desktop
    When smart paste publishes the transcript
    Then restoration waits for 1.5 s without any new read after the last read
    And without any read within 3 s the outcome is "not read" and nothing is restored
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Destination application] --> B{Application}
  B -- iPhone Mirroring or Windows App --> C[Unicode typing; no clipboard]
  B -- Screen Sharing --> D[Clipboard write for remote side; no keystroke]
  B -- Jump Desktop --> E[Clipboard paste; 1.5 s / 3 s timings]

", "start_line": 96, "end_line": 141, "start_byte": 5467, "end_byte": 7879}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md:L142-L176", "source": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 4 — Report honest outcomes `P1`

**Independent test:** Paste into a field, into a window without a text field, and with accessibility permission revoked; inspect outcomes, Enter and recovery.

  Scenario: Read observed
    Given the target read the transcript after the paste keystroke
    When smart paste completes

    When smart paste completes
    Then the outcome is "not read" and the recovery bubble (010) is offered as for an insertion failure
    And the previous clipboard content is not restored
    And no automatic Enter is sent
  Scenario: Accessibility permission missing
    Given Handy lacks accessibility permission
    When smart paste would send the paste keystroke
    Then no keystroke is sent and the outcome is "permission missing"
    And the transcript is kept for recovery
```

", "start_line": 142, "end_line": 176, "start_byte": 7879, "end_byte": 9489}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md:L177-L201", "source": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 5 — Choose smart paste in settings and CLI `P2`

**Criterion:** With smart paste on macOS, before writing, Handy saves every pasteboard item with all its types as data; it then prepares the general pasteboard for current-host-only content, adds the `org.nspasteboard.TransientType` marker, and publishes the transcript as an item whose plain-text data is provided on demand. Waiting and posting the chord never block the serving of pasteboard reads. The existing delay before the keystroke (`paste_delay_ms`) still applies, the fixed delay after it (`paste_delay_after_ms`) is replaced by smart paste timings, and the V key is resolved after any layout switch of AC-011 for the layout then active. **Criterion:** Restoration requires a read observed after the paste keystroke. ", "start_line": 390, "end_line": 406, "start_byte": 25284, "end_byte": 28444}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md:L407-L416", "source": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## QE Analysis

- **P0 gates/evidence:** Fake-pasteboard tests for multi-type save/restore, first-read once, pre-keystroke reads ignored, 300/800 ms and 1.5/3 s timings, `changeCount` guard; strategy table tests by bundle identifier; input-source tests (layout vs input method, ABC then US fallback, restoration); outcome mapping tests feeding 009 and 010; migration tests from reliable paste.

- **Missing evidence:** All runtime evidence; mockup of the paste method selector deferred before `spec-ship`.
- **Boundary:** QE defines risk and test sufficiency; the independent review judges requirements; Penflow governs UI design evidence; spec-test executes runtime proof.

", "start_line": 423, "end_line": 426, "start_byte": 30171, "end_byte": 30574}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md:L427-L435", "source": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## Edge Cases

- Application reads the pasteboard several times (probe then read): each read restarts the 300 ms quiet delay; all requests are served with the transcript.
- Handy quits or crashes while its on-demand item is on the pasteboard: before a normal exit Handy writes the transcript as plain data if no restoration is due; after a crash the item can no longer be served and the history keeps the transcript.
- Pasteboard content that cannot be read as data (promised by another app and failing): that type is skipped and listed in the debug log by type name only; the other types are restored.
- Layout switch fails: Cmd+V is sent with the current source, and the outcome still depends on the read.
- Second dictation before the first restoration: no intermediate restoration happens; if `changeCount` is unchanged since the first publication, the first snapshot stays the content to restore after the second dictation, otherwise the current content is saved as the new snapshot.

**Criterion:** Settings carry a persisted revision number returned by every read and incremented by 1 on every committed write from any surface, including writes made by Handy itself; a write that changes nothing and a read do not increment it. Writes accept `--expected-revision N`; a mismatch returns `revision_conflict` with the current revision in `error.details.current_revision` and writes nothing. All writers (UI commands, a running instance and a headless CLI process) are serialized by one cross-process settings lock, and each writer re-reads the stored settings under that lock before applying its change, so a write without expected revision applies to the latest settings and never discards fields changed by another writer.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 3

**Criterion:** When a Handy instance of the same user and settings store is running, the CLI sends the operation to it over a local channel accessible only to that user and waits up to 5 seconds for its answer; the instance applies it with its live state, re-registers affected shortcuts and notifies its UI. If no answer arrives in time, the CLI returns `unavailable` with `error.details.outcome` set to `unknown`, and agents must read again before retrying. If a running Handy without this channel (an older version) is detected, the CLI returns `unavailable` and never writes the store itself. When none is running, the CLI applies the operation to the settings store itself under the same lock and validation. Operations that need live state (for example the current destination) return `unavailable` without a running instance. No network listener and no MCP server are introduced.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Stories 2, 3 and 5

", "start_line": 21, "end_line": 22, "start_byte": 918, "end_byte": 947}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/009-pin-mode-and-enter-rule/spec.md:L23-L62", "source": ".specs/features/009-pin-mode-and-enter-rule/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 1 — Pin a destination from the badge `P1`

", "start_line": 91, "end_line": 136, "start_byte": 3681, "end_byte": 5460}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/008-settings-cli/plan.md:L102-L122", "source": ".specs/features/008-settings-cli/plan.md", "role": "plan", "text": "### Descriptors, output domain and contract rendering

Descriptor inventory covers every AppSettings field, with wire type, enum/range, mutable/read-only, secret/presence projection, owning domain, runtime effect and validator. Build a reviewed manifest plus an independent test inventory from serialized default settings and all UI adapters; a descriptor omission fails, not silently hides a setting. Existing scalar settings are generic-settable except internal fields (schema, revision, onboarding/migration markers, manager-only model state) and provider configuration, which remain read-only from CLI. API-key fields are secret and never generic-settable. Lists/maps return validation_failed naming their owning domain command, plus `not available in this build` when unregistered; include owning command even when unavailable to satisfy AC-002. Optional values have descriptor-defined null handling; non-null boolean accepts exactly true/false, numeric parses without overflow, enums use existing serde values, strings preserve bytes without trimming meaningful content.

Redact via explicit public projection, never AppSettings Serialize or Debug. `post_process_api_keys` becomes per-provider `{present:boolean}` only; nested/future secrets inherit the rule. All stdout, stderr, parse errors, IPC diagnostics and logs sanitize raw candidate values. Public errors use stable English text and object details, with field/issues where applicable; no OS trace, raw document or credential in details. Reject `paste_method=invalid_method` identically via UI and CLI rather than existing default-to-ctrl_v behavior. UI maps code+field to i18n keys, falling back to a translated generic error, not free-text parsing.

`output get [KEY]` and `output set KEY VALUE` delegate to the same descriptors for existing paste_method, clipboard_handling, auto_submit, auto_submit_key, paste_delay_ms, paste_delay_after_ms, reliable_paste, typing_tool, external_script_path and append_trailing_space. Existing enum values remain unchanged: ctrl_v/direct/none/shift_insert/ctrl_shift_v/external_script; dont_modify/copy_to_clipboard; enter/ctrl_enter/cmd_enter. When 007 ships, it extends the same output descriptor and validation path with paste_method=smart_paste on macOS (validation_failed outside macOS), using the existing commit_mutation service and Domain trait; 008 alone keeps the existing methods. Feature 007 owns the macOS migration/default and removal of the beta reliable_paste switch; the Windows reliable_paste switch/path and Linux methods stay unchanged. This is configuration, not insertion execution. Keep destination 006/009, insertion method and clipboard handling separate. The 007 outcome contract is: "insertion attempted, read observed", "not read", "permission missing", "typed", "clipboard handed over", "insertion failed". Only read observed and typed authorize automatic Enter in 009; not read, permission missing and insertion failed route to recovery in 010. Clipboard handed over is neither Enter nor verified insertion. Outcomes wait for the read/fallback decision and never claim text verified in a field. A committed output setting proves configuration only.

Domain trait registers command schema/help, file/`-` input, pure parsing/validation, preview, typed patch and export formatter. Valid dry-run loads latest revision, validates fully, emits preview/revision with exit 0, and does not persist or call effects. Invalid dry-run returns validation_failed/2 with issues, no success preview. `-` explicitly requests stdin, never prompts; non-UTF-8 text returns byte offset in details. Export `-` human mode is raw exchange content only; JSON is data.content. Fixture domain proves bulk merge/replace/atomic all-or-nothing and live-only unavailable behavior; it never appears in production help.

| Result | Exit |
|---|---|
| success | 0 |
| persistence_failed, internal_error | 1 |
| usage_error, validation_failed, shortcut_conflict, limit_exceeded | 2 |
| revision_conflict (`details.current_revision`) | 3 |
| not_found | 4 |
| unavailable (timeout: `details.outcome=unknown`) | 5 |

The enum+single renderer owns this mapping. Every JSON operation emits exactly one `{ok:true,revision:N,data:...}` or `{ok:false,error:{code,message,details:{...}}}` followed by newline; diagnostics go to stderr. No newly introduced HTTP endpoints: OpenAPI would misrepresent local IPC. Contract is the typed DTO/JSON-schema and command matrix in Step 2; no openapi.yaml generated.

- **Missing evidence:** No runtime test; starter prompt texts to be written in the plan; mockups deferred before `spec-ship`.
- **Boundary:** QE defines risk and test sufficiency; the independent review judges requirements; Penflow governs UI design evidence; spec-test executes runtime proof; a security audit of credential storage is separate.

", "start_line": 21, "end_line": 22, "start_byte": 1186, "end_byte": 1215}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/006-destination-application/spec.md:L23-L61", "source": ".specs/features/006-destination-application/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 1 — Insert into the application where dictation started `P1`

**Independent test:** Start a dictation in a text editor, switch to a browser during the recording, stop, and check where the text lands.

```gherkin

  Scenario: Switch app during recording
    Given TextEdit is the frontmost application
    When the user starts a dictation, switches to Safari, and stops the dictation
    Then Handy activates TextEdit before inserting
    And the text is inserted into TextEdit with the configured insertion method
  Scenario: No switch
    Given ChatGPT is the frontmost application
    When the user dictates without switching
    Then the text is inserted into ChatGPT as today
  Scenario: Handy itself is frontmost at start
    Given the Handy settings window is frontmost
    When the user starts a dictation
    Then no destination is captured
    And the text is inserted into whichever application is frontmost at the end, as today
```

", "start_line": 94, "end_line": 133, "start_byte": 4105, "end_byte": 5932}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/006-destination-application/spec.md:L134-L174", "source": ".specs/features/006-destination-application/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 4 — Preserve the transcript when the destination is unavailable `P1`

", "start_line": 21, "end_line": 22, "start_byte": 2026, "end_byte": 2055}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md:L23-L67", "source": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 1 — Paste without losing my clipboard `P1`

**As a** Handy user on macOS, **I want to** have the transcript pasted while my clipboard comes back intact, **so that** dictating never destroys what I had copied.

**Priority reason:** Clipboard loss is the main cost of clipboard-based insertion.
**Independent test:** Copy rich content (text with formatting and an image), dictate into TextEdit, and compare the clipboard before and after.

```gherkin
Feature: Smart paste restores the previous clipboard
  Scenario: Restore after the target reads the transcript
    Given the clipboard holds rich text and an image
    And the paste method is smart paste and the clipboard paste is used
    When a dictation produces "hello world" and TextEdit reads the clipboard after the paste keystroke
    Then TextEdit receives "hello world"
    And 300 ms after the last read the clipboard holds the same rich text and image as before
  Scenario: Probe then read
    Given a Chromium-based target reads the clipboard twice, 150 ms apart, after the paste keystroke
    When smart paste waits for restoration
    Then restoration happens 300 ms after the second read, not after the first
  Scenario: No read never restores the previous content
    Given the paste method is smart paste and the clipboard paste is used
    When the target never reads the clipboard within 800 ms after the paste keystroke
    Then the previous clipboard content is not restored
    And the transcript stays on the clipboard
    And the insertion outcome is "not read"
  Scenario: Empty clipboard before

    When the restoration runs
    Then the clipboard is empty again
```

**Criterion:** With smart paste on macOS, before writing, Handy saves every pasteboard item with all its types as data; it then prepares the general pasteboard for current-host-only content, adds the `org.nspasteboard.TransientType` marker, and publishes the transcript as an item whose plain-text data is provided on demand. The data provider supplies the full transcript on every request and reports the first request after the paste keystroke exactly once. Requests before the keystroke are served but do not count as the first read. The keystroke instant is recorded immediately before the first key-down of the Cmd+V chord is posted, as in the current reliable paste; reads served while the chord is held count. Waiting and posting the chord never block the serving of pasteboard reads. The existing delay before the keystroke (`paste_delay_ms`) still applies, the fixed delay after it (`paste_delay_after_ms`) is replaced by smart paste timings, and the V key is resolved after any layout switch of AC-011 for the layout then active. Saving the previous content is bounded to 200 ms and 50 MB; a type that cannot be saved within those bounds is skipped, and "exactly" in AC-009 applies to the saved types.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 1

**Criterion:** Smart paste reports one outcome per dictation: "insertion attempted, read observed" when a read followed the keystroke; "not read" when none did; "permission missing" when accessibility permission is absent (checked before the clipboard is touched, so no keystroke is sent and the clipboard is unchanged); "typed" for Unicode typing; "clipboard handed over" for Screen Sharing, shown on the indicator as "Text placed on the clipboard for the remote screen"; "insertion failed" when posting the chord or the Unicode key events fails, or the transaction cannot start. Direct insertion adds "inserted, verified" and "uncertain" (AC-017). Only "inserted, verified", "insertion attempted, read observed" and "typed" count as a successful insertion for automatic Enter (009). "Not read", "permission missing", "uncertain" and "insertion failed" are handled as an insertion failure by the recovery bubble (010). The outcome is known only after the read or the 800 ms decision delay; automatic Enter and recovery wait for it. "Clipboard handed over" is neither a success for automatic Enter nor a failure for recovery. Only "inserted, verified" states that the field contains the text, because the field was read back; every other outcome makes no claim about the field content. If a read arrives after "not read" was declared, the transcript (still on the clipboard) is served, the outcome stays "not read" for automatic Enter, and the recovery bubble states that the text may have been pasted after all.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 4

", "start_line": 380, "end_line": 389, "start_byte": 24549, "end_byte": 25284}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md:L390-L406", "source": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## Clarifications

- Decision 2026-10-12 (Julien, relayed by Codex): item 7 is now smart paste. The clipboard recovery window (10–15 s) is retired from the active program and is neither planned nor implemented for now; its earlier spec and plan are kept under `superseded/` for history. Requirement IDs of the retired scope (AC-001–AC-007, FR-001–FR-004, SC-001–SC-003) are not reused.
- Evidence basis: static analysis of Spokenly 2.30.9 (`.investigations/spokenly-smart-paste-2026-10-09/rapport.md`). The 300 ms delay, Jump Desktop timings and the 100 ms layout restoration come from that version; real insertion and compatibility are unverified until AC-016.
- Decision 2026-10-13 (Julien): Spokenly's restoration 800 ms after the keystroke without any read is not adopted, because a slow target could then paste the previous clipboard or an earlier transcript. 800 ms now only decides the outcome "not read"; quiet is measured after the last read (Chromium probes then reads), as in the current reliable paste.
- Decision 2026-10-13 (Julien): direct accessibility insertion is tried first and verified by reading the field back; this replaces the earlier wording that kept `AXSelectedText` as a separate method only.
- Current code (2026-10-12): the beta "reliable paste" on macOS already publishes a lazy promise, counts reads only after the paste keystroke, guards on `changeCount`, marks transient/concealed types and restores after a 200 ms quiet period with an 8 s timeout, but saves text only; the classic path restores after a fixed 60 ms without guard. Smart paste replaces the macOS reliable paste path.
- `[ASSUMED]` Reads before the paste keystroke (clipboard managers) do not count as the first read, as in the current reliable paste.
- Decision 2026-10-13 (Julien): smart paste becomes the macOS default and absorbs the Cmd+V users; users who chose another method keep it; Windows keeps its reliable paste; Screen Sharing does not restore the previous clipboard.
- `[ASSUMED]` Screen Sharing: the transcript stays on the clipboard for the remote side, since no local paste occurs; Spokenly's specific focus path for Screen Sharing is not reproduced.
- Residual limitation: an application that reads again more than 300 ms after its last read (or after the 8 s cap) receives the restored content; without any read the previous content is never restored. Native checks (AC-016) measure this with the chosen delays.
- Known limitation: with Screen Sharing the previous clipboard is not restored, because the transcript is handed to the remote side.
- To verify natively: whether AppKit calls the data provider again after a clipboard manager read it before the keystroke; a missing second call would produce a false "not read".
- Destination and PIN (006, 009) act before smart paste; direct accessibility insertion is the first step of smart paste (AC-017).
- Read attribution: each dictation publishes its own on-demand item; reads served for an item of an earlier dictation never start or delay the restoration of the current one.
- Program context: specified in list order (001–010); the settings CLI foundation (008) ships first.

", "start_line": 390, "end_line": 406, "start_byte": 25284, "end_byte": 28444}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md:L407-L416", "source": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## QE Analysis

- **Criticality:** High; **Blast radius:** Every macOS paste and the user's clipboard; **Primary risk:** Clipboard loss or wrong-layout keystrokes; **Confidence:** Medium for mechanism (static evidence plus existing reliable paste), low for application compatibility.
- **Dimensions:** Data integrity, functional correctness, compatibility (applications, layouts, input methods), concurrency/timing, permissions, privacy (transient and current-host-only marking), regression.
- **P0 gates/evidence:** Fake-pasteboard tests for multi-type save/restore, first-read once, pre-keystroke reads ignored, 300/800 ms and 1.5/3 s timings, `changeCount` guard; strategy table tests by bundle identifier; input-source tests (layout vs input method, ABC then US fallback, restoration); outcome mapping tests feeding 009 and 010; migration tests from reliable paste.
- **P1 gates/evidence:** AC-016 native checks per application and layout; clipboard-history manager check for the transient marker; CLI and UI selector checks.
- **Non-functional expectations:** Restoration within 50 ms of its deadline; no transcript, clipboard content or field value read through accessibility logged at any level; input source always restored even when the paste fails.
- **Missing evidence:** All runtime evidence; mockup of the paste method selector deferred before `spec-ship`.
- **Boundary:** QE defines risk and test sufficiency; the independent review judges requirements; Penflow governs UI design evidence; spec-test executes runtime proof.

", "start_line": 423, "end_line": 426, "start_byte": 30171, "end_byte": 30574}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md:L427-L435", "source": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## Edge Cases

- Application reads the pasteboard several times (probe then read): each read restarts the 300 ms quiet delay; all requests are served with the transcript.
- Handy quits or crashes while its on-demand item is on the pasteboard: before a normal exit Handy writes the transcript as plain data if no restoration is due; after a crash the item can no longer be served and the history keeps the transcript.
- Pasteboard content that cannot be read as data (promised by another app and failing): that type is skipped and listed in the debug log by type name only; the other types are restored.
- Layout switch fails: Cmd+V is sent with the current source, and the outcome still depends on the read.
- Second dictation before the first restoration: no intermediate restoration happens; if `changeCount` is unchanged since the first publication, the first snapshot stays the content to restore after the second dictation, otherwise the current content is saved as the new snapshot.
- Handy quits before restoration: the pending restoration runs before exit only when a read was observed and `changeCount` is unchanged; otherwise the transcript stays.

", "start_line": 59, "end_line": 93, "start_byte": 2505, "end_byte": 4013}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/008-settings-cli/spec.md:L94-L129", "source": ".specs/features/008-settings-cli/spec.md", "role": "spec", "text": "### Story 3 — Safe concurrent changes `P1`

```gherkin

  Scenario: Stale expected revision
    Given the CLI read revision 41
    And the UI committed a change producing revision 42
    When the CLI writes with "--expected-revision 41"
    Then the exit code is 3 with code "revision_conflict" and the current revision 42
    And nothing is written
  Scenario: Write without expected revision
    When the CLI writes one setting without an expected revision
    Then the write applies to the latest settings without discarding other fields changed meanwhile
  Scenario: Concurrent writers
    Given the UI and the CLI commit different settings at the same moment
    When both commits finish
    Then both changes are stored and the revision increased by 2
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Write request] --> B[Take settings write lock]
  B --> C{Expected revision given?}
  C -- No --> E[Apply to latest settings]
  C -- Yes --> D{Equals current revision?}
  D -- No --> F[revision_conflict; release lock]
  D -- Yes --> E
  E --> G[Persist atomically; revision plus 1]
  G --> H[Release lock; notify]
```

**Criterion:** Settings carry a persisted revision number returned by every read and incremented by 1 on every committed write from any surface, including writes made by Handy itself; a write that changes nothing and a read do not increment it. Writes accept `--expected-revision N`; a mismatch returns `revision_conflict` with the current revision in `error.details.current_revision` and writes nothing. All writers (UI commands, a running instance and a headless CLI process) are serialized by one cross-process settings lock, and each writer re-reads the stored settings under that lock before applying its change, so a write without expected revision applies to the latest settings and never discards fields changed by another writer.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 3

If a running Handy without this channel (an older version) is detected, the CLI returns `unavailable` and never writes the store itself. When none is running, the CLI applies the operation to the settings store itself under the same lock and validation. Operations that need live state (for example the current destination) return `unavailable` without a running instance. No network listener and no MCP server are introduced.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Stories 2, 3 and 5

- Non-UTF-8 stdin for a text import: `validation_failed` with the offending byte offset.

  participant IPC as Private channel
  participant Service as Live commit worker

    Service->>Native: prepare reversible effects

    Service->>Native: apply and confirm
    Service->>UI: settings-changed revision and keys
    Service-->>CLI: success envelope
  else no-op
    Service-->>CLI: current revision unchanged

    And a warning goes only to stderr when recovery was needed
  Scenario: Startup competes with offline write

    When both acquire shared ownership and transaction guards
    Then the write is visible at startup or routed to the new instance
    And each changed transaction increments revision exactly once

    When the CLI requests a mutation

", "start_line": 123, "end_line": 210, "start_byte": 22248, "end_byte": 25519}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/008-settings-cli/plan.md:L211-L248", "source": ".specs/features/008-settings-cli/plan.md", "role": "plan", "text": "## State Model

```gherkin
Feature: Mutation outcome
  Scenario: Refusal or no-op
    Given a current durable revision
    When validation fails or expected revision is stale
    Then the durable state and revision remain unchanged
    When a valid patch changes nothing
    Then success carries the unchanged revision
  Scenario: Failure after durable commit
    When persistence commits but a live effect fails
    Then the revision remains committed and error details state outcome committed
    And the affected runtime state is reconciled before another affected mutation
  Scenario: Timeout at the caller
    When the deadline expires after submission
    Then the caller reports outcome unknown until a fresh read resolves it
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Parsed
  Parsed --> Refused: invalid usage or unavailable owner
  Parsed --> Locked: owner established
  Locked --> Refused: validation or revision conflict
  Locked --> NoOp: same normalized value or dry-run
  Locked --> Prepared: valid changed patch
  Prepared --> Refused: prepare or persistence fails, compensate
  Prepared --> Durable: atomic replace succeeded
  Durable --> Applied: native effects and event complete
  Durable --> Reconcile: effect failure, outcome committed
  Applied --> [*]: success
  Reconcile --> Applied: repair live state
  Refused --> [*]: error, disk unchanged
  NoOp --> [*]: success, revision unchanged
  note right of Durable: Client timeout is an unknown observation, not rollback
```

", "start_line": 21, "end_line": 22, "start_byte": 2026, "end_byte": 2055}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md:L23-L67", "source": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 1 — Paste without losing my clipboard `P1`

**As a** Handy user on macOS, **I want to** have the transcript pasted while my clipboard comes back intact, **so that** dictating never destroys what I had copied.

**Priority reason:** Clipboard loss is the main cost of clipboard-based insertion.
**Independent test:** Copy rich content (text with formatting and an image), dictate into TextEdit, and compare the clipboard before and after.

```gherkin
Feature: Smart paste restores the previous clipboard
  Scenario: Restore after the target reads the transcript
    Given the clipboard holds rich text and an image
    And the paste method is smart paste and the clipboard paste is used
    When a dictation produces "hello world" and TextEdit reads the clipboard after the paste keystroke
    Then TextEdit receives "hello world"
    And 300 ms after the last read the clipboard holds the same rich text and image as before
  Scenario: Probe then read
    Given a Chromium-based target reads the clipboard twice, 150 ms apart, after the paste keystroke
    When smart paste waits for restoration
    Then restoration happens 300 ms after the second read, not after the first
  Scenario: No read never restores the previous content
    Given the paste method is smart paste and the clipboard paste is used
    When the target never reads the clipboard within 800 ms after the paste keystroke
    Then the previous clipboard content is not restored
    And the transcript stays on the clipboard
    And the insertion outcome is "not read"
  Scenario: Empty clipboard before
    Given the clipboard was empty before the dictation
    When the restoration runs
    Then the clipboard is empty again
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Transcript ready, destination frontmost] --> B[Save every item and type of the clipboard]
  B --> C[Prepare clipboard: current host only, transient marker]
  C --> D[Publish transcript as on-demand item]
  D --> E[Send paste keystroke]
  E --> F{Read observed after keystroke within 800 ms?}
  F -- Yes --> G[Wait until 300 ms without any new read]
  F -- No --> H[Outcome: not read; transcript stays; never restore]
  G --> I{changeCount unchanged since publication?}
  I -- Yes --> J[Restore saved content or clear]
  I -- No --> K[Leave the newer content]
```

  B --> C{Equal to the count recorded at publication?}
  C -- No --> D[Abandon restoration]

", "start_line": 246, "end_line": 249, "start_byte": 12696, "end_byte": 12835}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md:L250-L254", "source": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### AC-008

**Criterion:** With smart paste on macOS, before writing, Handy saves every pasteboard item with all its types as data; it then prepares the general pasteboard for current-host-only content, adds the `org.nspasteboard.TransientType` marker, and publishes the transcript as an item whose plain-text data is provided on demand. The data provider supplies the full transcript on every request and reports the first request after the paste keystroke exactly once. Requests before the keystroke are served but do not count as the first read. The keystroke instant is recorded immediately before the first key-down of the Cmd+V chord is posted, as in the current reliable paste; reads served while the chord is held count. Waiting and posting the chord never block the serving of pasteboard reads. The existing delay before the keystroke (`paste_delay_ms`) still applies, the fixed delay after it (`paste_delay_after_ms`) is replaced by smart paste timings, and the V key is resolved after any layout switch of AC-011 for the layout then active. Saving the previous content is bounded to 200 ms and 50 MB; a type that cannot be saved within those bounds is skipped, and "exactly" in AC-009 applies to the saved types.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 1

**Criterion:** Restoration requires a read observed after the paste keystroke. It runs once no new read has occurred for 300 ms after the last read, and at the latest 8 s after the first read if reads keep coming (for Jump Desktop, `com.p5sys.jump.mac.viewer`: 1.5 s of quiet). When no read is observed within 800 ms after the keystroke (3 s for Jump Desktop), the outcome is "not read", the saved snapshot is discarded and the previous content is never restored for that dictation: the transcript stays on the clipboard until the user or another application replaces it. A restoration puts back the saved items and types exactly, or clears the pasteboard if it was empty, only when the pasteboard `changeCount` still equals the value recorded at publication; otherwise it does nothing.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Stories 1 and 2

The accessibility permission check applies to the strategies that post key events (clipboard paste and Unicode typing). **Criterion:** Smart paste reports one outcome per dictation: "insertion attempted, read observed" when a read followed the keystroke; "not read" when none did; "permission missing" when accessibility permission is absent (checked before the clipboard is touched, so no keystroke is sent and the clipboard is unchanged); "typed" for Unicode typing; "clipboard handed over" for Screen Sharing, shown on the indicator as "Text placed on the clipboard for the remote screen"; "insertion failed" when posting the chord or the Unicode key events fails, or the transaction cannot start. Direct insertion adds "inserted, verified" and "uncertain" (AC-017). Only "inserted, verified", "insertion attempted, read observed" and "typed" count as a successful insertion for automatic Enter (009). "Not read", "permission missing", "uncertain" and "insertion failed" are handled as an insertion failure by the recovery bubble (010). The outcome is known only after the read or the 800 ms decision delay; automatic Enter and recovery wait for it. "Clipboard handed over" is neither a success for automatic Enter nor a failure for recovery. Only "inserted, verified" states that the field contains the text, because the field was read back; every other outcome makes no claim about the field content. If a read arrives after "not read" was declared, the transcript (still on the clipboard) is served, the outcome stays "not read" for automatic Enter, and the recovery bubble states that the text may have been pasted after all.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 4

- Decision 2026-10-12 (Julien, relayed by Codex): item 7 is now smart paste. The clipboard recovery window (10–15 s) is retired from the active program and is neither planned nor implemented for now; its earlier spec and plan are kept under `superseded/` for history. - Decision 2026-10-13 (Julien): Spokenly's restoration 800 ms after the keystroke without any read is not adopted, because a slow target could then paste the previous clipboard or an earlier transcript. 800 ms now only decides the outcome "not read"; quiet is measured after the last read (Chromium probes then reads), as in the current reliable paste.
- Decision 2026-10-13 (Julien): direct accessibility insertion is tried first and verified by reading the field back; this replaces the earlier wording that kept `AXSelectedText` as a separate method only.
- Current code (2026-10-12): the beta "reliable paste" on macOS already publishes a lazy promise, counts reads only after the paste keystroke, guards on `changeCount`, marks transient/concealed types and restores after a 200 ms quiet period with an 8 s timeout, but saves text only; the classic path restores after a fixed 60 ms without guard. Smart paste replaces the macOS reliable paste path.
- `[ASSUMED]` Reads before the paste keystroke (clipboard managers) do not count as the first read, as in the current reliable paste.
- Decision 2026-10-13 (Julien): smart paste becomes the macOS default and absorbs the Cmd+V users; users who chose another method keep it; Windows keeps its reliable paste; Screen Sharing does not restore the previous clipboard.
- `[ASSUMED]` Screen Sharing: the transcript stays on the clipboard for the remote side, since no local paste occurs; Spokenly's specific focus path for Screen Sharing is not reproduced.
- Residual limitation: an application that reads again more than 300 ms after its last read (or after the 8 s cap) receives the restored content; without any read the previous content is never restored. Native checks (AC-016) measure this with the chosen delays.
- Known limitation: with Screen Sharing the previous clipboard is not restored, because the transcript is handed to the remote side.
- To verify natively: whether AppKit calls the data provider again after a clipboard manager read it before the keystroke; a missing second call would produce a false "not read".
- Destination and PIN (006, 009) act before smart paste; direct accessibility insertion is the first step of smart paste (AC-017).
- Read attribution: each dictation publishes its own on-demand item; reads served for an item of an earlier dictation never start or delay the restoration of the current one.
- Program context: specified in list order (001–010); the settings CLI foundation (008) ships first.

", "start_line": 390, "end_line": 406, "start_byte": 25284, "end_byte": 28444}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md:L407-L416", "source": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## QE Analysis

- **Criticality:** High; **Blast radius:** Every macOS paste and the user's clipboard; **Primary risk:** Clipboard loss or wrong-layout keystrokes; **Confidence:** Medium for mechanism (static evidence plus existing reliable paste), low for application compatibility.
- **Dimensions:** Data integrity, functional correctness, compatibility (applications, layouts, input methods), concurrency/timing, permissions, privacy (transient and current-host-only marking), regression.
- **P0 gates/evidence:** Fake-pasteboard tests for multi-type save/restore, first-read once, pre-keystroke reads ignored, 300/800 ms and 1.5/3 s timings, `changeCount` guard; strategy table tests by bundle identifier; input-source tests (layout vs input method, ABC then US fallback, restoration); outcome mapping tests feeding 009 and 010; migration tests from reliable paste.
- **P1 gates/evidence:** AC-016 native checks per application and layout; clipboard-history manager check for the transient marker; CLI and UI selector checks.
- **Non-functional expectations:** Restoration within 50 ms of its deadline; no transcript, clipboard content or field value read through accessibility logged at any level; input source always restored even when the paste fails.
- **Missing evidence:** All runtime evidence; mockup of the paste method selector deferred before `spec-ship`.
- **Boundary:** QE defines risk and test sufficiency; the independent review judges requirements; Penflow governs UI design evidence; spec-test executes runtime proof.

", "start_line": 423, "end_line": 426, "start_byte": 30171, "end_byte": 30574}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md:L427-L435", "source": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## Edge Cases

- Application reads the pasteboard several times (probe then read): each read restarts the 300 ms quiet delay; all requests are served with the transcript.
- Handy quits or crashes while its on-demand item is on the pasteboard: before a normal exit Handy writes the transcript as plain data if no restoration is due; after a crash the item can no longer be served and the history keeps the transcript.
- Pasteboard content that cannot be read as data (promised by another app and failing): that type is skipped and listed in the debug log by type name only; the other types are restored.
- Layout switch fails: Cmd+V is sent with the current source, and the outcome still depends on the read.
- Second dictation before the first restoration: no intermediate restoration happens; if `changeCount` is unchanged since the first publication, the first snapshot stays the content to restore after the second dictation, otherwise the current content is saved as the new snapshot.
- Handy quits before restoration: the pending restoration runs before exit only when a read was observed and `changeCount` is unchanged; otherwise the transcript stays.

  Scenario: Read all settings

  Scenario: Discover settings
    When the user runs "handy settings keys --json"

  Scenario: Secrets are never output

    Then the exit code is 3 with code "revision_conflict" and the current revision 42
    And nothing is written
  Scenario: Write without expected revision
    When the CLI writes one setting without an expected revision
    Then the write applies to the latest settings without discarding other fields changed meanwhile
  Scenario: Concurrent writers
    Given the UI and the CLI commit different settings at the same moment
    When both commits finish
    Then both changes are stored and the revision increased by 2
```

```mermaid

  A[Write request] --> B[Take settings write lock]
  B --> C{Expected revision given?}
  C -- No --> E[Apply to latest settings]
  C -- Yes --> D{Equals current revision?}
  D -- No --> F[revision_conflict; release lock]

```

**Criterion:** Settings carry a persisted revision number returned by every read and incremented by 1 on every committed write from any surface, including writes made by Handy itself; a write that changes nothing and a read do not increment it. Writes accept `--expected-revision N`; a mismatch returns `revision_conflict` with the current revision in `error.details.current_revision` and writes nothing. All writers (UI commands, a running instance and a headless CLI process) are serialized by one cross-process settings lock, and each writer re-reads the stored settings under that lock before applying its change, so a write without expected revision applies to the latest settings and never discards fields changed by another writer.

", "start_line": 287, "end_line": 297, "start_byte": 15729, "end_byte": 17709}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/008-settings-cli/spec.md:L298-L307", "source": ".specs/features/008-settings-cli/spec.md", "role": "spec", "text": "## QE Analysis

- **Criticality:** High; **Blast radius:** All persisted settings and every program feature; **Primary risk:** Lost updates, divergent validation and secret leakage; **Confidence:** Medium (CLI and settings code mapped, nothing executed).
- **Dimensions:** API/contract compatibility, data integrity, concurrency, security (local channel, secrets), backward compatibility of existing flags, operability for agents.
- **P0 gates/evidence:** Contract tests for envelope, error codes and exit codes; UI/CLI validation parity tests per setting; concurrency tests with two writers and stale revision; routing tests with and without a running instance; secret redaction tests.
- **P1 gates/evidence:** Regression tests of existing flags; no window/tray/model on `handy settings`; read latency measurement; help text snapshot.
- **Non-functional expectations:** Reads within 2 seconds, instance answers within 5 seconds; local channel restricted to the current user; no setting values logged above debug level and secrets never logged.
- **Missing evidence:** No runtime test; the local channel mechanism per platform is chosen in the plan.
- **Boundary:** QE defines risk and test sufficiency; the independent review judges requirements; spec-test executes runtime proof; a security audit of the local channel is separate.

- Running instance hangs: the CLI times out after 5 seconds with `unavailable` and does not write the store itself, to avoid a conflicting writer.
- Settings store missing: reads return defaults with revision 0; the first write creates the store.
- Corrupted store: the existing salvage logic applies; the CLI reports a warning on stderr.
- Two CLI invocations at once without a running app: the write lock serializes them.
- Non-UTF-8 stdin for a text import: `validation_failed` with the offending byte offset.

", "start_line": 21, "end_line": 22, "start_byte": 918, "end_byte": 947}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/009-pin-mode-and-enter-rule/spec.md:L23-L62", "source": ".specs/features/009-pin-mode-and-enter-rule/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 1 — Pin a destination from the badge `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** pin the destination application from the badge, **so that** all my next dictations go there while I read or work elsewhere.

**Priority reason:** Pinning is the core of this item.
**Independent test:** Pin ChatGPT during a dictation, then dictate three times from other applications and check where each text lands.

```gherkin
Feature: Pin a destination
  Scenario: Pin from the badge
    Given a dictation is recording with destination ChatGPT
    When the user opens the badge menu and chooses "Pin ChatGPT"
    Then the badge shows ChatGPT with a pin mark
    And this dictation and the following ones are sent to ChatGPT
  Scenario: Pinned across app switches and new dictations
    Given ChatGPT is pinned
    When the user starts a dictation while Safari is frontmost
    Then the destination of this dictation is ChatGPT
    And at the end Handy activates ChatGPT and inserts the text there
  Scenario: Unpin
    Given ChatGPT is pinned
    When the user chooses "Unpin" in the badge menu
    Then the pin mark disappears
    And the next dictation captures the frontmost application again
```

flowchart TD

  B -- Yes --> C[Destination: pinned app]
  B -- No --> D[Destination: captured frontmost app as in 006]
  C --> E[Badge with pin mark]
  D --> F[Badge without pin mark]
  E --> G{User action in badge menu}
  F --> G
  G -- Pin current destination --> H[Pin stored; applies now and next dictations]
  G -- Unpin --> I[Pin cleared; next dictations capture frontmost]
  G -- Other app --> J[This dictation only; pin unchanged]
```

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** choose Never, Always or Only in PIN mode for automatic Enter, **so that** messages are sent automatically only where I want.

**Independent test:** For each value, dictate once pinned and once not pinned, and count Enter presses received by a test field.

```gherkin

  Scenario: Only in PIN mode, pinned
    Given automatic Enter is "Only in PIN mode"
    And ChatGPT is pinned
    When a dictation is inserted into ChatGPT successfully
    Then exactly one Enter key press is sent after the insertion
  Scenario: Only in PIN mode, not pinned
    Given automatic Enter is "Only in PIN mode"
    And nothing is pinned
    When a dictation is inserted successfully
    Then no Enter key press is sent
  Scenario: Always
    Given automatic Enter is "Always"
    When a dictation is inserted successfully
    Then exactly one Enter key press is sent
  Scenario: Never
    Given automatic Enter is "Never"
    When a dictation is inserted successfully
    Then no Enter key press is sent
  Scenario: Upgrade from the existing auto-submit
    Given the existing auto-submit was on with key Ctrl+Enter
    When settings load after upgrade
    Then automatic Enter is "Always" with key Ctrl+Enter
    And no other auto-submit control remains in the settings
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Insertion outcome] --> B{Insertion attempted successfully?}
  B -- No --> C[No Enter]
  B -- Yes --> D{Option}
  D -- Never --> C
  D -- Always --> E[Send one Enter]
  D -- Only in PIN mode --> F{Destination came from the pin?}
  F -- Yes --> E
  F -- No --> C
```

", "start_line": 21, "end_line": 22, "start_byte": 1186, "end_byte": 1215}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/006-destination-application/spec.md:L23-L61", "source": ".specs/features/006-destination-application/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 1 — Insert into the application where dictation started `P1`

", "start_line": 94, "end_line": 133, "start_byte": 4105, "end_byte": 5932}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/006-destination-application/spec.md:L134-L174", "source": ".specs/features/006-destination-application/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 4 — Preserve the transcript when the destination is unavailable `P1`

**As a** Handy user on macOS, **I want to** have the transcript pasted while my clipboard comes back intact, **so that** dictating never destroys what I had copied.

**Priority reason:** Clipboard loss is the main cost of clipboard-based insertion.
**Independent test:** Copy rich content (text with formatting and an image), dictate into TextEdit, and compare the clipboard before and after.

```gherkin
Feature: Smart paste restores the previous clipboard
  Scenario: Restore after the target reads the transcript
    Given the clipboard holds rich text and an image
    And the paste method is smart paste and the clipboard paste is used

    Then TextEdit receives "hello world"
    And 300 ms after the last read the clipboard holds the same rich text and image as before
  Scenario: Probe then read
    Given a Chromium-based target reads the clipboard twice, 150 ms apart, after the paste keystroke
    When smart paste waits for restoration
    Then restoration happens 300 ms after the second read, not after the first
  Scenario: No read never restores the previous content
    Given the paste method is smart paste and the clipboard paste is used
    When the target never reads the clipboard within 800 ms after the paste keystroke
    Then the previous clipboard content is not restored
    And the transcript stays on the clipboard
    And the insertion outcome is "not read"
  Scenario: Empty clipboard before

    When the restoration runs
    Then the clipboard is empty again
```

**Criterion:** With smart paste on macOS, before writing, Handy saves every pasteboard item with all its types as data; it then prepares the general pasteboard for current-host-only content, adds the `org.nspasteboard.TransientType` marker, and publishes the transcript as an item whose plain-text data is provided on demand. The data provider supplies the full transcript on every request and reports the first request after the paste keystroke exactly once. Requests before the keystroke are served but do not count as the first read. The keystroke instant is recorded immediately before the first key-down of the Cmd+V chord is posted, as in the current reliable paste; reads served while the chord is held count. Waiting and posting the chord never block the serving of pasteboard reads. The existing delay before the keystroke (`paste_delay_ms`) still applies, the fixed delay after it (`paste_delay_after_ms`) is replaced by smart paste timings, and the V key is resolved after any layout switch of AC-011 for the layout then active. Saving the previous content is bounded to 200 ms and 50 MB; a type that cannot be saved within those bounds is skipped, and "exactly" in AC-009 applies to the saved types.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 1

**Criterion:** Restoration requires a read observed after the paste keystroke. It runs once no new read has occurred for 300 ms after the last read, and at the latest 8 s after the first read if reads keep coming (for Jump Desktop, `com.p5sys.jump.mac.viewer`: 1.5 s of quiet). When no read is observed within 800 ms after the keystroke (3 s for Jump Desktop), the outcome is "not read", the saved snapshot is discarded and the previous content is never restored for that dictation: the transcript stays on the clipboard until the user or another application replaces it. A restoration puts back the saved items and types exactly, or clears the pasteboard if it was empty, only when the pasteboard `changeCount` still equals the value recorded at publication; otherwise it does nothing.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Stories 1 and 2

The accessibility permission check applies to the strategies that post key events (clipboard paste and Unicode typing). With clipboard handling "copy to clipboard", Unicode typing also leaves the transcript on the clipboard.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 3

**Criterion:** For the clipboard paste, when the current input source is a keyboard layout other than ABC or US, Handy selects `com.apple.keylayout.ABC`, or `com.apple.keylayout.US` when ABC cannot be selected, waits 50 ms for the switch to apply, sends Cmd+V, and restores the previous input source 100 ms after the last key of the chord is released. ", "start_line": 265, "end_line": 269, "start_byte": 15688, "end_byte": 16215}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md:L270-L274", "source": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### AC-012

**Criterion:** Smart paste reports one outcome per dictation: "insertion attempted, read observed" when a read followed the keystroke; "not read" when none did; "permission missing" when accessibility permission is absent (checked before the clipboard is touched, so no keystroke is sent and the clipboard is unchanged); "typed" for Unicode typing; "clipboard handed over" for Screen Sharing, shown on the indicator as "Text placed on the clipboard for the remote screen"; "insertion failed" when posting the chord or the Unicode key events fails, or the transaction cannot start. Direct insertion adds "inserted, verified" and "uncertain" (AC-017). Only "inserted, verified", "insertion attempted, read observed" and "typed" count as a successful insertion for automatic Enter (009). "Not read", "permission missing", "uncertain" and "insertion failed" are handled as an insertion failure by the recovery bubble (010). The outcome is known only after the read or the 800 ms decision delay; automatic Enter and recovery wait for it. "Clipboard handed over" is neither a success for automatic Enter nor a failure for recovery. Only "inserted, verified" states that the field contains the text, because the field was read back; every other outcome makes no claim about the field content. If a read arrives after "not read" was declared, the transcript (still on the clipboard) is served, the outcome stays "not read" for automatic Enter, and the recovery bubble states that the text may have been pasted after all.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 4

- Decision 2026-10-12 (Julien, relayed by Codex): item 7 is now smart paste. The clipboard recovery window (10–15 s) is retired from the active program and is neither planned nor implemented for now; its earlier spec and plan are kept under `superseded/` for history. - Decision 2026-10-13 (Julien): Spokenly's restoration 800 ms after the keystroke without any read is not adopted, because a slow target could then paste the previous clipboard or an earlier transcript. 800 ms now only decides the outcome "not read"; quiet is measured after the last read (Chromium probes then reads), as in the current reliable paste.
- Decision 2026-10-13 (Julien): direct accessibility insertion is tried first and verified by reading the field back; this replaces the earlier wording that kept `AXSelectedText` as a separate method only.
- Current code (2026-10-12): the beta "reliable paste" on macOS already publishes a lazy promise, counts reads only after the paste keystroke, guards on `changeCount`, marks transient/concealed types and restores after a 200 ms quiet period with an 8 s timeout, but saves text only; the classic path restores after a fixed 60 ms without guard. Smart paste replaces the macOS reliable paste path.
- `[ASSUMED]` Reads before the paste keystroke (clipboard managers) do not count as the first read, as in the current reliable paste.
- Decision 2026-10-13 (Julien): smart paste becomes the macOS default and absorbs the Cmd+V users; users who chose another method keep it; Windows keeps its reliable paste; Screen Sharing does not restore the previous clipboard.
- `[ASSUMED]` Screen Sharing: the transcript stays on the clipboard for the remote side, since no local paste occurs; Spokenly's specific focus path for Screen Sharing is not reproduced.
- Residual limitation: an application that reads again more than 300 ms after its last read (or after the 8 s cap) receives the restored content; without any read the previous content is never restored. Native checks (AC-016) measure this with the chosen delays.
- Known limitation: with Screen Sharing the previous clipboard is not restored, because the transcript is handed to the remote side.
- To verify natively: whether AppKit calls the data provider again after a clipboard manager read it before the keystroke; a missing second call would produce a false "not read".
- Destination and PIN (006, 009) act before smart paste; direct accessibility insertion is the first step of smart paste (AC-017).
- Read attribution: each dictation publishes its own on-demand item; reads served for an item of an earlier dictation never start or delay the restoration of the current one.
- Program context: specified in list order (001–010); the settings CLI foundation (008) ships first.

", "start_line": 390, "end_line": 406, "start_byte": 25284, "end_byte": 28444}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md:L407-L416", "source": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## QE Analysis

- **Criticality:** High; **Blast radius:** Every macOS paste and the user's clipboard; **Primary risk:** Clipboard loss or wrong-layout keystrokes; **Confidence:** Medium for mechanism (static evidence plus existing reliable paste), low for application compatibility.
- **Dimensions:** Data integrity, functional correctness, compatibility (applications, layouts, input methods), concurrency/timing, permissions, privacy (transient and current-host-only marking), regression.
- **P0 gates/evidence:** Fake-pasteboard tests for multi-type save/restore, first-read once, pre-keystroke reads ignored, 300/800 ms and 1.5/3 s timings, `changeCount` guard; strategy table tests by bundle identifier; input-source tests (layout vs input method, ABC then US fallback, restoration); outcome mapping tests feeding 009 and 010; migration tests from reliable paste.
- **P1 gates/evidence:** AC-016 native checks per application and layout; clipboard-history manager check for the transient marker; CLI and UI selector checks.
- **Non-functional expectations:** Restoration within 50 ms of its deadline; no transcript, clipboard content or field value read through accessibility logged at any level; input source always restored even when the paste fails.
- **Missing evidence:** All runtime evidence; mockup of the paste method selector deferred before `spec-ship`.
- **Boundary:** QE defines risk and test sufficiency; the independent review judges requirements; Penflow governs UI design evidence; spec-test executes runtime proof.

", "start_line": 423, "end_line": 426, "start_byte": 30171, "end_byte": 30574}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md:L427-L435", "source": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## Edge Cases

- Application reads the pasteboard several times (probe then read): each read restarts the 300 ms quiet delay; all requests are served with the transcript.
- Handy quits or crashes while its on-demand item is on the pasteboard: before a normal exit Handy writes the transcript as plain data if no restoration is due; after a crash the item can no longer be served and the history keeps the transcript.
- Pasteboard content that cannot be read as data (promised by another app and failing): that type is skipped and listed in the debug log by type name only; the other types are restored.
- Layout switch fails: Cmd+V is sent with the current source, and the outcome still depends on the read.
- Second dictation before the first restoration: no intermediate restoration happens; if `changeCount` is unchanged since the first publication, the first snapshot stays the content to restore after the second dictation, otherwise the current content is saved as the new snapshot.
- Handy quits before restoration: the pending restoration runs before exit only when a read was observed and `changeCount` is unchanged; otherwise the transcript stays.

", "start_line": 21, "end_line": 22, "start_byte": 934, "end_byte": 963}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/008-settings-cli/spec.md:L23-L58", "source": ".specs/features/008-settings-cli/spec.md", "role": "spec", "text": "### Story 1 — Read settings as JSON `P1`

**As an** automation user or agent, **I want to** read Handy's persistent settings as JSON, **so that** I can inspect configuration reliably from scripts.

**Priority reason:** Reading is the first capability every agent workflow needs.
**Independent test:** Run the read operations with and without a running Handy instance on an isolated store and parse stdout with a JSON parser.

```gherkin
Feature: Read settings
  Scenario: Read all settings
    When the user runs "handy settings get --json"
    Then stdout is one JSON envelope with ok true, the settings revision and every non-secret setting
    And the exit code is 0
  Scenario: Read one setting
    When the user runs "handy settings get paste_method --json"
    Then the envelope data contains only paste_method and its value
  Scenario: Discover settings
    When the user runs "handy settings keys --json"
    Then the envelope lists each settable key with its type, allowed values or range, and whether it is read-only
  Scenario: Secrets are never output
    Given a provider API key is stored
    When the user reads all settings
    Then the key value appears nowhere in stdout or stderr
    And the provider entry reports only that a key is present
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[handy settings get] --> B{Running Handy instance?}
  B -- Yes --> C[Instance answers from its live settings]
  B -- No --> D[CLI reads the store headlessly]
  C --> E[Redact secrets]
  D --> E
  E --> F[Print envelope with revision; exit 0]
```

", "start_line": 23, "end_line": 58, "start_byte": 963, "end_byte": 2505}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/008-settings-cli/spec.md:L59-L93", "source": ".specs/features/008-settings-cli/spec.md", "role": "spec", "text": "### Story 2 — Change settings with the same validation as the UI `P1`

**As an** automation user, **I want to** change settings from the CLI and be refused exactly when the UI would refuse, **so that** scripts cannot create a configuration the app rejects.

**Priority reason:** Shared validation is an explicit requirement and protects every feature of the program.
**Independent test:** Apply the same valid and invalid values through UI commands and CLI and compare stored results and error reasons.

```gherkin
Feature: Write settings
  Scenario: Valid scalar change
    When the user runs "handy settings set paste_method ctrl_v --json"
    Then the setting is stored, the revision increases by 1
    And the envelope reports the new value and revision
  Scenario: Invalid value
    When the user runs "handy settings set paste_delay_ms -5 --json"
    Then the exit code is 2
    And the envelope has ok false, code "validation_failed" and the same reason the UI shows
    And no setting changes
  Scenario: Running app reflects the change
    Given Handy is running with its settings open
    When a CLI write commits
    Then the settings UI shows the new value without restart
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[CLI write] --> B[Parse arguments]
  B --> C{Usage valid?}
  C -- No --> D[usage_error; exit 2]
  C -- Yes --> E[Shared validation used by UI]
  E --> F{Valid?}
  F -- No --> G[validation_failed; exit 2; nothing written]
  F -- Yes --> H[Atomic commit; revision plus 1; change event]
```

", "start_line": 59, "end_line": 93, "start_byte": 2505, "end_byte": 4013}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/008-settings-cli/spec.md:L94-L129", "source": ".specs/features/008-settings-cli/spec.md", "role": "spec", "text": "### Story 3 — Safe concurrent changes `P1`

**As an** automation user, **I want to** detect that settings changed since I read them, **so that** my script never silently overwrites someone else's change.

**Priority reason:** UI and CLI can write at the same time; lost updates would corrupt list settings such as replacements.
**Independent test:** Read the revision, change a setting in the UI, then write from the CLI with the old expected revision.

```gherkin
Feature: Revision checks
  Scenario: Stale expected revision
    Given the CLI read revision 41
    And the UI committed a change producing revision 42
    When the CLI writes with "--expected-revision 41"
    Then the exit code is 3 with code "revision_conflict" and the current revision 42
    And nothing is written
  Scenario: Write without expected revision
    When the CLI writes one setting without an expected revision
    Then the write applies to the latest settings without discarding other fields changed meanwhile
  Scenario: Concurrent writers
    Given the UI and the CLI commit different settings at the same moment
    When both commits finish
    Then both changes are stored and the revision increased by 2
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Write request] --> B[Take settings write lock]
  B --> C{Expected revision given?}
  C -- No --> E[Apply to latest settings]
  C -- Yes --> D{Equals current revision?}
  D -- No --> F[revision_conflict; release lock]
  D -- Yes --> E
  E --> G[Persist atomically; revision plus 1]
  G --> H[Release lock; notify]
```

", "start_line": 206, "end_line": 210, "start_byte": 8542, "end_byte": 9320}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/008-settings-cli/spec.md:L211-L215", "source": ".specs/features/008-settings-cli/spec.md", "role": "spec", "text": "### AC-002

**Criterion:** `handy settings get [KEY]` returns all non-secret settings or one key; `handy settings keys` lists settable keys with type, allowed values or range and read-only flag; `handy settings set KEY VALUE` changes one scalar setting. Secret values (API keys) are never printed; reads report only their presence. Unknown keys return `not_found`. `set` parses VALUE with the key's descriptor type (boolean `true`/`false`, integer, enumeration value, string). Generic `set` on a list key returns `validation_failed` naming the domain command to use; on a secret or read-only key it returns `validation_failed` stating that the key is changed in the settings UI. A top-level `--json` before `settings` is accepted as equivalent to `--json` after it. A headless read never creates the settings store.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Stories 1 and 2

**Criterion:** Every write goes through the same backend validation functions as the corresponding UI command, so a value the UI rejects is rejected by the CLI with the same error code and English message, and vice versa; the UI may show that message translated. **Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 2

", "start_line": 216, "end_line": 220, "start_byte": 10183, "end_byte": 10649}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/008-settings-cli/spec.md:L221-L225", "source": ".specs/features/008-settings-cli/spec.md", "role": "spec", "text": "### AC-004

**Criterion:** Settings carry a persisted revision number returned by every read and incremented by 1 on every committed write from any surface, including writes made by Handy itself; a write that changes nothing and a read do not increment it. Writes accept `--expected-revision N`; a mismatch returns `revision_conflict` with the current revision in `error.details.current_revision` and writes nothing. All writers (UI commands, a running instance and a headless CLI process) are serialized by one cross-process settings lock, and each writer re-reads the stored settings under that lock before applying its change, so a write without expected revision applies to the latest settings and never discards fields changed by another writer.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 3

**Criterion:** When a Handy instance of the same user and settings store is running, the CLI sends the operation to it over a local channel accessible only to that user and waits up to 5 seconds for its answer; the instance applies it with its live state, re-registers affected shortcuts and notifies its UI. If no answer arrives in time, the CLI returns `unavailable` with `error.details.outcome` set to `unknown`, and agents must read again before retrying. If a running Handy without this channel (an older version) is detected, the CLI returns `unavailable` and never writes the store itself. When none is running, the CLI applies the operation to the settings store itself under the same lock and validation. Operations that need live state (for example the current destination) return `unavailable` without a running instance. No network listener and no MCP server are introduced.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Stories 2, 3 and 5

- **Criticality:** High; **Blast radius:** All persisted settings and every program feature; **Primary risk:** Lost updates, divergent validation and secret leakage; **Confidence:** Medium (CLI and settings code mapped, nothing executed).
- **Dimensions:** API/contract compatibility, data integrity, concurrency, security (local channel, secrets), backward compatibility of existing flags, operability for agents.
- **P0 gates/evidence:** Contract tests for envelope, error codes and exit codes; UI/CLI validation parity tests per setting; concurrency tests with two writers and stale revision; routing tests with and without a running instance; secret redaction tests.
- **P1 gates/evidence:** Regression tests of existing flags; no window/tray/model on `handy settings`; read latency measurement; help text snapshot.
- **Non-functional expectations:** Reads within 2 seconds, instance answers within 5 seconds; local channel restricted to the current user; no setting values logged above debug level and secrets never logged.

- **Boundary:** QE defines risk and test sufficiency; the independent review judges requirements; spec-test executes runtime proof; a security audit of the local channel is separate.

", "start_line": 298, "end_line": 307, "start_byte": 17709, "end_byte": 19043}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/008-settings-cli/spec.md:L308-L315", "source": ".specs/features/008-settings-cli/spec.md", "role": "spec", "text": "## Edge Cases

- Running instance hangs: the CLI times out after 5 seconds with `unavailable` and does not write the store itself, to avoid a conflicting writer.
- Settings store missing: reads return defaults with revision 0; the first write creates the store.
- Corrupted store: the existing salvage logic applies; the CLI reports a warning on stderr.
- Two CLI invocations at once without a running app: the write lock serializes them.
- Non-UTF-8 stdin for a text import: `validation_failed` with the offending byte offset.

", "start_line": 21, "end_line": 22, "start_byte": 918, "end_byte": 947}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/009-pin-mode-and-enter-rule/spec.md:L23-L62", "source": ".specs/features/009-pin-mode-and-enter-rule/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 1 — Pin a destination from the badge `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** pin the destination application from the badge, **so that** all my next dictations go there while I read or work elsewhere.

**Independent test:** Pin ChatGPT during a dictation, then dictate three times from other applications and check where each text lands.

  Scenario: Pin from the badge

  Scenario: Pinned across app switches and new dictations
    Given ChatGPT is pinned
    When the user starts a dictation while Safari is frontmost
    Then the destination of this dictation is ChatGPT
    And at the end Handy activates ChatGPT and inserts the text there
  Scenario: Unpin
    Given ChatGPT is pinned
    When the user chooses "Unpin" in the badge menu
    Then the pin mark disappears
    And the next dictation captures the frontmost application again

  D --> F[Badge without pin mark]
  E --> G{User action in badge menu}
  F --> G
  G -- Pin current destination --> H[Pin stored; applies now and next dictations]
  G -- Unpin --> I[Pin cleared; next dictations capture frontmost]

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** choose Never, Always or Only in PIN mode for automatic Enter, **so that** messages are sent automatically only where I want.
