    When a dictation is inserted into ChatGPT successfully
    Then exactly one Enter key press is sent after the insertion
  Scenario: Only in PIN mode, not pinned
    Given automatic Enter is "Only in PIN mode"
    And nothing is pinned
    When a dictation is inserted successfully
    Then no Enter key press is sent
  Scenario: Always
    Given automatic Enter is "Always"
    When a dictation is inserted successfully
    Then exactly one Enter key press is sent
  Scenario: Never
    Given automatic Enter is "Never"
    When a dictation is inserted successfully
    Then no Enter key press is sent
  Scenario: Upgrade from the existing auto-submit

    When settings load after upgrade
    Then automatic Enter is "Always" with key Ctrl+Enter
    And no other auto-submit control remains in the settings
```

flowchart TD
  A[Insertion outcome] --> B{Insertion attempted successfully?}
  B -- No --> C[No Enter]
  B -- Yes --> D{Option}
  D -- Never --> C
  D -- Always --> E[Send one Enter]
  D -- Only in PIN mode --> F{Destination came from the pin?}
  F -- Yes --> E
  F -- No --> C
```

", "start_line": 22, "end_line": 31, "start_byte": 456, "end_byte": 924}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/009-pin-mode-and-enter-rule/spec.md:L137-L180", "source": ".specs/features/009-pin-mode-and-enter-rule/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 4 — Enter only after a successful insertion `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** never have Enter pressed when my text did not land, **so that** an empty or wrong message is never sent.

**Priority reason:** An Enter after a failed insertion can send an empty message or trigger an unintended action.
**Independent test:** Inject activation failure, insertion failure and recovery display, with automatic Enter "Always".

```gherkin
Feature: Enter after a successful insertion only
  Scenario: Destination unavailable
    Given automatic Enter is "Always"
    When the destination is unavailable at insertion time
    Then no Enter key press is sent
  Scenario: Insertion method failed
    Given automatic Enter is "Always"
    When the insertion method reports failure
    Then no Enter key press is sent
  Scenario: Paste method none
    Given the paste method is "none"
    When a dictation completes
    Then no Enter key press is sent
  Scenario: Smart paste without observed read
    Given the paste method is smart paste
    When the target never reads the clipboard and the outcome is "not read"
    Then no Enter key press is sent
  Scenario: Destination left before Enter
    Given automatic Enter is "Always" and the text was inserted into ChatGPT
    When another application becomes frontmost before the Enter press
    Then no Enter key press is sent
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Insertion step] --> B{Destination frontmost?}

  B -- Yes --> C{Method reported success?}
  C -- No --> X
  C -- Yes --> D{Smart paste read observed, or Windows reliable paste read confirmed, if used?}
  D -- No --> X
  D -- Yes --> E{Recovery shown instead of insertion?}
  E -- Yes --> X
  E -- No --> F[Apply Enter option]
```

", "start_line": 6, "end_line": 12, "start_byte": 87, "end_byte": 278}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L13-L36", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## Core Principles

1. **The spec is the functional source of truth, not the code.**
   If the spec says one thing and the code does another, the code is wrong (unless the spec was intentionally updated).

2. **Every feature has a spec — no implementation without a spec.**
   Before writing a single line of code, the corresponding `.specs/features/NNN-feature-name/spec.md` must exist.

3. **Specs are living — updated when behavior changes.**
   When a feature's behavior is modified, the spec.md is updated first (or simultaneously). Specs never become stale.

4. **Specs are visual and testable — Gherkin scenarios and Mermaid flows are mandatory.**
   Every user story in a spec.md must include Gherkin scenarios (source of truth for AI and test scaffolding) and a Mermaid flowchart (visual representation of the same flow). Text-only specs are incomplete.

5. **Code is linked to specs — every implementation is traceable.**
   After implementation, `implementation.md` maps every FR and AC to the `@spec` anchor comment placed directly in the source code. Anchor comments include a **brief description** and the **relative path to the spec file with a fragment anchor** for deep-linking:
   ```
   // @spec FR-001: Brief description — .specs/features/NNN-feature-name/spec.md#fr-001
   ```
   - The description (after `:`) is a short summary (<50 chars) of the FR/AC
   - The fragment `#fr-001` enables deep-linking within the Markdown ecosystem (GitHub, preview, `implementation.md` → `spec.md`)
   - `grep -rn "@spec FR-001"` continues to work regardless of line number changes
   - Multi-requirements: list each `ID: description` separated by commas (e.g. `// @spec FR-001: Fetch count, FR-003: Mark as read — spec.md#fr-001`)

`verify-output`.

Legacy dotted `/spec-*` aliases remain accepted during the migration window, but

", "start_line": 204, "end_line": 223, "start_byte": 8477, "end_byte": 9190}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L224-L250", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## README.md — Spec Registry

`.specs/README.md` is the centralized index of all spec artifacts. It is maintained automatically by spec commands.

**Update rules:**
- `/spec-init` creates it with initial content
- `/spec-specify` adds a feature row (Status: Draft) + regenerates Recent Activity from changelog.md
- `/spec-plan` updates feature status to Planned
- `/spec-implement` updates feature status to Implemented/In Progress + regenerates Recent Activity from changelog.md
- `/spec-stack` adds ADR rows + regenerates Recent Activity
- `/spec-refine` updates the `Last updated` date (does not modify feature rows)
- `/spec-propose` does not modify it (read-only command)
- `/spec-check` and `/spec-explain` do not modify it
- `/spec-status` does not modify any files (read-only command)

- `/spec-specify` checks matching roadmap items + adds deferred splits to `roadmap.md`
- `/spec-propose` reads `roadmap.md` including Deferred section (read-only)
- `/spec-refine project` re-evaluates roadmap after project profile changes + supports direct roadmap refinement
- `/spec-specify` detects emerging dependencies and roadmap item absorption
- Every update also refreshes the `Last updated` date in the header

**Section markers:** Updatable sections use `<!-- readme:features:start/end -->`, `<!-- readme:decisions:start/end -->`, `<!-- readme:activity:start/end -->` HTML comments. Do not remove these markers.

**Recovery:** If README.md is missing, any updating command rebuilds it by scanning existing `.specs/features/*/spec.md`, `.specs/stacks/decisions/ADR-*.md`, and `.specs/changelog.md`.

", "start_line": 224, "end_line": 250, "start_byte": 9190, "end_byte": 10866}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L251-L270", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## Lifecycle Hooks

LiveSpec supports **lifecycle hooks** — Markdown files with instructions injected before/after each command. Hooks enable customizing LiveSpec behavior without modifying core commands.

**Full protocol:** Read [`system/hooks.md`](../system/hooks.md) for the complete resolution protocol, naming conventions, and inheritance model.

**Quick reference:**
- 4 resolution levels: user integrations (`~/.config/livespec/*.md`) → global (`~/.claude/livespec/hooks/`) → project (`.specs/hooks/`) → local (`.specs/hooks/*.local.md`)
- Naming: `{before|after}-{command}.md` and `{before|after}-{command}.local.md` (Levels 1–3); user integrations target commands via frontmatter, not filename
- Inheritance: `mode: extend` (default, accumulate) or `mode: override` (replace chain at the level that declares it)
- Step-level hooks: `before-implement-step.md` / `after-implement-step.md`
- Discovery: `/spec-hooks [command]` to see active hooks; use `--create`/`--edit` to manage hooks

**User-level integrations.** Markdown files in `~/.config/livespec/` may
inject instructions into selected commands (Level 0 of hook resolution).
See [`integrations.md`](../system/integrations.md) for the full schema,
runtime CLI (`livespec hooks resolve`), and chained-pipeline semantics.

---

", "start_line": 251, "end_line": 270, "start_byte": 10866, "end_byte": 12167}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L271-L272", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## Rules for AI Tools

", "start_line": 271, "end_line": 272, "start_byte": 12167, "end_byte": 12190}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L273-L279", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### MANDATORY — Hooks Resolution Protocol

**You MUST resolve hooks before and after EVERY `/spec-*` command execution.** This is not optional. Failure to resolve hooks means conventions are not loaded and the command runs without context.

**Before starting any command:** resolve `before-{command}` hooks.
**After completing any command:** resolve `after-{command}` hooks.

", "start_line": 273, "end_line": 279, "start_byte": 12190, "end_byte": 12568}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L280-L293", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "#### Resolution algorithm (for each hook event)

For a given event (e.g., `before-plan`), Read files at 3 levels in order:

| Level | Path | Scope |
|-------|------|-------|
| 1. Global | `~/.claude/livespec/hooks/before-plan.md` | All LiveSpec projects |
| 2. Project | `.specs/hooks/before-plan.md` | This project (committed, team-shared) |
| 3. Local | `.specs/hooks/before-plan.local.md` | Personal (gitignored) |

- If a file does not exist at a level → skip that level silently.
- If the **local** hook has `mode: override` in its YAML frontmatter → execute **only** the local hook, skip global and project.
- Otherwise (`mode: extend`, the default) → execute **all** existing hooks in order: global → project → local.

", "start_line": 280, "end_line": 293, "start_byte": 12568, "end_byte": 13304}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L294-L318", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "#### Exhaustive hook table — all commands

| Command | Before hooks to resolve | After hooks to resolve |
|---------|------------------------|----------------------|
| `init` | `before-init` (global, project, local) | `after-init` (global, project, local) |
| `propose` | `before-propose` (global, project, local) | `after-propose` (global, project, local) |
| `specify` | `before-specify` (global, project, local) | `after-specify` (global, project, local) |
| `plan` | `before-plan` (global, project, local) | `after-plan` (global, project, local) |
| `implement` | `before-implement` (global, project, local) | `after-implement` (global, project, local) |
| `implement` (each step) | `before-implement-step` (global, project, local) | `after-implement-step` (global, project, local) |
| `check` | `before-check` (global, project, local) | `after-check` (global, project, local) |
| `test` | `before-test` (global, project, local) | `after-test` (global, project, local) |
| `explain` | `before-explain` (global, project, local) | `after-explain` (global, project, local) |
| `stack` | `before-stack` (global, project, local) | `after-stack` (global, project, local) |
| `feature` | `before-feature` (global, project, local) | `after-feature` (global, project, local) |
| `refine` | `before-refine` (global, project, local) | `after-refine` (global, project, local) |
| `preflight` | `before-preflight` (global, project, local) | `after-preflight` (global, project, local) |
| `fix` | `before-fix` (global, project, local) | `after-fix` (global, project, local) |

**No hooks:** `hooks`, `play-coverage`, `status`, `refresh-conventions` — these are diagnostic/utility commands.

**`feature` sub-commands:** `/spec-feature` wraps a pipeline (specify → clarify → plan → analyze → implement). Resolve `before-feature`/`after-feature` around the full pipeline AND resolve each sub-command's own hooks (before-specify, before-plan, before-implement, etc.) at each phase.

**`implement` step hooks:** In addition to `before-implement`/`after-implement` (once), resolve `before-implement-step`/`after-implement-step` before and after EACH implementation step.

", "start_line": 294, "end_line": 318, "start_byte": 13304, "end_byte": 15472}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L319-L332", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Version Check (ADVISORY)

Before executing any `/spec-*` command (except `/spec-init` and `/spec-migrate`):

1. Read `.specs/livespec-version` — if missing, assume v1

", "start_line": 319, "end_line": 332, "start_byte": 15472, "end_byte": 16042}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L333-L345", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Command discovery

", "start_line": 333, "end_line": 345, "start_byte": 16042, "end_byte": 16781}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L346-L353", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### When CREATING a new feature

", "start_line": 346, "end_line": 353, "start_byte": 16781, "end_byte": 17270}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L354-L361", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Changelog Convention

", "start_line": 354, "end_line": 361, "start_byte": 17270, "end_byte": 17546}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L362-L378", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Changelog Rotation

To prevent changelogs from growing unbounded:

**Global `.specs/changelog.md`:**
- Keeps entries for the **current year** only
- When adding an entry, if entries from previous years exist, move them to `.specs/archive/changelog-YYYY.md` (one file per year)
- Add a "Previous years" link section at the bottom: `> Archive: [2025](archive/changelog-2025.md) | [2024](archive/changelog-2024.md)`

**Per-feature `changelog.md`:**
- No automatic rotation (features are naturally scoped)

**README.md Recent Activity:**

", "start_line": 362, "end_line": 378, "start_byte": 17546, "end_byte": 18326}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L379-L386", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### When MODIFYING existing code

", "start_line": 379, "end_line": 386, "start_byte": 18326, "end_byte": 18698}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L387-L394", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### When DEBUGGING

", "start_line": 395, "end_line": 403, "start_byte": 18960, "end_byte": 19665}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L404-L413", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### When REVIEWING a feature

", "start_line": 404, "end_line": 413, "start_byte": 19665, "end_byte": 19929}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L414-L423", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## Diagram Requirements (Gherkin + Mermaid)

Every behavioral flow requires **two representations**:
1. **Gherkin** (```gherkin blocks) — the canonical, machine-parseable format. Source of truth for AI test scaffolding and all test derivation (unit, integration, E2E, visual).

", "start_line": 414, "end_line": 423, "start_byte": 19929, "end_byte": 20520}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L424-L431", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Gherkin Syntax Rules

- Each story must have at least 2 scenarios (happy path + edge case)
- Scenarios must be specific enough to derive Playwright test steps directly
- Use present tense, third person
- Fenced with ````gherkin` (not plain ``` blocks)

", "start_line": 424, "end_line": 431, "start_byte": 20520, "end_byte": 20860}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L432-L458", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### In spec.md — User Flow (Gherkin + flowchart)

Every user story requires Gherkin scenarios (source of truth for tests) followed by a Mermaid flowchart (visual aid):

```gherkin
Feature: User action
  Scenario: Happy path
    Given a precondition is true
    When  the user performs the action
    Then  the system produces outcome A
    And   the state is updated

  Scenario: Alternative path
    Given a different precondition
    When  the user performs the action
    Then  the system produces outcome B
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[User action] --> B{Decision point}
    B -- Yes --> C[Outcome A]
    B -- No --> D[Outcome B]
    C --> E[End state]
    D --> E
```

", "start_line": 432, "end_line": 458, "start_byte": 20860, "end_byte": 21542}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L459-L492", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### In plan.md — Sequence Diagram (Gherkin + sequenceDiagram)

    When  the user submits a new resource
    Then  the system persists the resource

    When  the user submits invalid data
    Then  the system returns a 400 error
    And   the resource is not created

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant C as Client
    participant A as API
    participant D as Database

    U->>C: Triggers action
    C->>A: POST /resource
    A->>D: Insert record
    D-->>A: record created
    A-->>C: 201 Created
    C-->>U: Shows confirmation
```

", "start_line": 459, "end_line": 492, "start_byte": 21542, "end_byte": 22387}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L493-L519", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### In plan.md — State Diagram (Gherkin + stateDiagram)

Native Quality Engineering Analysis is built into `spec-specify`, `spec-plan`, and `spec-test`. **Read** [`qe-analysis.md`](qe-analysis.md) for the native dimensions, risk classification, gates, evidence contract, anti-invention rules, boundaries, and per-command mapping. **As a** Handy user, **I want to** never have Enter pressed when my text did not land, **so that** an empty or wrong message is never sent.

**Priority reason:** An Enter after a failed insertion can send an empty message or trigger an unintended action.
**Independent test:** Inject activation failure, insertion failure and recovery display, with automatic Enter "Always".

Feature: Enter after a successful insertion only
  Scenario: Destination unavailable
    Given automatic Enter is "Always"
    When the destination is unavailable at insertion time
    Then no Enter key press is sent
  Scenario: Insertion method failed
    Given automatic Enter is "Always"
    When the insertion method reports failure
    Then no Enter key press is sent
  Scenario: Paste method none
    Given the paste method is "none"
    When a dictation completes
    Then no Enter key press is sent
  Scenario: Smart paste without observed read
    Given the paste method is smart paste
    When the target never reads the clipboard and the outcome is "not read"
    Then no Enter key press is sent

", "start_line": 6, "end_line": 12, "start_byte": 87, "end_byte": 278}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L13-L36", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## Core Principles

1. **The spec is the functional source of truth, not the code.**
   If the spec says one thing and the code does another, the code is wrong (unless the spec was intentionally updated).

2. **Every feature has a spec — no implementation without a spec.**
   Before writing a single line of code, the corresponding `.specs/features/NNN-feature-name/spec.md` must exist.

3. **Specs are living — updated when behavior changes.**
   When a feature's behavior is modified, the spec.md is updated first (or simultaneously). Specs never become stale.

4. **Specs are visual and testable — Gherkin scenarios and Mermaid flows are mandatory.**
   Every user story in a spec.md must include Gherkin scenarios (source of truth for AI and test scaffolding) and a Mermaid flowchart (visual representation of the same flow). Text-only specs are incomplete.

5. **Code is linked to specs — every implementation is traceable.**
   After implementation, `implementation.md` maps every FR and AC to the `@spec` anchor comment placed directly in the source code. Anchor comments include a **brief description** and the **relative path to the spec file with a fragment anchor** for deep-linking:
   ```
   // @spec FR-001: Brief description — .specs/features/NNN-feature-name/spec.md#fr-001
   ```
   - The description (after `:`) is a short summary (<50 chars) of the FR/AC
   - The fragment `#fr-001` enables deep-linking within the Markdown ecosystem (GitHub, preview, `implementation.md` → `spec.md`)
   - `grep -rn "@spec FR-001"` continues to work regardless of line number changes
   - Multi-requirements: list each `ID: description` separated by commas (e.g. `// @spec FR-001: Fetch count, FR-003: Mark as read — spec.md#fr-001`)

`.specs/README.md` is the centralized index of all spec artifacts. It is maintained automatically by spec commands.

**Update rules:**
- `/spec-init` creates it with initial content
- `/spec-specify` adds a feature row (Status: Draft) + regenerates Recent Activity from changelog.md
- `/spec-plan` updates feature status to Planned
- `/spec-implement` updates feature status to Implemented/In Progress + regenerates Recent Activity from changelog.md
- `/spec-stack` adds ADR rows + regenerates Recent Activity
- `/spec-refine` updates the `Last updated` date (does not modify feature rows)
- `/spec-propose` does not modify it (read-only command)
- `/spec-check` and `/spec-explain` do not modify it
- `/spec-status` does not modify any files (read-only command)
- `/spec-init` creates `roadmap.md` with inferred feature backlog
- `/spec-specify` checks matching roadmap items + adds deferred splits to `roadmap.md`
- `/spec-propose` reads `roadmap.md` including Deferred section (read-only)
- `/spec-refine project` re-evaluates roadmap after project profile changes + supports direct roadmap refinement
- `/spec-specify` detects emerging dependencies and roadmap item absorption
- Every update also refreshes the `Last updated` date in the header

**Section markers:** Updatable sections use `<!-- readme:features:start/end -->`, `<!-- readme:decisions:start/end -->`, `<!-- readme:activity:start/end -->` HTML comments. Do not remove these markers.

**Recovery:** If README.md is missing, any updating command rebuilds it by scanning existing `.specs/features/*/spec.md`, `.specs/stacks/decisions/ADR-*.md`, and `.specs/changelog.md`.

", "start_line": 224, "end_line": 250, "start_byte": 9190, "end_byte": 10866}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L251-L270", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## Lifecycle Hooks

LiveSpec supports **lifecycle hooks** — Markdown files with instructions injected before/after each command. Hooks enable customizing LiveSpec behavior without modifying core commands.

**Full protocol:** Read [`system/hooks.md`](../system/hooks.md) for the complete resolution protocol, naming conventions, and inheritance model.

**Quick reference:**
- 4 resolution levels: user integrations (`~/.config/livespec/*.md`) → global (`~/.claude/livespec/hooks/`) → project (`.specs/hooks/`) → local (`.specs/hooks/*.local.md`)
- Naming: `{before|after}-{command}.md` and `{before|after}-{command}.local.md` (Levels 1–3); user integrations target commands via frontmatter, not filename
- Inheritance: `mode: extend` (default, accumulate) or `mode: override` (replace chain at the level that declares it)
- Step-level hooks: `before-implement-step.md` / `after-implement-step.md`
- Discovery: `/spec-hooks [command]` to see active hooks; use `--create`/`--edit` to manage hooks

**User-level integrations.** Markdown files in `~/.config/livespec/` may
inject instructions into selected commands (Level 0 of hook resolution).
See [`integrations.md`](../system/integrations.md) for the full schema,
runtime CLI (`livespec hooks resolve`), and chained-pipeline semantics.

---

", "start_line": 251, "end_line": 270, "start_byte": 10866, "end_byte": 12167}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L271-L272", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## Rules for AI Tools

", "start_line": 271, "end_line": 272, "start_byte": 12167, "end_byte": 12190}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L273-L279", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### MANDATORY — Hooks Resolution Protocol

**You MUST resolve hooks before and after EVERY `/spec-*` command execution.** This is not optional. Failure to resolve hooks means conventions are not loaded and the command runs without context.

**Before starting any command:** resolve `before-{command}` hooks.
**After completing any command:** resolve `after-{command}` hooks.

", "start_line": 273, "end_line": 279, "start_byte": 12190, "end_byte": 12568}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L280-L293", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "#### Resolution algorithm (for each hook event)

For a given event (e.g., `before-plan`), Read files at 3 levels in order:

| Level | Path | Scope |
|-------|------|-------|
| 1. Global | `~/.claude/livespec/hooks/before-plan.md` | All LiveSpec projects |
| 2. Project | `.specs/hooks/before-plan.md` | This project (committed, team-shared) |
| 3. Local | `.specs/hooks/before-plan.local.md` | Personal (gitignored) |

- If a file does not exist at a level → skip that level silently.
- If the **local** hook has `mode: override` in its YAML frontmatter → execute **only** the local hook, skip global and project.
- Otherwise (`mode: extend`, the default) → execute **all** existing hooks in order: global → project → local.

", "start_line": 280, "end_line": 293, "start_byte": 12568, "end_byte": 13304}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L294-L318", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "#### Exhaustive hook table — all commands

| Command | Before hooks to resolve | After hooks to resolve |
|---------|------------------------|----------------------|
| `init` | `before-init` (global, project, local) | `after-init` (global, project, local) |
| `propose` | `before-propose` (global, project, local) | `after-propose` (global, project, local) |
| `specify` | `before-specify` (global, project, local) | `after-specify` (global, project, local) |
| `plan` | `before-plan` (global, project, local) | `after-plan` (global, project, local) |
| `implement` | `before-implement` (global, project, local) | `after-implement` (global, project, local) |
| `implement` (each step) | `before-implement-step` (global, project, local) | `after-implement-step` (global, project, local) |
| `check` | `before-check` (global, project, local) | `after-check` (global, project, local) |
| `test` | `before-test` (global, project, local) | `after-test` (global, project, local) |
| `explain` | `before-explain` (global, project, local) | `after-explain` (global, project, local) |
| `stack` | `before-stack` (global, project, local) | `after-stack` (global, project, local) |
| `feature` | `before-feature` (global, project, local) | `after-feature` (global, project, local) |
| `refine` | `before-refine` (global, project, local) | `after-refine` (global, project, local) |
| `preflight` | `before-preflight` (global, project, local) | `after-preflight` (global, project, local) |
| `fix` | `before-fix` (global, project, local) | `after-fix` (global, project, local) |

**No hooks:** `hooks`, `play-coverage`, `status`, `refresh-conventions` — these are diagnostic/utility commands.

**`feature` sub-commands:** `/spec-feature` wraps a pipeline (specify → clarify → plan → analyze → implement). Resolve `before-feature`/`after-feature` around the full pipeline AND resolve each sub-command's own hooks (before-specify, before-plan, before-implement, etc.) at each phase.

**`implement` step hooks:** In addition to `before-implement`/`after-implement` (once), resolve `before-implement-step`/`after-implement-step` before and after EACH implementation step.

", "start_line": 294, "end_line": 318, "start_byte": 13304, "end_byte": 15472}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L319-L332", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Version Check (ADVISORY)

Before executing any `/spec-*` command (except `/spec-init` and `/spec-migrate`):

1. Read `.specs/livespec-version` — if missing, assume v1
2. Resolve the LiveSpec repo path from `.specs/.livespec-path` (if missing, resolve from command symlink chain)

", "start_line": 333, "end_line": 345, "start_byte": 16042, "end_byte": 16781}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L346-L353", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### When CREATING a new feature

", "start_line": 346, "end_line": 353, "start_byte": 16781, "end_byte": 17270}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L354-L361", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Changelog Convention

", "start_line": 354, "end_line": 361, "start_byte": 17270, "end_byte": 17546}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L362-L378", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Changelog Rotation

", "start_line": 362, "end_line": 378, "start_byte": 17546, "end_byte": 18326}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L379-L386", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### When MODIFYING existing code

", "start_line": 379, "end_line": 386, "start_byte": 18326, "end_byte": 18698}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L387-L394", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### When DEBUGGING

", "start_line": 404, "end_line": 413, "start_byte": 19665, "end_byte": 19929}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L414-L423", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## Diagram Requirements (Gherkin + Mermaid)

Every behavioral flow requires **two representations**:
1. **Gherkin** (```gherkin blocks) — the canonical, machine-parseable format. Source of truth for AI test scaffolding and all test derivation (unit, integration, E2E, visual).

- Each story must have at least 2 scenarios (happy path + edge case)
- Scenarios must be specific enough to derive Playwright test steps directly
- Use present tense, third person
- Fenced with ````gherkin` (not plain ``` blocks)

", "start_line": 424, "end_line": 431, "start_byte": 20520, "end_byte": 20860}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L432-L458", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### In spec.md — User Flow (Gherkin + flowchart)

Every user story requires Gherkin scenarios (source of truth for tests) followed by a Mermaid flowchart (visual aid):

```gherkin
Feature: User action
  Scenario: Happy path
    Given a precondition is true
    When  the user performs the action
    Then  the system produces outcome A
    And   the state is updated

  Scenario: Alternative path
    Given a different precondition
    When  the user performs the action
    Then  the system produces outcome B
```

", "start_line": 21, "end_line": 22, "start_byte": 1269, "end_byte": 1298}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/010-recovery-bubble/spec.md:L23-L58", "source": ".specs/features/010-recovery-bubble/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 1 — Recover the text when the destination is unavailable `P1`

1. **The spec is the functional source of truth, not the code.**
   If the spec says one thing and the code does another, the code is wrong (unless the spec was intentionally updated).

2. **Every feature has a spec — no implementation without a spec.**
   Before writing a single line of code, the corresponding `.specs/features/NNN-feature-name/spec.md` must exist.

3. **Specs are living — updated when behavior changes.**
   When a feature's behavior is modified, the spec.md is updated first (or simultaneously). Specs never become stale.

4. **Specs are visual and testable — Gherkin scenarios and Mermaid flows are mandatory.**
   Every user story in a spec.md must include Gherkin scenarios (source of truth for AI and test scaffolding) and a Mermaid flowchart (visual representation of the same flow). Text-only specs are incomplete.

5. **Code is linked to specs — every implementation is traceable.**
   After implementation, `implementation.md` maps every FR and AC to the `@spec` anchor comment placed directly in the source code. Anchor comments include a **brief description** and the **relative path to the spec file with a fragment anchor** for deep-linking:
   ```
   // @spec FR-001: Brief description — .specs/features/NNN-feature-name/spec.md#fr-001
   ```
   - The description (after `:`) is a short summary (<50 chars) of the FR/AC
   - The fragment `#fr-001` enables deep-linking within the Markdown ecosystem (GitHub, preview, `implementation.md` → `spec.md`)
   - `grep -rn "@spec FR-001"` continues to work regardless of line number changes
   - Multi-requirements: list each `ID: description` separated by commas (e.g. `// @spec FR-001: Fetch count, FR-003: Mark as read — spec.md#fr-001`)

LiveSpec supports **lifecycle hooks** — Markdown files with instructions injected before/after each command. Hooks enable customizing LiveSpec behavior without modifying core commands.

**Full protocol:** Read [`system/hooks.md`](../system/hooks.md) for the complete resolution protocol, naming conventions, and inheritance model.

**Quick reference:**
- 4 resolution levels: user integrations (`~/.config/livespec/*.md`) → global (`~/.claude/livespec/hooks/`) → project (`.specs/hooks/`) → local (`.specs/hooks/*.local.md`)
- Naming: `{before|after}-{command}.md` and `{before|after}-{command}.local.md` (Levels 1–3); user integrations target commands via frontmatter, not filename
- Inheritance: `mode: extend` (default, accumulate) or `mode: override` (replace chain at the level that declares it)
- Step-level hooks: `before-implement-step.md` / `after-implement-step.md`
- Discovery: `/spec-hooks [command]` to see active hooks; use `--create`/`--edit` to manage hooks

**User-level integrations.** Markdown files in `~/.config/livespec/` may
inject instructions into selected commands (Level 0 of hook resolution).
See [`integrations.md`](../system/integrations.md) for the full schema,
runtime CLI (`livespec hooks resolve`), and chained-pipeline semantics.

---

", "start_line": 271, "end_line": 272, "start_byte": 12167, "end_byte": 12190}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L273-L279", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### MANDATORY — Hooks Resolution Protocol

**You MUST resolve hooks before and after EVERY `/spec-*` command execution.** This is not optional. Failure to resolve hooks means conventions are not loaded and the command runs without context.

**Before starting any command:** resolve `before-{command}` hooks.
**After completing any command:** resolve `after-{command}` hooks.

", "start_line": 273, "end_line": 279, "start_byte": 12190, "end_byte": 12568}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L280-L293", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "#### Resolution algorithm (for each hook event)

For a given event (e.g., `before-plan`), Read files at 3 levels in order:

| Level | Path | Scope |
|-------|------|-------|
| 1. Global | `~/.claude/livespec/hooks/before-plan.md` | All LiveSpec projects |
| 2. Project | `.specs/hooks/before-plan.md` | This project (committed, team-shared) |
| 3. Local | `.specs/hooks/before-plan.local.md` | Personal (gitignored) |

- If a file does not exist at a level → skip that level silently.
- If the **local** hook has `mode: override` in its YAML frontmatter → execute **only** the local hook, skip global and project.
- Otherwise (`mode: extend`, the default) → execute **all** existing hooks in order: global → project → local.

|---------|------------------------|----------------------|
| `init` | `before-init` (global, project, local) | `after-init` (global, project, local) |
| `propose` | `before-propose` (global, project, local) | `after-propose` (global, project, local) |
| `specify` | `before-specify` (global, project, local) | `after-specify` (global, project, local) |
| `plan` | `before-plan` (global, project, local) | `after-plan` (global, project, local) |
| `implement` | `before-implement` (global, project, local) | `after-implement` (global, project, local) |
| `implement` (each step) | `before-implement-step` (global, project, local) | `after-implement-step` (global, project, local) |
| `check` | `before-check` (global, project, local) | `after-check` (global, project, local) |
| `test` | `before-test` (global, project, local) | `after-test` (global, project, local) |
| `explain` | `before-explain` (global, project, local) | `after-explain` (global, project, local) |
| `stack` | `before-stack` (global, project, local) | `after-stack` (global, project, local) |
| `feature` | `before-feature` (global, project, local) | `after-feature` (global, project, local) |
| `refine` | `before-refine` (global, project, local) | `after-refine` (global, project, local) |
| `preflight` | `before-preflight` (global, project, local) | `after-preflight` (global, project, local) |
| `fix` | `before-fix` (global, project, local) | `after-fix` (global, project, local) |

**No hooks:** `hooks`, `play-coverage`, `status`, `refresh-conventions` — these are diagnostic/utility commands.

**`feature` sub-commands:** `/spec-feature` wraps a pipeline (specify → clarify → plan → analyze → implement). Resolve `before-feature`/`after-feature` around the full pipeline AND resolve each sub-command's own hooks (before-specify, before-plan, before-implement, etc.) at each phase.

Every behavioral flow requires **two representations**:
1. **Gherkin** (```gherkin blocks) — the canonical, machine-parseable format. Source of truth for AI test scaffolding and all test derivation (unit, integration, E2E, visual).
2. **Mermaid** — the visual representation of the same flow, for human comprehension.

Every `/spec-*` command must follow these execution rules:

1. **Intent check first**
   Confirm the command matches user intent; if not, propose the correct `/spec-*` command (see Intent Classification above).

2. **Ambiguity cap**
   Ask at most 2 clarifying questions. If ambiguity remains, proceed with explicit `[ASSUMED]` markers.

3. **Prerequisite gate**
   Validate required files before writing. If missing, stop and provide the minimal recovery command.

4. **Evidence-based reporting**
   Do not mark items as complete without file/test evidence.

5. **Definition of done**
   End each command with:
   - artifacts created/updated
   - unresolved blockers (if any)
   - next recommended command

", "start_line": 6, "end_line": 12, "start_byte": 87, "end_byte": 278}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L13-L36", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## Core Principles

1. **The spec is the functional source of truth, not the code.**
   If the spec says one thing and the code does another, the code is wrong (unless the spec was intentionally updated).

2. **Every feature has a spec — no implementation without a spec.**
   Before writing a single line of code, the corresponding `.specs/features/NNN-feature-name/spec.md` must exist.

3. **Specs are living — updated when behavior changes.**
   When a feature's behavior is modified, the spec.md is updated first (or simultaneously). Specs never become stale.

4. **Specs are visual and testable — Gherkin scenarios and Mermaid flows are mandatory.**
   Every user story in a spec.md must include Gherkin scenarios (source of truth for AI and test scaffolding) and a Mermaid flowchart (visual representation of the same flow). Text-only specs are incomplete.

5. **Code is linked to specs — every implementation is traceable.**
   After implementation, `implementation.md` maps every FR and AC to the `@spec` anchor comment placed directly in the source code. Anchor comments include a **brief description** and the **relative path to the spec file with a fragment anchor** for deep-linking:
   ```
   // @spec FR-001: Brief description — .specs/features/NNN-feature-name/spec.md#fr-001
   ```
   - The description (after `:`) is a short summary (<50 chars) of the FR/AC
   - The fragment `#fr-001` enables deep-linking within the Markdown ecosystem (GitHub, preview, `implementation.md` → `spec.md`)
   - `grep -rn "@spec FR-001"` continues to work regardless of line number changes
   - Multi-requirements: list each `ID: description` separated by commas (e.g. `// @spec FR-001: Fetch count, FR-003: Mark as read — spec.md#fr-001`)

`.specs/README.md` is the centralized index of all spec artifacts. It is maintained automatically by spec commands.

**Update rules:**
- `/spec-init` creates it with initial content
- `/spec-specify` adds a feature row (Status: Draft) + regenerates Recent Activity from changelog.md
- `/spec-plan` updates feature status to Planned
- `/spec-implement` updates feature status to Implemented/In Progress + regenerates Recent Activity from changelog.md
- `/spec-stack` adds ADR rows + regenerates Recent Activity
- `/spec-refine` updates the `Last updated` date (does not modify feature rows)
- `/spec-propose` does not modify it (read-only command)
- `/spec-check` and `/spec-explain` do not modify it
- `/spec-status` does not modify any files (read-only command)
- `/spec-init` creates `roadmap.md` with inferred feature backlog
- `/spec-specify` checks matching roadmap items + adds deferred splits to `roadmap.md`
- `/spec-propose` reads `roadmap.md` including Deferred section (read-only)
- `/spec-refine project` re-evaluates roadmap after project profile changes + supports direct roadmap refinement
- `/spec-specify` detects emerging dependencies and roadmap item absorption
- Every update also refreshes the `Last updated` date in the header

**Section markers:** Updatable sections use `<!-- readme:features:start/end -->`, `<!-- readme:decisions:start/end -->`, `<!-- readme:activity:start/end -->` HTML comments. Do not remove these markers.

**Recovery:** If README.md is missing, any updating command rebuilds it by scanning existing `.specs/features/*/spec.md`, `.specs/stacks/decisions/ADR-*.md`, and `.specs/changelog.md`.

", "start_line": 224, "end_line": 250, "start_byte": 9190, "end_byte": 10866}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L251-L270", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## Lifecycle Hooks

LiveSpec supports **lifecycle hooks** — Markdown files with instructions injected before/after each command. Hooks enable customizing LiveSpec behavior without modifying core commands.

**Full protocol:** Read [`system/hooks.md`](../system/hooks.md) for the complete resolution protocol, naming conventions, and inheritance model.

**Quick reference:**
- 4 resolution levels: user integrations (`~/.config/livespec/*.md`) → global (`~/.claude/livespec/hooks/`) → project (`.specs/hooks/`) → local (`.specs/hooks/*.local.md`)
- Naming: `{before|after}-{command}.md` and `{before|after}-{command}.local.md` (Levels 1–3); user integrations target commands via frontmatter, not filename
- Inheritance: `mode: extend` (default, accumulate) or `mode: override` (replace chain at the level that declares it)
- Step-level hooks: `before-implement-step.md` / `after-implement-step.md`
- Discovery: `/spec-hooks [command]` to see active hooks; use `--create`/`--edit` to manage hooks

**User-level integrations.** Markdown files in `~/.config/livespec/` may
inject instructions into selected commands (Level 0 of hook resolution).
See [`integrations.md`](../system/integrations.md) for the full schema,
runtime CLI (`livespec hooks resolve`), and chained-pipeline semantics.

---

", "start_line": 251, "end_line": 270, "start_byte": 10866, "end_byte": 12167}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L271-L272", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## Rules for AI Tools

", "start_line": 271, "end_line": 272, "start_byte": 12167, "end_byte": 12190}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L273-L279", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### MANDATORY — Hooks Resolution Protocol

**You MUST resolve hooks before and after EVERY `/spec-*` command execution.** This is not optional. Failure to resolve hooks means conventions are not loaded and the command runs without context.

**Before starting any command:** resolve `before-{command}` hooks.
**After completing any command:** resolve `after-{command}` hooks.

", "start_line": 273, "end_line": 279, "start_byte": 12190, "end_byte": 12568}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L280-L293", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "#### Resolution algorithm (for each hook event)

For a given event (e.g., `before-plan`), Read files at 3 levels in order:

| Level | Path | Scope |
|-------|------|-------|
| 1. Global | `~/.claude/livespec/hooks/before-plan.md` | All LiveSpec projects |
| 2. Project | `.specs/hooks/before-plan.md` | This project (committed, team-shared) |
| 3. Local | `.specs/hooks/before-plan.local.md` | Personal (gitignored) |

- If a file does not exist at a level → skip that level silently.
- If the **local** hook has `mode: override` in its YAML frontmatter → execute **only** the local hook, skip global and project.
- Otherwise (`mode: extend`, the default) → execute **all** existing hooks in order: global → project → local.

", "start_line": 280, "end_line": 293, "start_byte": 12568, "end_byte": 13304}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L294-L318", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "#### Exhaustive hook table — all commands

| Command | Before hooks to resolve | After hooks to resolve |
|---------|------------------------|----------------------|
| `init` | `before-init` (global, project, local) | `after-init` (global, project, local) |
| `propose` | `before-propose` (global, project, local) | `after-propose` (global, project, local) |
| `specify` | `before-specify` (global, project, local) | `after-specify` (global, project, local) |
| `plan` | `before-plan` (global, project, local) | `after-plan` (global, project, local) |
| `implement` | `before-implement` (global, project, local) | `after-implement` (global, project, local) |
| `implement` (each step) | `before-implement-step` (global, project, local) | `after-implement-step` (global, project, local) |
| `check` | `before-check` (global, project, local) | `after-check` (global, project, local) |
| `test` | `before-test` (global, project, local) | `after-test` (global, project, local) |
| `explain` | `before-explain` (global, project, local) | `after-explain` (global, project, local) |
| `stack` | `before-stack` (global, project, local) | `after-stack` (global, project, local) |
| `feature` | `before-feature` (global, project, local) | `after-feature` (global, project, local) |
| `refine` | `before-refine` (global, project, local) | `after-refine` (global, project, local) |
| `preflight` | `before-preflight` (global, project, local) | `after-preflight` (global, project, local) |
| `fix` | `before-fix` (global, project, local) | `after-fix` (global, project, local) |

**No hooks:** `hooks`, `play-coverage`, `status`, `refresh-conventions` — these are diagnostic/utility commands.

**`feature` sub-commands:** `/spec-feature` wraps a pipeline (specify → clarify → plan → analyze → implement). Resolve `before-feature`/`after-feature` around the full pipeline AND resolve each sub-command's own hooks (before-specify, before-plan, before-implement, etc.) at each phase.

**`implement` step hooks:** In addition to `before-implement`/`after-implement` (once), resolve `before-implement-step`/`after-implement-step` before and after EACH implementation step.

", "start_line": 294, "end_line": 318, "start_byte": 13304, "end_byte": 15472}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L319-L332", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Version Check (ADVISORY)

Before executing any `/spec-*` command (except `/spec-init` and `/spec-migrate`):

1. Read `.specs/livespec-version` — if missing, assume v1
2. Resolve the LiveSpec repo path from `.specs/.livespec-path` (if missing, resolve from command symlink chain)

", "start_line": 333, "end_line": 345, "start_byte": 16042, "end_byte": 16781}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L346-L353", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### When CREATING a new feature

", "start_line": 346, "end_line": 353, "start_byte": 16781, "end_byte": 17270}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L354-L361", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Changelog Convention

", "start_line": 354, "end_line": 361, "start_byte": 17270, "end_byte": 17546}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L362-L378", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Changelog Rotation

", "start_line": 362, "end_line": 378, "start_byte": 17546, "end_byte": 18326}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L379-L386", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### When MODIFYING existing code

", "start_line": 379, "end_line": 386, "start_byte": 18326, "end_byte": 18698}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L387-L394", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### When DEBUGGING

", "start_line": 404, "end_line": 413, "start_byte": 19665, "end_byte": 19929}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L414-L423", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## Diagram Requirements (Gherkin + Mermaid)

Every behavioral flow requires **two representations**:
1. **Gherkin** (```gherkin blocks) — the canonical, machine-parseable format. Source of truth for AI test scaffolding and all test derivation (unit, integration, E2E, visual).

- Each story must have at least 2 scenarios (happy path + edge case)
- Scenarios must be specific enough to derive Playwright test steps directly
- Use present tense, third person
- Fenced with ````gherkin` (not plain ``` blocks)

", "start_line": 424, "end_line": 431, "start_byte": 20520, "end_byte": 20860}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L432-L458", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### In spec.md — User Flow (Gherkin + flowchart)

Every user story requires Gherkin scenarios (source of truth for tests) followed by a Mermaid flowchart (visual aid):

```gherkin
Feature: User action
  Scenario: Happy path
    Given a precondition is true
    When  the user performs the action
    Then  the system produces outcome A
    And   the state is updated

  Scenario: Alternative path
    Given a different precondition
    When  the user performs the action
    Then  the system produces outcome B
```

New app acquires a per-user/store instance lease before loading settings, under settings.lock, publishes its private endpoint before releasing startup ownership, and keeps the lease until shutdown. A headless writer acquires settings.lock, then checks the new lease/endpoint and passive legacy state again immediately before commit. GUI startup for the new version uses that same lock; it reads a complete commit or establishes ownership before the CLI can mutate. The lease is separate from the transaction lock; a busy or starting owner never means offline permission. A stale new-version endpoint is reclaimable only after OS liveness/ownership proof and protected removal; ambiguous access returns unavailable with no write.

| OS | Private request channel / peer verification | Passive older-instance detection |
|---|---|---|
| macOS | Short AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM path in a canonical current-UID-owned directory (0700), with owner/type/device/inode guards; both endpoints enforce kernel peer UID via getpeereid before any application bytes | Inspect `/tmp/com_pais_handy_si.sock` type/owner without connecting, reading a legacy frame, invoking callback or removing it. Reuse inspect_legacy_path and its Absent/Occupied/Unavailable results. Stale/uncertain legacy resources refuse mutation rather than authorize deletion |
| Linux | AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM under validated current-UID-owned directory (0700), XDG_RUNTIME_DIR or short private fallback, with owner/type/device/inode guards; both endpoints enforce checked SO_PEERCRED UID before any application bytes | Query session DBus `com.pais.handy.SingleInstance` through NameHasOwner/GetNameOwner only; never own that name, serve ExecuteCallback or call it. Errors/unknown scope refuse mutation |
| Windows | Named pipe keyed by SID+store hash, protected current-logon-SID DACL, reject remote clients and verify client token | Query legacy `com.pais.handy-sim` mutex and `com.pais.handy-sic`/`com.pais.handy-siw` target without WM_COPYDATA. Never reserve the mutex or create a compatibility window/message loop. Missing/ambiguous ownership evidence refuses mutation |

Unix channel authorization uses the validated canonical current-UID directory with mode 0700 plus retained directory/socket owner, type, device/inode and single-link checks. Revalidate directory identity before/after bind and before accept/connect; refuse hostile aliases/replacements without touching substitutes. Bind without changing process-global umask, pathname chmod or a bootstrap-permission framework. Socket mode is diagnostic, not a portable security boundary. On macOS, ACLs can grant traversal/connection beyond ordinary mode bits, so mode 0700 alone is not exhaustive access proof: accepted clients and connected servers must each pass kernel-derived expected UID authentication before request parsing, response rendering or any application read/write. Failure closes/refuses the connection with no application bytes or store mutation; protocol UID/PID fields are never authorization evidence. Same-UID identity changes fail closed; no atomic pathname-race guarantee is claimed. Failed/closed socket names are retained rather than removed through a racy stat/check-then-unlink; Step 5 implements reviewed lease-proven reclamation so normal restart remains possible. Never delete the legacy singleton path.

**Informative:** Inspect [Linux unix(7)](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/unix.7.html) for pathname/socket permission portability and kernel SO_PEERCRED context; inspect [Apple getpeereid(3)](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/System/Conceptual/ManPages_iPhoneOS/man3/getpeereid.3.html) for both-side peer effective UID authentication. Cargo.lock resolves 2.4.0; recalculate identities if that dependency changes. Legacy identities do not prove store identity, so refuse conservatively for a same-user legacy owner even with an apparently different store. Do not connect/send an empty command: macOS empty streams can invoke show-window. Detected old instance means unavailable/5 and byte-identical store/revision, for reads or writes that would otherwise go to it.

Real older-binary race observations are pending release evidence, never a demand to recreate replay.

Requests to a running new app carry protocol version, user/store identity, opaque request ID, typed operation, expected revision and dry_run. Bound UTF-8 frames to 1 MiB, reject malformed/oversized input without raw dumps. Domain imports share this technical limit until their owner defines another. Requests contain no raw argv. Use a monotonic 5 s end-to-end response deadline, including lock/persistence/transport wait. Successful M1 reads finish within 2 s; timeout failures are measured separately. No offline fallback write or blind retry after submission/timeout; reread revision/value first. Late replies cannot resurrect an expired request.

", "start_line": 22, "end_line": 31, "start_byte": 456, "end_byte": 924}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/009-pin-mode-and-enter-rule/spec.md:L137-L180", "source": ".specs/features/009-pin-mode-and-enter-rule/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 4 — Enter only after a successful insertion `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** never have Enter pressed when my text did not land, **so that** an empty or wrong message is never sent.

**Priority reason:** An Enter after a failed insertion can send an empty message or trigger an unintended action.
**Independent test:** Inject activation failure, insertion failure and recovery display, with automatic Enter "Always".

```gherkin
Feature: Enter after a successful insertion only
  Scenario: Destination unavailable
    Given automatic Enter is "Always"
    When the destination is unavailable at insertion time
    Then no Enter key press is sent
  Scenario: Insertion method failed
    Given automatic Enter is "Always"
    When the insertion method reports failure
    Then no Enter key press is sent
  Scenario: Paste method none
    Given the paste method is "none"
    When a dictation completes
    Then no Enter key press is sent
  Scenario: Smart paste without observed read
    Given the paste method is smart paste
    When the target never reads the clipboard and the outcome is "not read"
    Then no Enter key press is sent
  Scenario: Destination left before Enter
    Given automatic Enter is "Always" and the text was inserted into ChatGPT
    When another application becomes frontmost before the Enter press
    Then no Enter key press is sent
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Insertion step] --> B{Destination frontmost?}
  B -- No --> X[No Enter]
  B -- Yes --> C{Method reported success?}
  C -- No --> X
  C -- Yes --> D{Smart paste read observed, or Windows reliable paste read confirmed, if used?}
  D -- No --> X
  D -- Yes --> E{Recovery shown instead of insertion?}
  E -- Yes --> X
  E -- No --> F[Apply Enter option]
```

", "start_line": 21, "end_line": 22, "start_byte": 1269, "end_byte": 1298}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/010-recovery-bubble/spec.md:L23-L58", "source": ".specs/features/010-recovery-bubble/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 1 — Recover the text when the destination is unavailable `P1`

", "start_line": 23, "end_line": 58, "start_byte": 1298, "end_byte": 2876}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/010-recovery-bubble/spec.md:L59-L95", "source": ".specs/features/010-recovery-bubble/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 2 — Recover the text when no text field is focused `P1`

**Priority reason:** Pasting with no editable field loses the text silently.

```gherkin
Feature: Recovery bubble when no field is editable
  Scenario: Focus is not editable
    Given accessibility permission is granted
    And the focused element of the destination is classified not editable
    When insertion is due
    Then the bubble appears with the reason "No text field is focused"
    And nothing is pasted
  Scenario: Classification undetermined
    Given the focused element cannot be classified
    When insertion is due
    Then Handy inserts as usual and no bubble appears
  Scenario: Setting off
    Given "Show the bubble when no text field is focused" is off
    When the focused element is not editable
    Then Handy inserts as usual
```

flowchart TD

  B -- No --> C[Insert as usual]
  B -- Yes --> D{Focused element}
  D -- Editable --> C
  D -- Undetermined --> C
  D -- Not editable --> E{Setting on?}
  E -- Yes --> F[Bubble: no text field]

", "start_line": 6, "end_line": 12, "start_byte": 87, "end_byte": 278}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L13-L36", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## Core Principles

1. **The spec is the functional source of truth, not the code.**
   If the spec says one thing and the code does another, the code is wrong (unless the spec was intentionally updated).

2. **Every feature has a spec — no implementation without a spec.**
   Before writing a single line of code, the corresponding `.specs/features/NNN-feature-name/spec.md` must exist.

3. **Specs are living — updated when behavior changes.**
   When a feature's behavior is modified, the spec.md is updated first (or simultaneously). Specs never become stale.

4. **Specs are visual and testable — Gherkin scenarios and Mermaid flows are mandatory.**
   Every user story in a spec.md must include Gherkin scenarios (source of truth for AI and test scaffolding) and a Mermaid flowchart (visual representation of the same flow). Text-only specs are incomplete.

5. **Code is linked to specs — every implementation is traceable.**
   After implementation, `implementation.md` maps every FR and AC to the `@spec` anchor comment placed directly in the source code. Anchor comments include a **brief description** and the **relative path to the spec file with a fragment anchor** for deep-linking:
   ```
   // @spec FR-001: Brief description — .specs/features/NNN-feature-name/spec.md#fr-001
   ```
   - The description (after `:`) is a short summary (<50 chars) of the FR/AC
   - The fragment `#fr-001` enables deep-linking within the Markdown ecosystem (GitHub, preview, `implementation.md` → `spec.md`)
   - `grep -rn "@spec FR-001"` continues to work regardless of line number changes
   - Multi-requirements: list each `ID: description` separated by commas (e.g. `// @spec FR-001: Fetch count, FR-003: Mark as read — spec.md#fr-001`)

", "start_line": 204, "end_line": 223, "start_byte": 8477, "end_byte": 9190}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L224-L250", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## README.md — Spec Registry

`.specs/README.md` is the centralized index of all spec artifacts. It is maintained automatically by spec commands.

**Update rules:**
- `/spec-init` creates it with initial content
- `/spec-specify` adds a feature row (Status: Draft) + regenerates Recent Activity from changelog.md
- `/spec-plan` updates feature status to Planned
- `/spec-implement` updates feature status to Implemented/In Progress + regenerates Recent Activity from changelog.md
- `/spec-stack` adds ADR rows + regenerates Recent Activity
- `/spec-refine` updates the `Last updated` date (does not modify feature rows)
- `/spec-propose` does not modify it (read-only command)
- `/spec-check` and `/spec-explain` do not modify it
- `/spec-status` does not modify any files (read-only command)
- `/spec-init` creates `roadmap.md` with inferred feature backlog
- `/spec-specify` checks matching roadmap items + adds deferred splits to `roadmap.md`
- `/spec-propose` reads `roadmap.md` including Deferred section (read-only)
- `/spec-refine project` re-evaluates roadmap after project profile changes + supports direct roadmap refinement
- `/spec-specify` detects emerging dependencies and roadmap item absorption
- Every update also refreshes the `Last updated` date in the header

**Section markers:** Updatable sections use `<!-- readme:features:start/end -->`, `<!-- readme:decisions:start/end -->`, `<!-- readme:activity:start/end -->` HTML comments. Do not remove these markers.

**Recovery:** If README.md is missing, any updating command rebuilds it by scanning existing `.specs/features/*/spec.md`, `.specs/stacks/decisions/ADR-*.md`, and `.specs/changelog.md`.

", "start_line": 224, "end_line": 250, "start_byte": 9190, "end_byte": 10866}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L251-L270", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## Lifecycle Hooks

LiveSpec supports **lifecycle hooks** — Markdown files with instructions injected before/after each command. Hooks enable customizing LiveSpec behavior without modifying core commands.

**Full protocol:** Read [`system/hooks.md`](../system/hooks.md) for the complete resolution protocol, naming conventions, and inheritance model.

**Quick reference:**
- 4 resolution levels: user integrations (`~/.config/livespec/*.md`) → global (`~/.claude/livespec/hooks/`) → project (`.specs/hooks/`) → local (`.specs/hooks/*.local.md`)
- Naming: `{before|after}-{command}.md` and `{before|after}-{command}.local.md` (Levels 1–3); user integrations target commands via frontmatter, not filename
- Inheritance: `mode: extend` (default, accumulate) or `mode: override` (replace chain at the level that declares it)
- Step-level hooks: `before-implement-step.md` / `after-implement-step.md`
- Discovery: `/spec-hooks [command]` to see active hooks; use `--create`/`--edit` to manage hooks

**User-level integrations.** Markdown files in `~/.config/livespec/` may
inject instructions into selected commands (Level 0 of hook resolution).
See [`integrations.md`](../system/integrations.md) for the full schema,
runtime CLI (`livespec hooks resolve`), and chained-pipeline semantics.

---

", "start_line": 251, "end_line": 270, "start_byte": 10866, "end_byte": 12167}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L271-L272", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## Rules for AI Tools

", "start_line": 271, "end_line": 272, "start_byte": 12167, "end_byte": 12190}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L273-L279", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### MANDATORY — Hooks Resolution Protocol

**You MUST resolve hooks before and after EVERY `/spec-*` command execution.** This is not optional. Failure to resolve hooks means conventions are not loaded and the command runs without context.

**Before starting any command:** resolve `before-{command}` hooks.
**After completing any command:** resolve `after-{command}` hooks.

", "start_line": 273, "end_line": 279, "start_byte": 12190, "end_byte": 12568}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L280-L293", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "#### Resolution algorithm (for each hook event)

For a given event (e.g., `before-plan`), Read files at 3 levels in order:

| Level | Path | Scope |
|-------|------|-------|
| 1. Global | `~/.claude/livespec/hooks/before-plan.md` | All LiveSpec projects |
| 2. Project | `.specs/hooks/before-plan.md` | This project (committed, team-shared) |
| 3. Local | `.specs/hooks/before-plan.local.md` | Personal (gitignored) |

- If a file does not exist at a level → skip that level silently.
- If the **local** hook has `mode: override` in its YAML frontmatter → execute **only** the local hook, skip global and project.
- Otherwise (`mode: extend`, the default) → execute **all** existing hooks in order: global → project → local.

", "start_line": 280, "end_line": 293, "start_byte": 12568, "end_byte": 13304}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L294-L318", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "#### Exhaustive hook table — all commands

| Command | Before hooks to resolve | After hooks to resolve |
|---------|------------------------|----------------------|
| `init` | `before-init` (global, project, local) | `after-init` (global, project, local) |
| `propose` | `before-propose` (global, project, local) | `after-propose` (global, project, local) |
| `specify` | `before-specify` (global, project, local) | `after-specify` (global, project, local) |
| `plan` | `before-plan` (global, project, local) | `after-plan` (global, project, local) |
| `implement` | `before-implement` (global, project, local) | `after-implement` (global, project, local) |
| `implement` (each step) | `before-implement-step` (global, project, local) | `after-implement-step` (global, project, local) |
| `check` | `before-check` (global, project, local) | `after-check` (global, project, local) |
| `test` | `before-test` (global, project, local) | `after-test` (global, project, local) |
| `explain` | `before-explain` (global, project, local) | `after-explain` (global, project, local) |
| `stack` | `before-stack` (global, project, local) | `after-stack` (global, project, local) |
| `feature` | `before-feature` (global, project, local) | `after-feature` (global, project, local) |
| `refine` | `before-refine` (global, project, local) | `after-refine` (global, project, local) |
| `preflight` | `before-preflight` (global, project, local) | `after-preflight` (global, project, local) |
| `fix` | `before-fix` (global, project, local) | `after-fix` (global, project, local) |

**No hooks:** `hooks`, `play-coverage`, `status`, `refresh-conventions` — these are diagnostic/utility commands.

**`feature` sub-commands:** `/spec-feature` wraps a pipeline (specify → clarify → plan → analyze → implement). Resolve `before-feature`/`after-feature` around the full pipeline AND resolve each sub-command's own hooks (before-specify, before-plan, before-implement, etc.) at each phase.

**`implement` step hooks:** In addition to `before-implement`/`after-implement` (once), resolve `before-implement-step`/`after-implement-step` before and after EACH implementation step.

", "start_line": 294, "end_line": 318, "start_byte": 13304, "end_byte": 15472}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L319-L332", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Version Check (ADVISORY)

", "start_line": 354, "end_line": 361, "start_byte": 17270, "end_byte": 17546}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L362-L378", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Changelog Rotation

|---|---|
| New feature request | `/spec-specify` |

| Audit / spec-code alignment | `/spec-check` |

| What should I build next? / Propose next feature | `/spec-propose` |
| Full feature pipeline (specify → clarify → plan → analyze → implement) | `/spec-feature` |
| Refine or update project-level artifacts | `/spec-refine project` |
| Refine or update an existing feature spec | `/spec-refine [feature]` |

Every `/spec-*` command must follow these execution rules:

1. **Intent check first**
   Confirm the command matches user intent; if not, propose the correct `/spec-*` command (see Intent Classification above).

2. **Ambiguity cap**
   Ask at most 2 clarifying questions. If ambiguity remains, proceed with explicit `[ASSUMED]` markers.

3. **Prerequisite gate**
   Validate required files before writing. If missing, stop and provide the minimal recovery command.

4. **Evidence-based reporting**
   Do not mark items as complete without file/test evidence.

5. **Definition of done**
   End each command with:
   - artifacts created/updated
   - unresolved blockers (if any)
   - next recommended command

- `Resume With:` exact `/spec-*` command or flag

Descriptor inventory covers every AppSettings field, with wire type, enum/range, mutable/read-only, secret/presence projection, owning domain, runtime effect and validator. Build a reviewed manifest plus an independent test inventory from serialized default settings and all UI adapters; a descriptor omission fails, not silently hides a setting. Existing scalar settings are generic-settable except internal fields (schema, revision, onboarding/migration markers, manager-only model state) and provider configuration, which remain read-only from CLI. API-key fields are secret and never generic-settable. Lists/maps return validation_failed naming their owning domain command, plus `not available in this build` when unregistered; include owning command even when unavailable to satisfy AC-002. Optional values have descriptor-defined null handling; non-null boolean accepts exactly true/false, numeric parses without overflow, enums use existing serde values, strings preserve bytes without trimming meaningful content.

Redact via explicit public projection, never AppSettings Serialize or Debug. `post_process_api_keys` becomes per-provider `{present:boolean}` only; nested/future secrets inherit the rule. All stdout, stderr, parse errors, IPC diagnostics and logs sanitize raw candidate values. Public errors use stable English text and object details, with field/issues where applicable; no OS trace, raw document or credential in details. Reject `paste_method=invalid_method` identically via UI and CLI rather than existing default-to-ctrl_v behavior. UI maps code+field to i18n keys, falling back to a translated generic error, not free-text parsing.

`output get [KEY]` and `output set KEY VALUE` delegate to the same descriptors for existing paste_method, clipboard_handling, auto_submit, auto_submit_key, paste_delay_ms, paste_delay_after_ms, reliable_paste, typing_tool, external_script_path and append_trailing_space. Existing enum values remain unchanged: ctrl_v/direct/none/shift_insert/ctrl_shift_v/external_script; dont_modify/copy_to_clipboard; enter/ctrl_enter/cmd_enter. When 007 ships, it extends the same output descriptor and validation path with paste_method=smart_paste on macOS (validation_failed outside macOS), using the existing commit_mutation service and Domain trait; 008 alone keeps the existing methods. Feature 007 owns the macOS migration/default and removal of the beta reliable_paste switch; the Windows reliable_paste switch/path and Linux methods stay unchanged. This is configuration, not insertion execution. Keep destination 006/009, insertion method and clipboard handling separate. The 007 outcome contract is: "insertion attempted, read observed", "not read", "permission missing", "typed", "clipboard handed over", "insertion failed". Only read observed and typed authorize automatic Enter in 009; not read, permission missing and insertion failed route to recovery in 010. Clipboard handed over is neither Enter nor verified insertion. Outcomes wait for the read/fallback decision and never claim text verified in a field. A committed output setting proves configuration only.

Domain trait registers command schema/help, file/`-` input, pure parsing/validation, preview, typed patch and export formatter. Valid dry-run loads latest revision, validates fully, emits preview/revision with exit 0, and does not persist or call effects. Invalid dry-run returns validation_failed/2 with issues, no success preview. `-` explicitly requests stdin, never prompts; non-UTF-8 text returns byte offset in details. Export `-` human mode is raw exchange content only; JSON is data.content. Fixture domain proves bulk merge/replace/atomic all-or-nothing and live-only unavailable behavior; it never appears in production help.

| Result | Exit |
|---|---|
| success | 0 |
| persistence_failed, internal_error | 1 |
| usage_error, validation_failed, shortcut_conflict, limit_exceeded | 2 |
| revision_conflict (`details.current_revision`) | 3 |
| not_found | 4 |
| unavailable (timeout: `details.outcome=unknown`) | 5 |

The enum+single renderer owns this mapping. Every JSON operation emits exactly one `{ok:true,revision:N,data:...}` or `{ok:false,error:{code,message,details:{...}}}` followed by newline; diagnostics go to stderr. No newly introduced HTTP endpoints: OpenAPI would misrepresent local IPC. Contract is the typed DTO/JSON-schema and command matrix in Step 2; no openapi.yaml generated.

", "start_line": 22, "end_line": 31, "start_byte": 456, "end_byte": 924}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/009-pin-mode-and-enter-rule/spec.md:L137-L180", "source": ".specs/features/009-pin-mode-and-enter-rule/spec.md", "role": "reference", "text": "### Story 4 — Enter only after a successful insertion `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** never have Enter pressed when my text did not land, **so that** an empty or wrong message is never sent.

**Priority reason:** An Enter after a failed insertion can send an empty message or trigger an unintended action.
**Independent test:** Inject activation failure, insertion failure and recovery display, with automatic Enter "Always".

```gherkin
Feature: Enter after a successful insertion only
  Scenario: Destination unavailable
    Given automatic Enter is "Always"
    When the destination is unavailable at insertion time
    Then no Enter key press is sent
  Scenario: Insertion method failed
    Given automatic Enter is "Always"
    When the insertion method reports failure
    Then no Enter key press is sent
  Scenario: Paste method none
    Given the paste method is "none"
    When a dictation completes
    Then no Enter key press is sent
  Scenario: Smart paste without observed read
    Given the paste method is smart paste
    When the target never reads the clipboard and the outcome is "not read"
    Then no Enter key press is sent
  Scenario: Destination left before Enter
    Given automatic Enter is "Always" and the text was inserted into ChatGPT
    When another application becomes frontmost before the Enter press
    Then no Enter key press is sent
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Insertion step] --> B{Destination frontmost?}
  B -- No --> X[No Enter]
  B -- Yes --> C{Method reported success?}
  C -- No --> X
  C -- Yes --> D{Smart paste read observed, or Windows reliable paste read confirmed, if used?}
  D -- No --> X
  D -- Yes --> E{Recovery shown instead of insertion?}
  E -- Yes --> X
  E -- No --> F[Apply Enter option]
```

    Given a dictation started in Notes
    When Notes quits before the dictation ends
    Then nothing is inserted
    And a bubble appears in place of the live indicator with the beginning of the transcript
    And the bubble states "Notes is no longer open"
  Scenario: Activation not confirmed
    Given the destination did not become frontmost within the 006 limit
    When insertion is due
    Then the bubble appears with the reason "Could not bring the app forward"
  Scenario: No automatic Enter
    Given automatic Enter is "Always"
    When the bubble is shown instead of an insertion
    Then no Enter key press is sent
```

", "start_line": 6, "end_line": 12, "start_byte": 87, "end_byte": 278}, {"section_id": ".specs/spec-system.md:L13-L36", "source": ".specs/spec-system.md", "role": "reference", "text": "## Core Principles

1. **The spec is the functional source of truth, not the code.**
   If the spec says one thing and the code does another, the code is wrong (unless the spec was intentionally updated).

2. **Every feature has a spec — no implementation without a spec.**
   Before writing a single line of code, the corresponding `.specs/features/NNN-feature-name/spec.md` must exist.

3. **Specs are living — updated when behavior changes.**
   When a feature's behavior is modified, the spec.md is updated first (or simultaneously). Specs never become stale.

4. **Specs are visual and testable — Gherkin scenarios and Mermaid flows are mandatory.**
   Every user story in a spec.md must include Gherkin scenarios (source of truth for AI and test scaffolding) and a Mermaid flowchart (visual representation of the same flow). Text-only specs are incomplete.

5. **Code is linked to specs — every implementation is traceable.**
   After implementation, `implementation.md` maps every FR and AC to the `@spec` anchor comment placed directly in the source code. Anchor comments include a **brief description** and the **relative path to the spec file with a fragment anchor** for deep-linking:
   ```
   // @spec FR-001: Brief description — .specs/features/NNN-feature-name/spec.md#fr-001
   ```
   - The description (after `:`) is a short summary (<50 chars) of the FR/AC
   - The fragment `#fr-001` enables deep-linking within the Markdown ecosystem (GitHub, preview, `implementation.md` → `spec.md`)
   - `grep -rn "@spec FR-001"` continues to work regardless of line number changes
   - Multi-requirements: list each `ID: description` separated by commas (e.g. `// @spec FR-001: Fetch count, FR-003: Mark as read — spec.md#fr-001`)
